title: Hope in a Broken World
intro: This is a series of discovery Bible sessions designed for people who are not believers, but who are open to reading the Bible and exploring Jesus. There are 3 sets of sessions, so choose the set that best fits the “starting point” of the person you are reading with.

lessons.title: Hope Does Not Judge
lessons.question: How does Jesus treat people others have written off?
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus? Does your view of Him change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?
lessons.note: The religious leaders used this woman as a trap. They dragged her out in public and demanded she be stoned. Jesus didn't deny her sin, but He turned the question back on everyone holding a stone, and one by one they walked away. He was the only one without sin, the only one with the right to condemn her, and He chose not to. Then He gave her a new start: go and sin no more.
lessons.reflect: Who have you been quick to judge? And where do you need to hear Jesus say "neither do I condemn thee"?
lessons.declare: Jesus does not condemn me. He gives me a new start.

vs.t: And the scribes and Pharisees brought unto him a woman taken in adultery; and when they had set her in the midst,
vs.e: Now the scribes and Pharisees came, with a woman who had been taken in the act of sinning against the married relation;
vs.w: The scribes and the Pharisees brought a woman taken in adultery. Having set her in the middle,

vs.t: They say unto him, Master, this woman was taken in adultery, in the very act.
vs.e: And putting her forward, they said to him, Master, this woman has been taken in the very act of sinning against the married relation.
vs.w: they told him, “Teacher, we found this woman in adultery, in the very act.

vs.t: Now Moses in the law commanded us, that such should be stoned: but what sayest thou?
vs.e: Now in the law Moses gave directions that such women were to be stoned; what do you say about it?
vs.w: Now in our law, Moses commanded us to stone such women. What then do you say about her?”

vs.t: This they said, tempting him, that they might have to accuse him. But Jesus stooped down, and with his finger wrote on the ground, as though he heard them not.
vs.e: They said this, testing him, so that they might have something against him. But Jesus, with his head bent down, made letters on the floor with his finger.
vs.w: They said this testing him, that they might have something to accuse him of. But Jesus stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.

vs.t: So when they continued asking him, he lifted up himself, and said unto them, He that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone at her.
vs.e: But when they went on with their questions, he got up and said to them, Let him among you who is without sin be the first to send a stone at her.
vs.w: But when they continued asking him, he looked up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw the first stone at her.”

vs.t: And again he stooped down, and wrote on the ground.
vs.e: And again, with bent head, he made letters on the floor.
vs.w: Again he stooped down and wrote on the ground with his finger.

vs.t: And they which heard it, being convicted by their own conscience, went out one by one, beginning at the eldest, even unto the last: and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst.
vs.e: And when his words came to their ears, they went out one by one, starting with the oldest even to the last, because they were conscious of what was in their hearts: and Jesus was there by himself with the woman before him.
vs.w: They, when they heard it, being convicted by their conscience, went out one by one, beginning from the oldest, even to the last. Jesus was left alone with the woman where she was, in the middle.

vs.t: When Jesus had lifted up himself, and saw none but the woman, he said unto her, Woman, where are those thine accusers? hath no man condemned thee?
vs.e: Then Jesus got up, and seeing nobody but the woman, he said to her, Where are the men who said things against you? did no one give a decision against you?
vs.w: Jesus, standing up, saw her and said, “Woman, where are your accusers? Did no one condemn you?”

vs.t: She said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said unto her, Neither do I condemn thee: go, and sin no more.
vs.e: And she said, No man, Lord. And Jesus said, And I do not give a decision against you: go, and never do wrong again.
vs.w: She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus said, “Neither do I condemn you. Go your way. From now on, sin no more.”

vs.t: Judge not, that ye be not judged.
vs.e: Be not judges of others, and you will not be judged.
vs.w: “Don’t judge, so that you won’t be judged.

vs.t: For with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged: and with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you again.
vs.e: For as you have been judging, so you will be judged, and with your measure will it be measured to you.
vs.w: For with whatever judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you.

vs.t: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but considerest not the beam that is in thine own eye?
vs.e: And why do you take note of the grain of dust in your brother's eye, but take no note of the bit of wood which is in your eye?
vs.w: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye?

vs.t: Or how wilt thou say to thy brother, Let me pull out the mote out of thine eye; and, behold, a beam is in thine own eye?
vs.e: Or how will you say to your brother, Let me take out the grain of dust from your eye, when you yourself have a bit of wood in your eye?
vs.w: Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye;’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye?

vs.t: Thou hypocrite, first cast out the beam out of thine own eye; and then shalt thou see clearly to cast out the mote out of thy brother’s eye.
vs.e: You false one, first take out the bit of wood from your eye, then will you see clearly to take out the grain of dust from your brother's eye.
vs.w: You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.

lessons.title: Hope for the Hopeless Sinner
lessons.sub: The Pharisee and the tax collector
lessons.question: Who does God accept: the proud or the humble?
ask: Is there anything that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?
lessons.note: The Pharisee measured himself against other people and looked good. The tax collector measured himself against God, and all he could say was "God be merciful to me a sinner." Jesus said it was the tax collector who went home right with God. Then Jesus welcomed little children: the kingdom belongs to those who come with empty hands and simple trust.
lessons.reflect: Do you tend to measure yourself against other people, or against God?
lessons.declare: God, be merciful to me. I come to You humbly, like a child.

vs.t: And he spake this parable unto certain which trusted in themselves that they were righteous, and despised others:
vs.e: And he made this story for some people who were certain that they were good, and had a low opinion of others:
vs.w: He spoke also this parable to certain people who were convinced of their own righteousness, and who despised all others.

vs.t: Two men went up into the temple to pray; the one a Pharisee, and the other a publican.
vs.e: Two men went up to the Temple for prayer; one a Pharisee, and the other a tax-farmer.
vs.w: “Two men went up into the temple to pray; one was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.

vs.t: The Pharisee stood and prayed thus with himself, God, I thank thee, that I am not as other men are, extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even as this publican.
vs.e: The Pharisee, taking up his position, said to himself these words: God, I give you praise because I am not like other men, who take more than their right, who are evil-doers, who are untrue to their wives, or even like this tax-farmer.
vs.w: The Pharisee stood and prayed to himself like this: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of men, extortionists, unrighteous, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.

vs.t: I fast twice in the week, I give tithes of all that I possess.
vs.e: Twice in the week I go without food; I give a tenth of all I have.
vs.w: I fast twice a week. I give tithes of all that I get.’

vs.t: And the publican, standing afar off, would not lift up so much as his eyes unto heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying, God be merciful to me a sinner.
vs.e: The tax-farmer, on the other hand, keeping far away, and not lifting up even his eyes to heaven, made signs of grief and said, God, have mercy on me, a sinner.
vs.w: But the tax collector, standing far away, wouldn’t even lift up his eyes to heaven, but beat his breast, saying, ‘God, be merciful to me, a sinner!’

vs.t: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other: for every one that exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.
vs.e: I say to you, This man went back to his house with God's approval, and not the other: for everyone who makes himself high will be made low and whoever makes himself low will be made high.
vs.w: I tell you, this man went down to his house justified rather than the other; for everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but he who humbles himself will be exalted.”

vs.t: And they brought unto him also infants, that he would touch them: but when his disciples saw it, they rebuked them.
vs.e: And they took their children to him, so that he might put his hands on them: but when the disciples saw it, they said sharp words to them
vs.w: They were also bringing their babies to him, that he might touch them. But when the disciples saw it, they rebuked them.

vs.t: But Jesus called them unto him, and said, Suffer little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.
vs.e: But Jesus sent for them, saying, Let the children come to me, and do not keep them away, for of such is the kingdom of heaven.
vs.w: Jesus summoned them, saying, “Allow the little children to come to me, and don’t hinder them, for God’s Kingdom belongs to such as these.

vs.t: Verily I say unto you, Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter therein.
vs.e: Truly I say to you, Whoever does not put himself under the kingdom of God like a little child, will not come into it at all.
vs.w: Most certainly, I tell you, whoever doesn’t receive God’s Kingdom like a little child, he will in no way enter into it.”

lessons.title: Hope Changes Things
lessons.sub: Jesus and the man everyone hated
lessons.question: What happens when Jesus comes to your house?
ask: What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus? Does your view of Him change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?
How do lives change in this story?
lessons.note: Zacchaeus was rich, but hated and alone. Jesus stopped under his tree, called him by name and invited Himself home. Something about Jesus completely changed him: he gave to the poor and paid back four times what he had stolen. He no longer had to hide his sin and guilt. Jesus came to seek and to save the lost.
lessons.reflect: What would change in your life if Jesus came to your house today?
lessons.declare: Jesus came to seek and to save the lost, and He is seeking me.

vs.t: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
vs.e: And he went into Jericho, and when he was going through it,
vs.w: He entered and was passing through Jericho.

vs.t: And, behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
vs.e: A man, named Zacchaeus, who was the chief tax-farmer, and a man of wealth,
vs.w: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

vs.t: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
vs.e: Made an attempt to get a view of Jesus, and was not able to do so, because of the people, for he was a small man.
vs.w: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.

vs.t: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
vs.e: And he went quickly in front of them and got up into a tree to see him, for he was going that way.
vs.w: He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.

vs.t: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
vs.e: And when Jesus came to the place, looking up, he said to him, Zacchaeus, be quick and come down, for I am coming to your house today.
vs.w: When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”

vs.t: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
vs.e: And he came down quickly, and took him into his house with joy.
vs.w: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.

vs.t: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
vs.e: And when they saw it, they were all angry, saying, He has gone into the house of a sinner.
vs.w: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”

vs.t: And Zaccheus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
vs.e: And Zacchaeus, waiting before him, said to the Lord, See, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone wrongly, I give him back four times as much.
vs.w: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”

vs.t: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
vs.e: And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, for even he is a son of Abraham.
vs.w: Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.

vs.t: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
vs.e: For the Son of man came to make search for those who are wandering from the way, and to be their Saviour.
vs.w: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

vs.t: No man, when he hath lighted a candle, covereth it with a vessel, or putteth it under a bed; but setteth it on a candlestick, that they which enter in may see the light.
vs.e: No man, when the light is lighted, puts a cover over it, or puts it under a bed, but he puts it on its table, so that those who come in may see the light.
vs.w: “No one, when he has lit a lamp, covers it with a container, or puts it under a bed; but puts it on a stand, that those who enter in may see the light.

vs.t: For nothing is secret, that shall not be made manifest; neither any thing hid, that shall not be known and come abroad.
vs.e: For nothing is put out of view which will not be made clear, and nothing is secret of which the knowledge will not come to light.
vs.w: For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed; nor anything secret that will not be known and come to light.

lessons.memtext: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
lessons.memE: For the Son of man came to make search for those who are wandering from the way, and to be their Saviour.
lessons.memW: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

lessons.title: Jesus Offers Hope to Everyone
lessons.question: Is anyone too far away for Jesus?
ask: What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus? Does your view of Him change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?
How do lives change in this story?
lessons.note: Jews and Samaritans did not mix, men did not talk to women alone, and this woman came to the well at midday to avoid people. Jesus crossed every barrier, knew all about her past, and still offered her living water. She ran back to the town that avoided her, and many believed. The good news is for every nation, every background, everyone.
lessons.reflect: Who do you think is too far from God? What does this story say to that?
lessons.declare: Jesus is the Saviour of the world. His hope is for everyone, including me.

vs.t: And he must needs go through Samaria.
vs.e: And it was necessary for him to go through Samaria.
vs.w: He needed to pass through Samaria.

vs.t: Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
vs.e: So he came to a town of Samaria which was named Sychar, near to the bit of land which Jacob gave to his son Joseph:
vs.w: So he came to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son, Joseph.

vs.t: Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.
vs.e: Now Jacob's fountain was there. Jesus, being tired after his journey, was resting by the fountain. It was about the sixth hour.
vs.w: Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

vs.t: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
vs.e: A woman of Samaria came to get water, and Jesus said to her, Give me some water.
vs.w: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”

vs.t: (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat.)
vs.e: For his disciples had gone to the town to get food.
vs.w: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.

vs.t: Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
vs.e: The woman of Samaria said to him, Why do you, a Jew, make a request for water to me, a woman of Samaria? She said this because Jews have nothing to do with the people of Samaria.
vs.w: The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)

vs.t: Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
vs.e: In answer Jesus said, If you had knowledge of what God gives freely and who it is who says to you, Give me water, you would make your prayer to him, and he would give you living water.
vs.w: Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

vs.t: The woman saith unto him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep: from whence then hast thou that living water?
vs.e: The woman said to him, Sir, you have no vessel and the fountain is deep; from where will you get the living water?
vs.w: The woman said to him, “Sir, you have nothing to draw with, and the well is deep. So where do you get that living water?

vs.t: Art thou greater than our father Jacob, which gave us the well, and drank thereof himself, and his children, and his cattle?
vs.e: Are you greater than our father Jacob who gave us the fountain and took the water of it himself, with his children and his cattle?
vs.w: Are you greater than our father, Jacob, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, as did his children and his livestock?”

vs.t: Jesus answered and said unto her, Whosoever drinketh of this water shall thirst again:
vs.e: Jesus said to her, Everyone who takes this water will be in need of it again:
vs.w: Jesus answered her, “Everyone who drinks of this water will thirst again,

vs.t: But whosoever drinketh of the water that I shall give him shall never thirst; but the water that I shall give him shall be in him a well of water springing up into everlasting life.
vs.e: But whoever takes the water I give him will never be in need of drink again; for the water I give him will become in him a fountain of eternal life.
vs.w: but whoever drinks of the water that I will give him will never thirst again; but the water that I will give him will become in him a well of water springing up to eternal life.”

vs.t: The woman saith unto him, Sir, give me this water, that I thirst not, neither come hither to draw.
vs.e: The woman said to him, Sir, give me this water, so that I may not be in need again of drink and will not have to come all this way for it.
vs.w: The woman said to him, “Sir, give me this water, so that I don’t get thirsty, neither come all the way here to draw.”

vs.t: Jesus saith unto her, Go, call thy husband, and come hither.
vs.e: Jesus said to her, Go, get your husband and come back here with him.
vs.w: Jesus said to her, “Go, call your husband, and come here.”

vs.t: The woman answered and said, I have no husband. Jesus said unto her, Thou hast well said, I have no husband:
vs.e: In answer, the woman said, I have no husband. Jesus said to her, You have said rightly, I have no husband:
vs.w: The woman answered, “I have no husband.” Jesus said to her, “You said well, ‘I have no husband,’

vs.t: For thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast is not thy husband: in that saidst thou truly.
vs.e: You have had five husbands, and the man you have now is not your husband: that was truly said.
vs.w: for you have had five husbands; and he whom you now have is not your husband. This you have said truly.”

vs.t: The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.
vs.e: The woman said to him, I am certain that the Messiah, who is named Christ, is coming; when he comes he will make all things clear to us.
vs.w: The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah comes, he who is called Christ. When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”

vs.t: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.
vs.e: Jesus said to her, I, who am talking to you, am he.
vs.w: Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one who speaks to you.”

vs.t: And upon this came his disciples, and marvelled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why talkest thou with her?
vs.e: At that point the disciples came back, and they were surprised to see him talking to a woman; but not one of them said to him, What is your purpose? or, Why are you talking to her?
vs.w: At this, his disciples came. They marveled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?”

vs.t: The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men,
vs.e: Then the woman put down her water-pot and went into the town, and said to the people,
vs.w: So the woman left her water pot, went away into the city, and said to the people,

vs.t: Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?
vs.e: Come and see a man who has been talking to me of everything I ever did! Is it possible that this is the Christ?
vs.w: “Come, see a man who told me everything that I did. Can this be the Christ?”

vs.t: Then they went out of the city, and came unto him.
vs.e: So they went out of the town and came to him.
vs.w: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

vs.t: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did.
vs.e: Now a number of the people of that town had faith in him because of the woman's witness: He has been talking to me of everything I ever did.
vs.w: From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I did.”

vs.t: So when the Samaritans were come unto him, they besought him that he would tarry with them: and he abode there two days.
vs.e: So when the people came to him they made request to him to be among them for a time, and he was there two days.
vs.w: So when the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay with them. He stayed there two days.

vs.t: And many more believed because of his own word;
vs.e: And a great number more of them came to have faith in him because of what he himself said.
vs.w: Many more believed because of his word.

vs.t: And said unto the woman, Now we believe, not because of thy saying: for we have heard him ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Saviour of the world.
vs.e: And they said to the woman, Now we have faith, but not because of your story: we ourselves have given ear to his words, and we are certain that he is truly the Saviour of the world.
vs.w: They said to the woman, “Now we believe, not because of your speaking; for we have heard for ourselves, and know that this is indeed the Christ, the Savior of the world.”

vs.t: Now after two days he departed thence, and went into Galilee.
vs.e: And after the two days he went on from there into Galilee.
vs.w: After the two days he went out from there and went into Galilee.

vs.t: For so hath the Lord commanded us, saying, I have set thee to be a light of the Gentiles, that thou shouldest be for salvation unto the ends of the earth.
vs.e: For so the Lord has given us orders, saying, I have given you for a light to the Gentiles so that you may be for salvation to the ends of the earth.
vs.w: For so has the Lord commanded us, saying, ‘I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should bring salvation to the uttermost parts of the earth.’ ”

vs.t: And when the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of the Lord: and as many as were ordained to eternal life believed.
vs.e: And the Gentiles, hearing this, were glad and gave glory to the word of God: and those marked out by God for eternal life had faith.
vs.w: As the Gentiles heard this, they were glad, and glorified the word of God. As many as were appointed to eternal life believed.

vs.t: And the word of the Lord was published throughout all the region.
vs.e: And the word of the Lord went through all the country.
vs.w: The Lord’s word was spread abroad throughout all the region.

lessons.title: Hope in God's Mercy
lessons.question: How much has God forgiven us, and how should we forgive?
ask: Is there anything that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about God? Does your view of God change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?
lessons.note: The servant owed a debt he could never repay in many lifetimes, and the king forgave it all, moved with compassion. Then that same servant grabbed someone who owed him a tiny amount. Jesus is showing us how big our debt to God is and how great His mercy is. Those who have been forgiven much are called to forgive.
lessons.reflect: Is there someone you need to forgive, the way God has forgiven you?
lessons.declare: God has forgiven me a debt I could never pay. I choose to forgive others.

vs.t: Then came Peter to him, and said, Lord, how oft shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? till seven times?

vs.w: Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Until seven times?”

lessons.title: Hope Is Waiting for You
lessons.sub: The lost son and the running father
lessons.question: What is God like when we come home?
ask: What do you learn about people in this story?
Who does the father represent? Who do the two sons represent?
What do you learn about God? Does your view of Him change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?
lessons.note: The younger son wasted everything and came home planning to beg for a servant's job. But while he was still a great way off, the father saw him, was moved with compassion, ran, and kissed him. The older son, who never left, was angry and stayed outside. The Father is waiting for both kinds of people: those who ran away and those who never really came close.
lessons.reflect: Are you more like the younger son or the older son right now? What is the Father saying to you?
lessons.declare: My Father is running to meet me. Hope is waiting for me at home.

vs.t: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
vs.e: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
vs.w: He said, “A certain man had two sons.

vs.t: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
vs.e: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me that part of your property which will be mine. And he made division of his goods between them.
vs.w: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ He divided his livelihood between them.

vs.t: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
vs.e: And not long after, the younger son got together everything which was his and took a journey into a far-away country, and there all his money went in foolish living.
vs.w: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.

vs.t: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.

vs.w: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

vs.t: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
vs.e: And so great was his need that he would have been glad to take the pigs' food, and no one gave him anything.
vs.w: He wanted to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.

vs.t: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!

vs.w: But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!

vs.t: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,

vs.w: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.

vs.t: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
vs.e: I am no longer good enough to be named your son: make me like one of your servants.
vs.w: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.” ’

vs.t: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
vs.e: And he got up and went to his father. But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with pity for him and went quickly and took him in his arms and gave him a kiss.
vs.w: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

vs.w: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and sandals on his feet.

vs.t: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:

vs.w: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’

vs.t: And he was angry, and would not go in: therefore came his father out, and intreated him.

vs.w: But he was angry, and would not go in. Therefore his father came out, and begged him.

vs.t: And he answering said to his father, Lo, these many years do I serve thee, neither transgressed I at any time thy commandment: and yet thou never gavest me a kid, that I might make merry with my friends:

vs.w: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.

vs.t: But as soon as this thy son was come, which hath devoured thy living with harlots, thou hast killed for him the fatted calf.
vs.e: But when this your son came, who has been wasting your property with bad women, you put to death the fat young ox for him.

vs.t: And he said unto him, Son, thou art ever with me, and all that I have is thine.

vs.w: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.

vs.t: It was meet that we should make merry, and be glad: for this thy brother was dead, and is alive again; and was lost, and is found.

lessons.title: Power over the Storm
lessons.question: Who is Jesus, that even the wind and sea obey Him?
lessons.note: Experienced fishermen were terrified as the boat filled with water, while Jesus slept. They woke Him with an accusation: "carest thou not that we perish?" He spoke three words to the wind and sea, and there was a great calm. Their fear of the storm turned into a bigger question: who is this?
lessons.reflect: What storm are you facing right now? What would it mean to bring it to Jesus?
lessons.declare: Jesus has power over every storm in my life.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.w: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.

vs.e: And a great storm of wind came up, and the waves came into the boat, so that the boat was now becoming full.

vs.w: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and they woke him up, and told him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”

vs.t: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
vs.e: And he came out of his sleep, and gave strong orders to the wind, and said to the sea, Peace, be at rest. And the wind went down, and there was a great calm.
vs.w: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

vs.t: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
vs.e: And he said to them, Why are you full of fear? have you still no faith?
vs.w: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”

vs.t: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
vs.e: And their fear was great, and they said one to another, Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea do his orders?
vs.w: They were greatly afraid, and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”

lessons.title: Power to Forgive
lessons.sub: The man let down through the roof
lessons.question: What is our deepest need?
lessons.note: Four friends dug through a roof to bring a paralysed man to Jesus. Everyone expected a healing, but Jesus first said, "Son, thy sins be forgiven thee." The religious leaders were right that only God can forgive sins. Jesus then healed the man to prove He has that authority. Our deepest need is not just a better body or better circumstances, but forgiveness.
lessons.reflect: Who brought you to Jesus, or who could you carry to Him like those four friends?
lessons.declare: Jesus has authority on earth to forgive my sins.

lessons.title: Power over Evil
lessons.sub: The man no chains could hold
lessons.question: Is anyone too far gone for Jesus?
lessons.note: This man lived among the tombs, crying and cutting himself, and no chain could hold him. Everyone had given up on him. Jesus crossed the lake to meet him and set him free with a word. Afterwards he sat clothed and in his right mind, and Jesus sent him home to tell his family what great things the Lord had done.
lessons.reflect: What chains do people around you live under? What hope does this story give?
lessons.declare: Jesus sets the captive free. No one is too far gone for Him.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?

vs.w: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,

vs.t: Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
vs.e: Because he had frequently been prisoned in chains and iron bands, and the chains had been parted and the bands broken by him: and no man was strong enough to make him quiet.
vs.w: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.

vs.t: And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.
vs.e: And all the time, by day and by night, in the place of the dead, and in the mountains, he was crying out and cutting himself with stones.
vs.w: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.

vs.t: But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,
vs.e: And when he saw Jesus from far off, he went quickly to him and gave him worship;
vs.w: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,

vs.t: And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.
vs.e: And crying out with a loud voice he said, What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? In God's name, do not be cruel to me.
vs.w: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”

vs.t: For he said unto him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.
vs.e: For Jesus had said to him, Come out of the man, you unclean spirit.
vs.w: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”

vs.t: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
vs.e: And Jesus said, What is your name? And he made answer, My name is Legion, because there are a great number of us.
vs.w: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”

vs.t: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
vs.e: And he made strong prayers to him not to send them away out of the country.
vs.w: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

vs.t: Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.
vs.e: Now on the mountain side there was a great herd of pigs getting their food.
vs.w: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.

vs.t: And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.
vs.e: And they said to him, Send us into the pigs, so that we may go into them.
vs.w: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”

vs.t: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.
vs.e: And he let them do it. And the unclean spirits came out and went into the pigs; and the herd went rushing down a sharp slope into the sea, about two thousand of them; and they came to their death in the sea.
vs.w: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.

vs.t: And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.
vs.e: And their keepers went running and gave an account of it in the town and in the country. And people came to see what had taken place.
vs.w: Those who fed them fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.

vs.t: And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
vs.e: And they came to Jesus, and saw the man in whom had been the evil spirits seated, clothed and with full use of his senses, and they were full of fear.
vs.w: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.

vs.t: And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine.
vs.e: And those who had seen it gave them an account of what had been done to him who had the evil spirits, and of the fate of the pigs.
vs.w: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.

vs.t: And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.
vs.e: And they made a request to him to go out of their country.
vs.w: They began to beg him to depart from their region.

vs.t: And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.
vs.e: And when he was getting into the boat, the man in whom had been the evil spirits had a great desire to come with him.
vs.w: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.

vs.t: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
vs.e: And he would not let him, but said to him, Go to your house, to your friends, and give them news of the great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.
vs.w: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”

vs.t: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.
vs.e: And he went on his way, and made public in the country of Decapolis what great things Jesus had done for him: and all men were full of wonder.
vs.w: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.

lessons.memtext: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
lessons.memE: And he would not let him, but said to him, Go to your house, to your friends, and give them news of the great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.
lessons.memW: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”

G1140: a dæmonic being; by extension a deity
neuter of a derivative of G1142 (δαίμων);
G1653: to compassionate (by word or deed, specially, by divine grace)
have compassion (pity on), have (obtain, receive, shew) mercy (on)

lessons.title: Power to Open Eyes
lessons.question: What does it mean to really see?
lessons.note: The disciples wanted someone to blame for the man's blindness. Jesus said it was so the works of God could be shown in him. The healed man could not answer every hard question, but he knew one thing: once he was blind, and now he could see. In the end he saw more than his eyes could: he believed and worshipped Jesus.
lessons.reflect: What is one thing you know for sure about Jesus so far?
lessons.declare: Once I was blind, but now I see.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: And as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind from his birth.
vs.e: And when he went on his way, he saw a man blind from birth.
vs.w: As he passed by, he saw a man blind from birth.

vs.t: And his disciples asked him, saying, Master, who did sin, this man, or his parents, that he was born blind?
vs.e: And his disciples put a question to him, saying, Master, was it because of this man's sin, or the sin of his father and mother, that he has been blind from birth?
vs.w: His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, that he was born blind?”

vs.t: Jesus answered, Neither hath this man sinned, nor his parents: but that the works of God should be made manifest in him.
vs.e: Jesus said in answer, It was not because of his sin, or because of his father's or mother's; it was so that the works of God might be seen openly in him.
vs.w: Jesus answered, “This man didn’t sin, nor did his parents; but, that the works of God might be revealed in him.

vs.t: I must work the works of him that sent me, while it is day: the night cometh, when no man can work.
vs.e: While it is day we have to do the works of him who sent me: the night comes when no work may be done.
vs.w: I must work the works of him who sent me while it is day. The night is coming, when no one can work.

vs.t: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
vs.e: As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
vs.w: While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”

vs.t: When he had thus spoken, he spat on the ground, and made clay of the spittle, and he anointed the eyes of the blind man with the clay,
vs.e: Having said these words, he put earth, mixed with water from his mouth, on the man's eyes,
vs.w: When he had said this, he spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, anointed the blind man’s eyes with the mud,

vs.t: And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.
vs.e: And said to him, Go and make yourself clean in the bath of Siloam (the sense of the name is, Sent). So he went away and, after washing, came back able to see.
vs.w: and said to him, “Go, wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). So he went away, washed, and came back seeing.

vs.t: The neighbours therefore, and they which before had seen him that he was blind, said, Is not this he that sat and begged?
vs.e: Then the neighbours and others who had seen him before in the street, with his hand out for money, said, Is not this the man who got money from people?
vs.w: The neighbors therefore, and those who saw that he was blind before, said, “Isn’t this he who sat and begged?”

vs.t: Some said, This is he: others said, He is like him: but he said, I am he.
vs.e: Some said, It is he: others said, No, but he is like him. He said, I am he.
vs.w: Others were saying, “It is he.” Still others were saying, “He looks like him.” He said, “I am he.”

vs.t: Therefore said they unto him, How were thine eyes opened?
vs.e: So they said to him, How then were your eyes made open?
vs.w: They therefore were asking him, “How were your eyes opened?”

vs.t: He answered and said, A man that is called Jesus made clay, and anointed mine eyes, and said unto me, Go to the pool of Siloam, and wash: and I went and washed, and I received sight.
vs.e: His answer was: The man who is named Jesus put earth mixed with water on my eyes, and said to me, Go and make yourself clean in Siloam: so I went away and, after washing, am now able to see.
vs.w: He answered, “A man called Jesus made mud, anointed my eyes, and said to me, ‘Go to the pool of Siloam and wash.’ So I went away and washed, and I received sight.”

vs.t: Then again called they the man that was blind, and said unto him, Give God the praise: we know that this man is a sinner.
vs.e: So they sent a second time for the man who had been blind and they said to him, Give glory to God: it is clear to us that this man is a sinner.
vs.w: So they called the man who was blind a second time, and said to him, “Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.”

vs.t: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
vs.e: He said in answer, I have no knowledge if he is a sinner or not, but one thing I am certain about; I was blind, and now I see.
vs.w: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

vs.t: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when he had found him, he said unto him, Dost thou believe on the Son of God?
vs.e: It came to the ears of Jesus that they had put him out, and meeting him he said, Have you faith in the Son of man?
vs.w: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and finding him, he said, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”

vs.t: He answered and said, Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him?
vs.e: He said in answer, And who is he, Lord? Say, so that I may have faith in him.
vs.w: He answered, “Who is he, Lord, that I may believe in him?”

vs.t: And Jesus said unto him, Thou hast both seen him, and it is he that talketh with thee.
vs.e: Jesus said to him, You have seen him; it is he who is talking to you.
vs.w: Jesus said to him, “You have both seen him, and it is he who speaks with you.”

vs.t: And he said, Lord, I believe. And he worshipped him.
vs.e: And he said, Lord, I have faith. And he gave him worship.
vs.w: He said, “Lord, I believe!” and he worshiped him.

lessons.memtext: He answered and said, Whether he be a sinner or no, I know not: one thing I know, that, whereas I was blind, now I see.
lessons.memE: He said in answer, I have no knowledge if he is a sinner or not, but one thing I am certain about; I was blind, and now I see.
lessons.memW: He therefore answered, “I don’t know if he is a sinner. One thing I do know: that though I was blind, now I see.”

G5185: opaque (as if smoky), i.e. (by analogy) blind (physically or mentally)
G4100: to have faith (in, upon, or with respect to, a person or thing), i.e. credit; by implication, to entrust (especially one's spiritual well-being to Christ)
believe(-r), commit (to trust), put in trust with

lessons.title: Power over Death
lessons.question: Is there hope beyond death?
lessons.note: Lazarus had been dead four days when Jesus arrived. Martha and Mary were heartbroken, and Jesus wept with them. Then He made an incredible claim: "I am the resurrection, and the life." He called into the tomb, and the dead man walked out. Jesus cares about our grief, and He has the final word over death.
lessons.reflect: Jesus asked Martha, "Believest thou this?" How would you answer Him?
lessons.declare: Jesus is the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in Him shall live.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: Then when Jesus came, he found that he had lain in the grave four days already.
vs.e: Now when Jesus came, he made the discovery that Lazarus had been put into the earth four days before.
vs.w: So when Jesus came, he found that he had been in the tomb four days already.

vs.t: Now Bethany was nigh unto Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off:
vs.e: Now Bethany was near to Jerusalem, about two miles away;
vs.w: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.

vs.t: And many of the Jews came to Martha and Mary, to comfort them concerning their brother.
vs.e: And a number of Jews had come to Martha and Mary to give them comfort about their brother.
vs.w: Many of the Jews had joined the women around Martha and Mary, to console them concerning their brother.

vs.t: Then Martha, as soon as she heard that Jesus was coming, went and met him: but Mary sat still in the house.
vs.e: When Martha had the news that Jesus was on the way, she went out to him, but Mary did not go from the house.
vs.w: Then when Martha heard that Jesus was coming, she went and met him, but Mary stayed in the house.

vs.t: Then said Martha unto Jesus, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
vs.e: Then Martha said to Jesus, Lord, if you had been here my brother would not be dead.
vs.w: Therefore Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.

vs.t: But I know, that even now, whatsoever thou wilt ask of God, God will give it thee.
vs.e: But I am certain that, even now, whatever request you make to God, God will give it to you.
vs.w: Even now I know that whatever you ask of God, God will give you.”

vs.t: Jesus saith unto her, Thy brother shall rise again.
vs.e: Jesus said to her, Your brother will come to life again.
vs.w: Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”

vs.t: Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day.
vs.e: Martha said to him, I am certain that he will come to life again when all come back from the dead at the last day.
vs.w: Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.”

vs.t: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
vs.e: Jesus said to her, I am myself that day and that life; he who has faith in me will have life even if he is dead;
vs.w: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.

vs.t: And whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die. Believest thou this?
vs.e: And no one who is living and has faith in me will ever see death. Is this your faith?
vs.w: Whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”

vs.t: She saith unto him, Yea, Lord: I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, which should come into the world.
vs.e: She said to him, Yes, Lord: my faith is that you are the Christ, the Son of God, who was to come into the world.
vs.w: She said to him, “Yes, Lord. I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world.”

vs.t: Then when Mary was come where Jesus was, and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying unto him, Lord, if thou hadst been here, my brother had not died.
vs.e: When Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she went down at his feet, saying, Lord, if you had been here my brother would not be dead.
vs.w: Therefore when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw him, she fell down at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.”

vs.t: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping which came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,
vs.e: And when Jesus saw her weeping, and saw the Jews weeping who came with her, his spirit was moved and he was troubled,
vs.w: When Jesus therefore saw her weeping, and the Jews weeping who came with her, he groaned in the spirit, and was troubled,

vs.t: And said, Where have ye laid him? They said unto him, Lord, come and see.
vs.e: And said, Where have you put him? They said, Come and see, Lord.
vs.w: and said, “Where have you laid him?” They told him, “Lord, come and see.”

vs.t: Jesus wept.
vs.e: And Jesus himself was weeping.
vs.w: Jesus wept.

vs.t: Then said the Jews, Behold how he loved him!
vs.e: So the Jews said, See how dear he was to him!
vs.w: The Jews therefore said, “See how much affection he had for him!”

vs.t: And some of them said, Could not this man, which opened the eyes of the blind, have caused that even this man should not have died?
vs.e: But some of them said, This man, who made open the eyes of the blind man, was he not able to keep his friend from death?
vs.w: Some of them said, “Couldn’t this man, who opened the eyes of him who was blind, have also kept this man from dying?”

vs.t: Jesus therefore again groaning in himself cometh to the grave. It was a cave, and a stone lay upon it.
vs.e: So Jesus, deeply troubled in heart, came to the place of the dead. It was a hole in the rock, and a stone was over the opening.
vs.w: Jesus therefore, again groaning in himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.

vs.t: Jesus said, Take ye away the stone. Martha, the sister of him that was dead, saith unto him, Lord, by this time he stinketh: for he hath been dead four days.
vs.e: Jesus said, Take away the stone. Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said, Lord, by this time the body will be smelling, for he has been dead four days.
vs.w: Jesus said, “Take away the stone.” Martha, the sister of him who was dead, said to him, “Lord, by this time there is a stench, for he has been dead four days.”

vs.t: Jesus saith unto her, Said I not unto thee, that, if thou wouldest believe, thou shouldest see the glory of God?
vs.e: Jesus said to her, Did I not say to you that if you had faith you would see the glory of God?
vs.w: Jesus said to her, “Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?”

vs.t: Then they took away the stone from the place where the dead was laid. And Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
vs.e: So they took away the stone. And Jesus, looking up to heaven, said, Father, I give praise to you for hearing me.
vs.w: So they took away the stone from the place where the dead man was lying. Jesus lifted up his eyes, and said, “Father, I thank you that you listened to me.

vs.t: And I knew that thou hearest me always: but because of the people which stand by I said it, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.
vs.e: I was certain that your ears are at all times open to me, but I said it because of these who are here, so that they may see that you sent me.
vs.w: I know that you always listen to me, but because of the multitude standing around I said this, that they may believe that you sent me.”

vs.t: And when he thus had spoken, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth.
vs.e: Then he said in a loud voice, Lazarus, come out!
vs.w: When he had said this, he cried with a loud voice, “Lazarus, come out!”

vs.t: And he that was dead came forth, bound hand and foot with graveclothes: and his face was bound about with a napkin. Jesus saith unto them, Loose him, and let him go.
vs.e: And he who was dead came out, with linen bands folded tightly about his hands and feet, and a cloth about his face. Jesus said to them, Make him free and let him go.
vs.w: He who was dead came out, bound hand and foot with wrappings, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, “Free him, and let him go.”

lessons.memtext: Jesus said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:
lessons.memE: Jesus said to her, I am myself that day and that life; he who has faith in me will have life even if he is dead;
lessons.memW: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. He who believes in me will still live, even if he dies.

G386: a standing up again, i.e. (literally) a resurrection from death (individual, genitive case or by implication, (its author)), or (figuratively) a (moral) recovery (of spiritual truth)
raised to life again, resurrection, rise from the dead, that should rise, rising again

lessons.title: The Risen Lord
lessons.question: Can I really believe Jesus rose from the dead?
lessons.note: The disciples were hiding behind locked doors when the risen Jesus stood among them and said, "Peace be unto you." Thomas wasn't there and refused to believe without proof. A week later Jesus came again and invited him to touch His wounds. Thomas answered, "My Lord and my God." John says these signs are written so that you might believe and have life.
lessons.reflect: What doubts or questions do you still have? Jesus welcomed Thomas's honesty.
lessons.declare: Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and believing, I have life through His name.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: Then the same day at evening, being the first day of the week, when the doors were shut where the disciples were assembled for fear of the Jews, came Jesus and stood in the midst, and saith unto them, Peace be unto you.
vs.e: At evening on that day, the first day of the week, when, for fear of the Jews, the doors were shut where the disciples were, Jesus came among them and said to them, May peace be with you!
vs.w: When therefore it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and when the doors were locked where the disciples were assembled, for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the middle, and said to them, “Peace be to you.”

vs.t: And when he had so said, he shewed unto them his hands and his side. Then were the disciples glad, when they saw the Lord.
vs.e: And when he had said this, he let them see his hands and his side. Then the disciples were glad when they saw the Lord.
vs.w: When he had said this, he showed them his hands and his side. The disciples therefore were glad when they saw the Lord.

vs.t: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you.
vs.e: And Jesus said to them again, May peace be with you! As the Father sent me, even so I now send you.
vs.w: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

vs.t: And when he had said this, he breathed on them, and saith unto them, Receive ye the Holy Ghost:
vs.e: And when he had said this, breathing on them, he said to them, Let the Holy Spirit come on you:
vs.w: When he had said this, he breathed on them, and said to them, “Receive the Holy Spirit!

vs.t: Whose soever sins ye remit, they are remitted unto them; and whose soever sins ye retain, they are retained.
vs.e: Any to whom you give forgiveness, will be made free from their sins; and any from whom you keep back forgiveness, will still be in their sins.
vs.w: If you forgive anyone’s sins, they have been forgiven them. If you retain anyone’s sins, they have been retained.”

vs.t: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
vs.e: Now Thomas, one of the twelve, named Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
vs.w: But Thomas, one of the twelve, called Didymus, wasn’t with them when Jesus came.

vs.t: The other disciples therefore said unto him, We have seen the Lord. But he said unto them, Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.
vs.e: So the other disciples said to him, We have seen the Lord. But he said to them, If I do not see in his hands the print of the nails and put my finger into the print of the nails, and if I do not put my hand into his side, I will never have belief.
vs.w: The other disciples therefore said to him, “We have seen the Lord!” But he said to them, “Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails, put my finger into the print of the nails, and put my hand into his side, I will not believe.”

vs.t: And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.
vs.e: And after eight days, his disciples were again in the house and Thomas was with them. Though the doors were shut, Jesus came, and taking his place in the middle of them, he said, May peace be with you!
vs.w: After eight days again his disciples were inside and Thomas was with them. Jesus came, the doors being locked, and stood in the middle, and said, “Peace be to you.”

vs.t: Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.
vs.e: Then he said to Thomas, Put out your finger, and see my hands; and put your hand here into my side: and be no longer in doubt but have belief.
vs.w: Then he said to Thomas, “Reach here your finger, and see my hands. Reach here your hand, and put it into my side. Don’t be unbelieving, but believing.”

vs.t: And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.
vs.e: And Thomas said in answer, My Lord and my God!
vs.w: Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”

vs.t: Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
vs.e: Jesus said to him, Because you have seen me you have belief: a blessing will be on those who have belief though they have not seen me!
vs.w: Jesus said to him, “Because you have seen me, you have believed. Blessed are those who have not seen, and have believed.”

vs.t: And many other signs truly did Jesus in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book:
vs.e: A number of other signs Jesus did before his disciples which are not recorded in this book:
vs.w: Therefore Jesus did many other signs in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book;

vs.t: But these are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.
vs.e: But these are recorded, so that you may have faith that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and so that, having this faith you may have life in his name.
vs.w: but these are written, that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing you may have life in his name.

lessons.title: In the Beginning
lessons.question: Where did we come from, and why are we here?
lessons.note: The Bible's story begins with God. He created the heavens and the earth, and everything He made was very good. People were made differently from everything else: in God's own image, to know Him, enjoy Him and care for His world. There was only one boundary, and it came with a warning.
lessons.reflect: What does it mean to you that you were made in God's image?
lessons.declare: God created me in His image, and He made everything very good.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
vs.e: At the first God made the heaven and the earth.
vs.w: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

vs.t: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
vs.e: And God said, Let us make man in our image, like us: and let him have rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the air and over the cattle and over all the earth and over every living thing which goes flat on the earth.
vs.w: God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”

vs.t: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
vs.e: And God made man in his image, in the image of God he made him: male and female he made them.
vs.w: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

vs.t: And God blessed them, and God said unto them, Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over every living thing that moveth upon the earth.
vs.e: And God gave them his blessing and said to them, Be fertile and have increase, and make the earth full and be masters of it; be rulers over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the air and over every living thing moving on the earth.
vs.w: God blessed them. God said to them, “Be fruitful, multiply, fill the earth, and subdue it. Have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the sky, and over every living thing that moves on the earth.”

vs.t: And God said, Behold, I have given you every herb bearing seed, which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree, in the which is the fruit of a tree yielding seed; to you it shall be for meat.
vs.e: And God said, See, I have given you every plant producing seed, on the face of all the earth, and every tree which has fruit producing seed: they will be for your food:
vs.w: God said, “Behold, I have given you every herb yielding seed, which is on the surface of all the earth, and every tree, which bears fruit yielding seed. It will be your food.

vs.t: And to every beast of the earth, and to every fowl of the air, and to every thing that creepeth upon the earth, wherein there is life, I have given every green herb for meat: and it was so.
vs.e: And to every beast of the earth and to every bird of the air and every living thing moving on the face of the earth I have given every green plant for food: and it was so.
vs.w: To every animal of the earth, and to every bird of the sky, and to everything that creeps on the earth, in which there is life, I have given every green herb for food;” and it was so.

vs.t: And God saw every thing that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. And the evening and the morning were the sixth day.
vs.e: And God saw everything which he had made and it was very good. And there was evening and there was morning, the sixth day.
vs.w: God saw everything that he had made, and, behold, it was very good. There was evening and there was morning, a sixth day.

vs.t: And the Lord God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to dress it and to keep it.
vs.e: And the Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to do work in it and take care of it.
vs.w: Yahweh God took the man, and put him into the garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

vs.t: And the Lord God commanded the man, saying, Of every tree of the garden thou mayest freely eat:
vs.e: And the Lord God gave the man orders, saying, You may freely take of the fruit of every tree of the garden:
vs.w: Yahweh God commanded the man, saying, “You may freely eat of every tree of the garden;

vs.t: But of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, thou shalt not eat of it: for in the day that thou eatest thereof thou shalt surely die.
vs.e: But of the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil you may not take; for on the day when you take of it, death will certainly come to you.
vs.w: but you shall not eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil; for in the day that you eat of it, you will surely die.”

lessons.memtext: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
lessons.memE: And God made man in his image, in the image of God he made him: male and female he made them.
lessons.memW: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
