lessons.title: Everything Broke
lessons.question: Why is the world so broken?
lessons.note: The serpent questioned God's word and His goodness. Adam and Eve chose their own way, and everything changed: shame, hiding, blame, pain and separation from God. Yet the first thing God did was come looking for them: "Where art thou?" He even made them clothes of skins, a first picture of a covering that would cost a life.
lessons.reflect: Where do you see the brokenness of Genesis 3 in the world, or in your own life?
lessons.declare: Sin broke our relationship with God, but God still comes looking for me.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?
vs.e: Now the snake was wiser than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made. And he said to the woman, Has God truly said that you may not take of the fruit of any tree in the garden?
vs.w: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”

vs.t: And the woman said unto the serpent, We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden:
vs.e: And the woman said, We may take of the fruit of the trees in the garden:
vs.w: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,

vs.t: But of the fruit of the tree which is in the midst of the garden, God hath said, Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.
vs.e: But of the fruit of the tree in the middle of the garden, God has said, If you take of it or put your hands on it, death will come to you.
vs.w: but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’ ”

vs.t: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
vs.e: And the snake said, Death will not certainly come to you:
vs.w: The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,

vs.t: For God doth know that in the day ye eat thereof, then your eyes shall be opened, and ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.
vs.e: For God sees that on the day when you take of its fruit, your eyes will be open, and you will be as gods, having knowledge of good and evil.
vs.w: for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

vs.t: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and a tree to be desired to make one wise, she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.
vs.e: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and a delight to the eyes, and to be desired to make one wise, she took of its fruit, and gave it to her husband.
vs.w: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.

vs.t: And the eyes of them both were opened, and they knew that they were naked; and they sewed fig leaves together, and made themselves aprons.
vs.e: And their eyes were open and they were conscious that they had no clothing and they made themselves coats of leaves stitched together.
vs.w: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.

vs.t: And they heard the voice of the Lord God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the Lord God amongst the trees of the garden.
vs.e: And there came to them the sound of the Lord God walking in the garden in the evening wind: and the man and his wife went to a secret place among the trees of the garden, away from the eyes of the Lord God.
vs.w: They heard Yahweh God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden.

vs.t: And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?
vs.e: And the voice of the Lord God came to the man, saying, Where are you?
vs.w: Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

vs.t: And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.
vs.e: And he said, Hearing your voice in the garden I was full of fear, because I was without clothing: and I kept myself from your eyes.
vs.w: The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”

vs.t: And he said, Who told thee that thou wast naked? Hast thou eaten of the tree, whereof I commanded thee that thou shouldest not eat?
vs.e: And he said, Who gave you the knowledge that you were without clothing? Have you taken of the fruit of the tree which I said you were not to take?
vs.w: God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”

vs.t: And the man said, The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.
vs.e: And the man said, The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me the fruit of the tree and I took it.
vs.w: The man said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”

vs.t: And the Lord God said unto the woman, What is this that thou hast done? And the woman said, The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.
vs.e: And the Lord God said to the woman, What have you done? And the woman said, I was tricked by the deceit of the snake and I took it.
vs.w: Yahweh God said to the woman, “What have you done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

vs.t: Unto Adam also and to his wife did the Lord God make coats of skins, and clothed them.
vs.e: And the Lord God made for Adam and for his wife coats of skins for their clothing.
vs.w: Yahweh God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.

vs.t: And the Lord God said, Behold, the man is become as one of us, to know good and evil: and now, lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever:
vs.e: And the Lord God said, Now the man has become like one of us, having knowledge of good and evil; and now if he puts out his hand and takes of the fruit of the tree of life, he will go on living for ever.
vs.w: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—”

vs.t: Therefore the Lord God sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken.
vs.e: So the Lord God sent him out of the garden of Eden to be a worker on the earth from which he was taken.
vs.w: Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.

vs.t: So he drove out the man; and he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life.
vs.e: So he sent the man out; and at the east of the garden of Eden he put winged ones and a flaming sword turning every way to keep the way to the tree of life.
vs.w: So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.

lessons.title: Judgment and Rescue
lessons.question: How does God respond to evil?
lessons.note: Evil filled the earth and it grieved God's heart. A holy God must judge evil, but He also provided a way of escape: an ark. Noah found grace in God's eyes, and everyone who went into the ark was saved. Afterwards God made a covenant, with the rainbow as its sign.
lessons.reflect: The ark had one door. What does that suggest about God's way of rescue?
lessons.declare: God judges sin, but by His grace He provides a way of rescue.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: And God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.
vs.e: And the Lord saw that the sin of man was great on the earth, and that all the thoughts of his heart were evil.
vs.w: Yahweh saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of man’s heart was continually only evil.

vs.t: And it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him at his heart.
vs.e: And the Lord had sorrow because he had made man on the earth, and grief was in his heart.
vs.w: Yahweh was sorry that he had made man on the earth, and it grieved him in his heart.

vs.t: And the Lord said, I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth; both man, and beast, and the creeping thing, and the fowls of the air; for it repenteth me that I have made them.
vs.e: And the Lord said, I will take away man, whom I have made, from the face of the earth, even man and beast and that which goes on the earth and every bird of the air; for I have sorrow for having made them.
vs.w: Yahweh said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the surface of the ground—man, along with animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky—for I am sorry that I have made them.”

vs.t: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
vs.e: But Noah had grace in the eyes of God.
vs.w: But Noah found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.

vs.t: And God said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth.
vs.e: And God said to Noah, The end of all flesh has come; the earth is full of their violent doings, and now I will put an end to them with the earth.
vs.w: God said to Noah, “I will bring an end to all flesh, for the earth is filled with violence through them. Behold, I will destroy them and the earth.

vs.t: Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.
vs.e: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood with rooms in it, and make it safe from the water inside and out.
vs.w: Make a ship of gopher wood. You shall make rooms in the ship, and shall seal it inside and outside with pitch.

vs.t: And the Lord said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.
vs.e: And the Lord said to Noah, Take all your family and go into the ark, for you only in this generation have I seen to be upright.
vs.w: Yahweh said to Noah, “Come with all of your household into the ship, for I have seen your righteousness before me in this generation.

vs.t: And I will establish my covenant with you; neither shall all flesh be cut off any more by the waters of a flood; neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth.
vs.e: And I will make my agreement with you; never again will all flesh be cut off by the waters; never again will the waters come over all the earth for its destruction.
vs.w: I will establish my covenant with you: All flesh will not be cut off any more by the waters of the flood. There will never again be a flood to destroy the earth.”

vs.t: And God said, This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:
vs.e: And God said, This is the sign of the agreement which I make between me and you and every living thing with you, for all future generations:
vs.w: God said, “This is the token of the covenant which I make between me and you and every living creature that is with you, for perpetual generations:

vs.t: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.
vs.e: I will put my bow in the cloud and it will be for a sign of the agreement between me and the earth.
vs.w: I set my rainbow in the cloud, and it will be a sign of a covenant between me and the earth.

lessons.memtext: But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.
lessons.memE: But Noah had grace in the eyes of God.
lessons.memW: But Noah found favor in Yahweh’s eyes.

lessons.title: God Will Provide
lessons.question: What does it cost to make things right with God?
lessons.note: God asked Abraham to offer his only son, Isaac. As they climbed the mountain, Isaac asked, "where is the lamb?" Abraham answered, "God will provide himself a lamb." At the last moment God stopped him and provided a ram in Isaac's place. A substitute died so that the son could live. The story points forward to another Son, on another hill.
lessons.reflect: What do you think it means for someone to take your place?
lessons.declare: God Himself provides the Lamb in my place.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.
vs.e: Now after these things, God put Abraham to the test, and said to him, Abraham; and he said, Here am I.
vs.w: After these things, God tested Abraham, and said to him, “Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”

vs.t: And he said, Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac, whom thou lovest, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.
vs.e: And he said to him, Take your son, your dearly loved only son Isaac, and go to the land of Moriah and give him as a burned offering on one of the mountains of which I will give you knowledge.
vs.w: He said, “Now take your son, your only son, Isaac, whom you love, and go into the land of Moriah. Offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains which I will tell you of.”

vs.t: And Abraham rose up early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son, and clave the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.
vs.e: And Abraham got up early in the morning, and made ready his ass, and took with him two of his young men and Isaac, his son, and after the wood for the burned offering had been cut, he went on his way to the place of which God had given him word.
vs.w: Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his donkey; and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son. He split the wood for the burnt offering, and rose up, and went to the place of which God had told him.

vs.t: Then on the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.
vs.e: And on the third day, Abraham, lifting up his eyes, saw the place a long way off.
vs.w: On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place far off.

vs.t: And Abraham said unto his young men, Abide ye here with the ass; and I and the lad will go yonder and worship, and come again to you.
vs.e: Then he said to his young men, Keep here with the ass; and I and the boy will go on and give worship and come back again to you.
vs.w: Abraham said to his young men, “Stay here with the donkey. The boy and I will go over there. We will worship, and come back to you.”

vs.t: And Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took the fire in his hand, and a knife; and they went both of them together.
vs.e: And Abraham put the wood for the burned offering on his son's back, and he himself took the fire and the knife in his hand, and the two of them went on together.
vs.w: Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son. He took in his hand the fire and the knife. They both went together.

vs.t: And Isaac spake unto Abraham his father, and said, My father: and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, Behold the fire and the wood: but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?
vs.e: Then Isaac said to Abraham, My father; and he said, Here am I, my son. And he said, We have wood and fire here, but where is the lamb for the burned offering?
vs.w: Isaac spoke to Abraham his father, and said, “My father?” He said, “Here I am, my son.” He said, “Here is the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for a burnt offering?”

vs.t: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
vs.e: And Abraham said, God himself will give the lamb for the burned offering: so they went on together.
vs.w: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.

vs.t: And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built an altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar upon the wood.
vs.e: And they came to the place of which God had given him knowledge; and there Abraham made the altar and put the wood in place on it, and having made tight the bands round Isaac his son, he put him on the wood on the altar.
vs.w: They came to the place which God had told him of. Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, on the wood.

vs.t: And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
vs.e: And stretching out his hand, Abraham took the knife to put his son to death.
vs.w: Abraham stretched out his hand, and took the knife to kill his son.

vs.t: And the angel of the Lord called unto him out of heaven, and said, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I.
vs.e: But the voice of the angel of the Lord came from heaven, saying, Abraham, Abraham: and he said, Here am I.
vs.w: Yahweh’s angel called to him out of the sky, and said, “Abraham, Abraham!” He said, “Here I am.”

vs.t: And he said, Lay not thine hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him: for now I know that thou fearest God, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son from me.
vs.e: And he said, Let not your hand be stretched out against the boy to do anything to him; for now I am certain that the fear of God is in your heart, because you have not kept back your son, your only son, from me.
vs.w: He said, “Don’t lay your hand on the boy or do anything to him. For now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me.”

vs.t: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
vs.e: And lifting up his eyes, Abraham saw a sheep fixed by its horns in the brushwood: and Abraham took the sheep and made a burned offering of it in place of his son.
vs.w: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.

vs.t: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah–jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.
vs.e: And Abraham gave that place the name Yahweh-yireh: as it is said to this day, In the mountain the Lord is seen.
vs.w: Abraham called the name of that place “Yahweh Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “On Yahweh’s mountain, it will be provided.”

lessons.memE: And Abraham said, God himself will give the lamb for the burned offering: so they went on together.
lessons.memW: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.

lessons.title: The Promised Saviour
lessons.question: Who did God promise to send?
lessons.note: Hundreds of years before it happened, God promised a child born of a virgin, called Immanuel, "God with us". Isaiah described a servant who would be wounded for our transgressions and carry our sins. Then one night, angels told shepherds the good news: the Saviour had been born in Bethlehem.
lessons.reflect: Why do you think the angels called it "good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people"?
lessons.declare: Unto me is born a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
vs.e: For this cause the Lord himself will give you a sign; a young woman is now with child, and she will give birth to a son, and she will give him the name Immanuel.
vs.w: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold, the virgin will conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.

vs.t: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.
vs.e: But it was our pain he took, and our diseases were put on him: while to us he seemed as one diseased, on whom God's punishment had come.
vs.w: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.

vs.t: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
vs.e: But it was for our sins he was wounded, and for our evil doings he was crushed: he took the punishment by which we have peace, and by his wounds we are made well.
vs.w: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

vs.t: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
vs.e: We all went wandering like sheep; going every one of us after his desire; and the Lord put on him the punishment of us all.
vs.w: All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

vs.t: And there were in the same country shepherds abiding in the field, keeping watch over their flock by night.
vs.e: And in the same country there were keepers of sheep in the fields, watching over their flock by night.
vs.w: There were shepherds in the same country staying in the field, and keeping watch by night over their flock.

vs.t: And, lo, the angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone round about them: and they were sore afraid.
vs.e: And an angel of the Lord came to them, and the glory of the Lord was shining round about them: and fear came on them.
vs.w: Behold, an angel of the Lord stood by them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were terrified.

vs.t: And the angel said unto them, Fear not: for, behold, I bring you good tidings of great joy, which shall be to all people.
vs.e: And the angel said, Have no fear; for truly, I give you good news of great joy which will be for all the people:
vs.w: The angel said to them, “Don’t be afraid, for behold, I bring you good news of great joy which will be to all the people.

vs.t: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
vs.e: For on this day, in the town of David, a Saviour has come to birth, who is Christ the Lord.
vs.w: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

vs.t: And this shall be a sign unto you; Ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger.
vs.e: And this is the sign to you: you will see a young child folded in linen, in the place where the cattle have their food.
vs.w: This is the sign to you: you will find a baby wrapped in strips of cloth, lying in a feeding trough.”

vs.t: And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising God, and saying,
vs.e: And suddenly there was with the angel a great band of spirits from heaven, giving praise to God, and saying,
vs.w: Suddenly, there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly army praising God, and saying,

vs.t: Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.
vs.e: Glory to God in the highest, and on the earth peace among men with whom he is well pleased.
vs.w: “Glory to God in the highest, on earth peace, good will toward men.”

lessons.memtext: For unto you is born this day in the city of David a Saviour, which is Christ the Lord.
lessons.memE: For on this day, in the town of David, a Saviour has come to birth, who is Christ the Lord.
lessons.memW: For there is born to you today, in David’s city, a Savior, who is Christ the Lord.

lessons.title: The Cross and the Empty Tomb
lessons.sub: He is not here, He is risen
lessons.question: Why did Jesus die, and does it matter that He rose?
lessons.note: Jesus was crucified between two criminals. Even on the cross He prayed for those killing Him and promised paradise to a dying thief who turned to Him. Like the lamb in Abraham's story, He died in our place. Three days later the women found the tomb empty: "He is not here, but is risen."
lessons.reflect: Which person at the cross do you relate to most: the crowd, a soldier, the thief, or the women watching?
lessons.declare: Jesus died for me and He is risen, just as He said.
ask: Is there anything in this story that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about people in this story?
What do you learn about Jesus or God? Does your view change?
Where do you see yourself in this story? Why?

vs.t: And when they were come to the place, which is called Calvary, there they crucified him, and the malefactors, one on the right hand, and the other on the left.
vs.e: And when they came to the place which is named Golgotha, they put him on the cross, and the evil-doers, one on the right side, and the other on the left.
vs.w: When they came to the place that is called “The Skull”, they crucified him there with the criminals, one on the right and the other on the left.

vs.t: Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do. And they parted his raiment, and cast lots.
vs.e: And Jesus said, Father, let them have forgiveness, for they have no knowledge of what they are doing. And they made division of his clothing among them by the decision of chance.
vs.w: Jesus said, “Father, forgive them, for they don’t know what they are doing.” Dividing his garments among them, they cast lots.

vs.t: And the people stood beholding. And the rulers also with them derided him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God.
vs.e: And the people were looking on. And the rulers made sport of him, saying, He was a saviour of others; let him do something for himself, if he is the Christ, the man of God's selection.
vs.w: The people stood watching. The rulers with them also scoffed at him, saying, “He saved others. Let him save himself, if this is the Christ of God, his chosen one!”

vs.t: And the soldiers also mocked him, coming to him, and offering him vinegar,
vs.e: And the men of the army made sport of him, coming to him and giving him bitter wine,
vs.w: The soldiers also mocked him, coming to him and offering him vinegar,

vs.t: And saying, If thou be the king of the Jews, save thyself.
vs.e: And saying, If you are the King of the Jews, get yourself free.
vs.w: and saying, “If you are the King of the Jews, save yourself!”

vs.t: And a superscription also was written over him in letters of Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
vs.e: And these words were put in writing over him, THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.
vs.w: An inscription was also written over him in letters of Greek, Latin, and Hebrew: “THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS.”

vs.t: And one of the malefactors which were hanged railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself and us.
vs.e: And one of the evil-doers on the cross, with bitter feeling, said to him, Are you not the Christ? Get yourself and us out of this.
vs.w: One of the criminals who was hanged insulted him, saying, “If you are the Christ, save yourself and us!”

vs.t: But the other answering rebuked him, saying, Dost not thou fear God, seeing thou art in the same condemnation?
vs.e: But the other, protesting, said, Have you no fear of God? for you have a part in the same punishment,
vs.w: But the other answered, and rebuking him said, “Don’t you even fear God, seeing you are under the same condemnation?

vs.t: And we indeed justly; for we receive the due reward of our deeds: but this man hath done nothing amiss.
vs.e: And with reason; for we have the right reward of our acts, but this man has done nothing wrong.
vs.w: And we indeed justly, for we receive the due reward for our deeds, but this man has done nothing wrong.”

vs.t: And he said unto Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest into thy kingdom.
vs.e: And he said, Jesus, keep me in mind when you come in your kingdom.
vs.w: He said to Jesus, “Lord, remember me when you come into your Kingdom.”

vs.t: And Jesus said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.
vs.e: And he said to him, Truly I say to you, Today you will be with me in Paradise.
vs.w: Jesus said to him, “Assuredly I tell you, today you will be with me in Paradise.”

vs.t: And it was about the sixth hour, and there was a darkness over all the earth until the ninth hour.
vs.e: And it was now about the sixth hour; and all the land was dark till the ninth hour;
vs.w: It was now about the sixth hour, and darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.

vs.t: And the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent in the midst.
vs.e: The light of the sun went out, and the curtain in the Temple was parted in two.
vs.w: The sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was torn in two.

vs.t: And when Jesus had cried with a loud voice, he said, Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit: and having said thus, he gave up the ghost.
vs.e: And Jesus gave a loud cry and said, Father, into your hands I give my spirit: and when he had said this, he gave up his spirit.
vs.w: Jesus, crying with a loud voice, said, “Father, into your hands I commit my spirit!” Having said this, he breathed his last.

vs.t: Now when the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.
vs.e: And when the captain saw what was done, he gave praise to God, saying, Without doubt this was an upright man.
vs.w: When the centurion saw what was done, he glorified God, saying, “Certainly this was a righteous man.”

vs.t: Now upon the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came unto the sepulchre, bringing the spices which they had prepared, and certain others with them.
vs.e: But on the first day of the week, at dawn, they came to the place where his body had been put, taking the spices which they had got ready.
vs.w: But on the first day of the week, at early dawn, they and some others came to the tomb, bringing the spices which they had prepared.

vs.t: And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre.
vs.e: And they saw that the stone had been rolled away.
vs.w: They found the stone rolled away from the tomb.

vs.t: And they entered in, and found not the body of the Lord Jesus.
vs.e: And they went in, but the body of the Lord Jesus was not there.
vs.w: They entered in, and didn’t find the Lord Jesus’ body.

vs.t: And it came to pass, as they were much perplexed thereabout, behold, two men stood by them in shining garments:
vs.e: And while they were in doubt about it, they saw two men in shining clothing by them:
vs.w: While they were greatly perplexed about this, behold, two men stood by them in dazzling clothing.

vs.t: And as they were afraid, and bowed down their faces to the earth, they said unto them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?
vs.e: And while their faces were bent down to the earth in fear, these said to them, Why are you looking for the living among the dead?
vs.w: Becoming terrified, they bowed their faces down to the earth. They said to them, “Why do you seek the living among the dead?

vs.t: He is not here, but is risen: remember how he spake unto you when he was yet in Galilee,
vs.e: He is not here, he has come back to life: have in mind what he said to you when he was still in Galilee, saying,
vs.w: He isn’t here, but is risen. Remember what he told you when he was still in Galilee,

vs.t: Saying, The Son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and the third day rise again.
vs.e: The Son of man will be given up into the hands of evil-doers, and be put to death on the cross, and on the third day he will come back to life.
vs.w: saying that the Son of Man must be delivered up into the hands of sinful men and be crucified, and the third day rise again?”

lessons.title: Your Response: Receive Jesus
lessons.sub: Will you say "I do" to Him?
lessons.question: What will I do with Jesus?
ask: What do these verses say about our problem?
What has God done about it?
What does God ask us to do?
lessons.note: Whichever set you have read, you have met Jesus: the One who forgives, welcomes, heals, sets free and conquers death, the Lamb God promised from the very beginning. The Bible says we have all sinned, and the wages of sin is death. But God showed His love in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us. Salvation is a gift of grace, received through faith, not earned. Believe in your heart that God raised Jesus from the dead and confess with your mouth that He is Lord. Jesus is knocking; you open the door.
lessons.reflect: Is there anything holding you back from receiving Jesus today?
lessons.declare: Jesus is Lord, and God raised Him from the dead. I open the door of my heart to Him.

vs.t: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
vs.e: For all have done wrong and are far from the glory of God;
vs.w: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;

vs.t: For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.
vs.e: For the reward of sin is death; but what God freely gives is eternal life in Jesus Christ our Lord.
vs.w: For the wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.

vs.t: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
vs.e: But God has made clear his love to us, in that, when we were still sinners, Christ gave his life for us.
vs.w: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

vs.t: For by grace are ye saved through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is the gift of God:
vs.e: Because by grace you have salvation through faith; and that not of yourselves: it is given by God:
vs.w: for by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God,

vs.t: Not of works, lest any man should boast.
vs.e: Not by works, so that no man may take glory to himself.
vs.w: not of works, that no one would boast.

vs.t: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
vs.e: Because, if you say with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and have faith in your heart that God has made him come back from the dead, you will have salvation:
vs.w: that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

vs.t: For with the heart man believeth unto righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made unto salvation.
vs.e: For with the heart man has faith to get righteousness, and with the mouth he says that Jesus is Lord to get salvation.
vs.w: For with the heart, one believes resulting in righteousness; and with the mouth confession is made resulting in salvation.

vs.t: Behold, I stand at the door, and knock: if any man hear my voice, and open the door, I will come in to him, and will sup with him, and he with me.
vs.e: See, I am waiting at the door and giving the sign; if my voice comes to any man's ears and he makes the door open, I will come in to him, and will take food with him and he with me.
vs.w: Behold, I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him, and will dine with him, and he with me.

title: Revive Me Again
intro: "Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?" (Psalm 85:6). Drifted from God? You are not too far gone. The Father is waiting with open arms. In these sessions, come back honestly, receive His mercy, rekindle your first love, and let revival start in your own heart.

lessons.title: The Father Is Waiting
lessons.sub: Coming home to His open arms
lessons.question: How does God respond when we come back to Him?
ask: What made the son decide to go home?
What did the father do when he saw him?
What do you learn about God's heart toward those who wander?
Where do you see yourself in this story?
lessons.note: The son "came to himself" in a pig pen and rehearsed a speech about being a servant. But the father had been watching the road. He saw his son a great way off, was moved with compassion, ran, and kissed him before the speech was finished. He gave him the robe, the ring and the shoes of a son, not a servant. However far you have drifted, this is how your Father receives you.
lessons.reflect: What has kept you away from God? What do you need to hear the Father say to you?
lessons.declare: My Father is running to meet me. I am coming home.

vs.t: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
vs.e: And he said, A certain man had two sons:
vs.w: He said, “A certain man had two sons.

vs.t: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me the portion of goods that falleth to me. And he divided unto them his living.
vs.e: And the younger of them said to his father, Father, give me that part of your property which will be mine. And he made division of his goods between them.
vs.w: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ He divided his livelihood between them.

vs.t: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.
vs.e: And not long after, the younger son got together everything which was his and took a journey into a far-away country, and there all his money went in foolish living.
vs.w: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.

vs.t: And when he had spent all, there arose a mighty famine in that land; and he began to be in want.
vs.e: And when everything was gone, there was no food to be had in that country, and he was in need.
vs.w: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.

vs.t: And he went and joined himself to a citizen of that country; and he sent him into his fields to feed swine.
vs.e: And he went and put himself into the hands of one of the people of that country, and he sent him into his fields to give the pigs their food.
vs.w: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

vs.t: And he would fain have filled his belly with the husks that the swine did eat: and no man gave unto him.
vs.e: And so great was his need that he would have been glad to take the pigs' food, and no one gave him anything.
vs.w: He wanted to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.

vs.t: And when he came to himself, he said, How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough and to spare, and I perish with hunger!
vs.e: But when he came to his senses, he said, What numbers of my father's servants have bread enough, and more, while I am near to death here through need of food!
vs.w: But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!

vs.t: I will arise and go to my father, and will say unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and before thee,
vs.e: I will get up and go to my father, and will say to him, Father, I have done wrong, against heaven and in your eyes:
vs.w: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.

vs.t: And am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.
vs.e: I am no longer good enough to be named your son: make me like one of your servants.
vs.w: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.” ’

vs.t: And he arose, and came to his father. But when he was yet a great way off, his father saw him, and had compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.
vs.e: And he got up and went to his father. But while he was still far away, his father saw him and was moved with pity for him and went quickly and took him in his arms and gave him a kiss.
vs.w: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

vs.t: And the son said unto him, Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.
vs.e: And his son said to him, Father, I have done wrong, against heaven and in your eyes: I am no longer good enough to be named your son.
vs.w: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

vs.t: But the father said to his servants, Bring forth the best robe, and put it on him; and put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet:
vs.e: But the father said to his servants, Get out the first robe quickly, and put it on him, and put a ring on his hand and shoes on his feet:
vs.w: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and sandals on his feet.

vs.t: And bring hither the fatted calf, and kill it; and let us eat, and be merry:
vs.e: And get the fat young ox and put it to death, and let us have a feast, and be glad.
vs.w: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let’s eat, and celebrate;

vs.t: For this my son was dead, and is alive again; he was lost, and is found. And they began to be merry.
vs.e: For this, my son, who was dead, is living again; he had gone away from me, and has come back. And they were full of joy.
vs.w: for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ Then they began to celebrate.

lessons.title: Honest Before God
lessons.sub: Create in me a clean heart
lessons.question: How do I come clean with God?
ask: What does David ask God for?
What does God promise if we confess our sins?
What happens to those who cover their sins?
lessons.note: David wrote Psalm 51 after his adultery and the murder of Uriah. He did not hide or excuse it. He named his sin, asked for mercy, and asked God to wash him, create a clean heart and restore the joy of his salvation. Coming back starts with honesty. If we confess, God is faithful and just to forgive and cleanse.
lessons.reflect: Is there something you need to bring into the light and confess to God today?
lessons.declare: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

vs.t: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David, when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath–sheba. Have mercy upon me, O God, according to thy lovingkindness: according unto the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions.
vs.e: Have pity on me, O God, in your mercy; out of a full heart, take away my sin.
vs.w: Have mercy on me, God, according to your loving kindness. According to the multitude of your tender mercies, blot out my transgressions.

vs.t: Wash me throughly from mine iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
vs.e: Let all my wrongdoing be washed away, and make me clean from evil.
vs.w: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity. Cleanse me from my sin.

vs.t: For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.
vs.e: For I am conscious of my error; my sin is ever before me.
vs.w: For I know my transgressions. My sin is constantly before me.

vs.t: Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight: that thou mightest be justified when thou speakest, and be clear when thou judgest.
vs.e: Against you, you only, have I done wrong, working that which is evil in your eyes; so that your words may be seen to be right, and you may be clear when you are judging.
vs.w: Against you, and you only, I have sinned, and done that which is evil in your sight, so you may be proved right when you speak, and justified when you judge.

vs.t: Behold, I was shapen in iniquity; and in sin did my mother conceive me.
vs.e: Truly, I was formed in evil, and in sin did my mother give me birth.
vs.w: Behold, I was born in iniquity. My mother conceived me in sin.

vs.t: Behold, thou desirest truth in the inward parts: and in the hidden part thou shalt make me to know wisdom.
vs.e: Your desire is for what is true in the inner parts: in the secrets of my soul you will give me knowledge of wisdom.
vs.w: Behold, you desire truth in the inward parts. You teach me wisdom in the inmost place.

vs.t: Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
vs.e: Make me free from sin with hyssop: let me be washed whiter than snow.
vs.w: Purify me with hyssop, and I will be clean. Wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.

vs.t: Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
vs.e: Make me full of joy and rapture; so that the bones which have been broken may be glad.
vs.w: Let me hear joy and gladness, that the bones which you have broken may rejoice.

vs.t: Hide thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities.
vs.e: Let your face be turned from my wrongdoing, and take away all my sins.
vs.w: Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all of my iniquities.

vs.t: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
vs.e: Make a clean heart in me, O God; give me a right spirit again.
vs.w: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

vs.t: Cast me not away from thy presence; and take not thy holy spirit from me.
vs.e: Do not put me away from before you, or take your holy spirit from me.
vs.w: Don’t throw me from your presence, and don’t take your Holy Spirit from me.

vs.t: Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation; and uphold me with thy free spirit.
vs.e: Give me back the joy of your salvation; let a free spirit be my support.
vs.w: Restore to me the joy of your salvation. Uphold me with a willing spirit.

vs.t: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
vs.e: If we say openly that we have done wrong, he is upright and true to his word, giving us forgiveness of sins and making us clean from all evil.
vs.w: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

vs.t: He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.
vs.e: He who keeps his sins secret will not do well; but one who is open about them, and gives them up, will get mercy.
vs.w: He who conceals his sins doesn’t prosper, but whoever confesses and renounces them finds mercy.

lessons.memtext: Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.
lessons.memE: Make a clean heart in me, O God; give me a right spirit again.
lessons.memW: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.

lessons.title: Restored After Failure
lessons.question: Can Jesus still use me after I have failed Him?
ask: How did Peter fail Jesus?
How did Jesus restore him?
What did Jesus ask Peter to do next?
Where do you see yourself in Peter's story?
lessons.note: Peter promised to die for Jesus, then denied Him three times and wept bitterly. After the resurrection, Jesus cooked him breakfast and asked three times, "Lovest thou me?", one question for each denial. He did not shame Peter; He restored him and gave him work to do: "Feed my sheep." Your failure is not the end of your story.
lessons.reflect: Jesus asks you today, "Lovest thou me?" How do you answer Him?
lessons.declare: Jesus restores me after failure and calls me to love and follow Him again.

vs.t: Then took they him, and led him, and brought him into the high priest’s house. And Peter followed afar off.
vs.e: And they made him a prisoner and took him away to the house of the high priest. But Peter went after them at a distance.
vs.w: They seized him, and led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. But Peter followed from a distance.

vs.t: And when they had kindled a fire in the midst of the hall, and were set down together, Peter sat down among them.
vs.e: And a fire was lighted in the middle of the open square, and they were seated together, and Peter was among them.
vs.w: When they had kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard, and had sat down together, Peter sat among them.

vs.t: But a certain maid beheld him as he sat by the fire, and earnestly looked upon him, and said, This man was also with him.
vs.e: And a certain woman-servant, seeing him in the light of the fire, and looking at him with attention, said, This man was with him.
vs.w: A certain servant girl saw him as he sat in the light, and looking intently at him, said, “This man also was with him.”

vs.t: And he denied him, saying, Woman, I know him not.
vs.e: But he said, Woman, it is not true; I have no knowledge of him.
vs.w: He denied Jesus, saying, “Woman, I don’t know him.”

vs.t: And after a little while another saw him, and said, Thou art also of them. And Peter said, Man, I am not.
vs.e: And after a little time, another saw him and said, You are one of them; and he said, Man, I am not.
vs.w: After a little while someone else saw him, and said, “You also are one of them!” But Peter answered, “Man, I am not!”

vs.t: And about the space of one hour after another confidently affirmed, saying, Of a truth this fellow also was with him: for he is a Galilean.
vs.e: And after about an hour, another man said, with decision, Certainly this man was with him, for he is a Galilaean.
vs.w: After about one hour passed, another confidently affirmed, saying, “Truly this man also was with him, for he is a Galilean!”

vs.t: And Peter said, Man, I know not what thou sayest. And immediately, while he yet spake, the cock crew.
vs.e: And Peter said, Man, I have no knowledge of these things of which you are talking. And straight away, while he was saying these words, there came the cry of a cock.
vs.w: But Peter said, “Man, I don’t know what you are talking about!” Immediately, while he was still speaking, a rooster crowed.

vs.t: And the Lord turned, and looked upon Peter. And Peter remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said unto him, Before the cock crow, thou shalt deny me thrice.
vs.e: And the Lord, turning, gave Peter a look. And the words of the Lord came to Peter's mind, how he had said, This night, before the hour of the cock's cry, you will be false to me three times.
vs.w: The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Then Peter remembered the Lord’s word, how he said to him, “Before the rooster crows you will deny me three times.”

vs.t: And Peter went out, and wept bitterly.
vs.e: And he went out, weeping bitterly.
vs.w: He went out, and wept bitterly.

vs.t: So when they had dined, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my lambs.
vs.e: Then when they had taken food, Jesus said to Simon Peter, Simon, son of John, is your love for me greater than the love of these others? He said to him, Yes, Lord; you are certain of my love for you. He said to him, Then give my lambs food.
vs.w: So when they had eaten their breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me more than these?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Feed my lambs.”

vs.t: He saith to him again the second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith unto him, Yea, Lord; thou knowest that I love thee. He saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
vs.e: Again, a second time, he said to him, Simon, son of John, have you any love for me? Yes, Lord, he said, you are certain of my love for you. Then take care of my sheep, said Jesus.
vs.w: He said to him again a second time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you love me?” He said to him, “Yes, Lord; you know that I have affection for you.” He said to him, “Tend my sheep.”

vs.t: He saith unto him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved because he said unto him the third time, Lovest thou me? And he said unto him, Lord, thou knowest all things; thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith unto him, Feed my sheep.
vs.e: He said to him a third time, Simon, son of John, am I dear to you? Now Peter was troubled in his heart because he put the question a third time, Am I dear to you? And he said to him, Lord, you have knowledge of all things; you see that you are dear to me. Jesus said to him, Then give my sheep food.
vs.w: He said to him the third time, “Simon, son of Jonah, do you have affection for me?” Peter was grieved because he asked him the third time, “Do you have affection for me?” He said to him, “Lord, you know everything. You know that I have affection for you.” Jesus said to him, “Feed my sheep.

vs.t: Verily, verily, I say unto thee, When thou wast young, thou girdedst thyself, and walkedst whither thou wouldest: but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another shall gird thee, and carry thee whither thou wouldest not.
vs.e: Truly I say to you, When you were young, you made yourself ready and went wherever you had a desire to go: but when you are old, you will put out your hands and another will make you ready, and you will be taken where you have no desire to go.
vs.w: Most certainly I tell you, when you were young, you dressed yourself and walked where you wanted to. But when you are old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you don’t want to go.”

vs.t: This spake he, signifying by what death he should glorify God. And when he had spoken this, he saith unto him, Follow me.
vs.e: Now this he said, pointing out the sort of death by which he would give God glory. And after saying this, he said to him, Come after me.
vs.w: Now he said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. When he had said this, he said to him, “Follow me.”

lessons.title: Remember Your First Love
lessons.sub: Return to what you did at first
lessons.question: What happened to my first love for Jesus?
ask: What did Jesus praise in the church at Ephesus, and what did He have against them?
What three things does Jesus tell them to do?
What does God promise in Hosea 14?
lessons.note: The church at Ephesus worked hard and stood for truth, but had left its first love. Busy service can replace closeness with Jesus. His cure is simple: remember how far you have fallen, repent, and do the first works again. Through Hosea, God promises to heal backsliding and love us freely.
lessons.reflect: What did you do when you first loved Jesus (prayer, the Word, worship, telling others) that you can return to this week?
lessons.declare: I remember my first love. I repent and return to the things I did at first.

vs.t: I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and how thou canst not bear them which are evil: and thou hast tried them which say they are apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars:
vs.e: I have knowledge of your doings, and of your hard work and long waiting, and that you will not put up with evil men, and have put to the test those who say they are Apostles and are not, and have seen that they are false;
vs.w: “I know your works, and your toil and perseverance, and that you can’t tolerate evil men, and have tested those who call themselves apostles, and they are not, and found them false.

vs.t: And hast borne, and hast patience, and for my name’s sake hast laboured, and hast not fainted.
vs.e: And you have the power of waiting, and have undergone trouble because of my name, without weariness.
vs.w: You have perseverance and have endured for my name’s sake, and have not grown weary.

vs.t: Nevertheless I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.
vs.e: But I have this against you, that you are turned away from your first love.
vs.w: But I have this against you, that you left your first love.

vs.t: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.
vs.e: So keep in mind where you were at first, and be changed in heart and do the first works; or I will come to you, and will take away your light from its place, if your hearts are not changed.
vs.w: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works; or else I am coming to you swiftly, and will move your lamp stand out of its place, unless you repent.

vs.t: For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.
vs.e: For my people have done two evils; they have given up me, the fountain of living waters, and have made for themselves water-holes, cut out from the rock, broken water-holes, of no use for storing water.
vs.w: “For my people have committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the spring of living waters, and cut out cisterns for themselves: broken cisterns that can’t hold water.

vs.t: O Israel, return unto the Lord thy God; for thou hast fallen by thine iniquity.
vs.e: O Israel, come back to the Lord your God; for your evil-doing has been the cause of your fall.
vs.w: Israel, return to Yahweh your God; for you have fallen because of your sin.

vs.t: Take with you words, and turn to the Lord: say unto him, Take away all iniquity, and receive us graciously: so will we render the calves of our lips.
vs.e: Take with you words, and come back to the Lord; say to him, Let there be forgiveness for all wrongdoing, so that we may take what is good, and give in payment the fruit of our lips.
vs.w: Take words with you, and return to Yahweh. Tell him, “Forgive all our sins, and accept that which is good: so we offer our lips like bulls.

vs.t: Asshur shall not save us; we will not ride upon horses: neither will we say any more to the work of our hands, Ye are our gods: for in thee the fatherless findeth mercy.
vs.e: Assyria will not be our salvation; we will not go on horses; we will not again say to the work of our hands, You are our gods; for in you there is mercy for the child who has no father.
vs.w: Assyria can’t save us. We won’t ride on horses; neither will we say any more to the work of our hands, ‘Our gods!’ for in you the fatherless finds mercy.”

vs.t: I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely: for mine anger is turned away from him.
vs.e: I will put right their errors; freely will my love be given to them, for my wrath is turned away from him.
vs.w: “I will heal their waywardness. I will love them freely; for my anger is turned away from him.

lessons.memtext: Remember therefore from whence thou art fallen, and repent, and do the first works; or else I will come unto thee quickly, and will remove thy candlestick out of his place, except thou repent.
lessons.memE: So keep in mind where you were at first, and be changed in heart and do the first works; or I will come to you, and will take away your light from its place, if your hearts are not changed.
lessons.memW: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and do the first works; or else I am coming to you swiftly, and will move your lamp stand out of its place, unless you repent.

lessons.title: Draw Near Again
lessons.sub: Return to Me and I will return to you
lessons.question: How do I get close to God again?
ask: What does God say to those who have turned away?
What steps does James give for drawing near to God?
What does God promise in return?
lessons.note: God's invitation is repeated all through Scripture: "Return unto me, and I will return unto you." To backsliders He says, "Return... and I will heal your backslidings." James gives practical steps: submit to God, resist the devil, draw near, cleanse your hands and humble yourself. Each step you take toward God, He meets you.
lessons.reflect: What is one practical step you can take this week to draw near to God?
lessons.declare: I draw near to God, and He draws near to me.

vs.t: Even from the days of your fathers ye are gone away from mine ordinances, and have not kept them. Return unto me, and I will return unto you, saith the Lord of hosts. But ye said, Wherein shall we return?
vs.e: From the days of your fathers you have been turned away from my rules and have not kept them. Come back to me, and I will come back to you, says the Lord of armies. But you say, How are we to come back?
vs.w: From the days of your fathers you have turned away from my ordinances, and have not kept them. Return to me, and I will return to you,” says Yahweh of Armies. “But you say, ‘How shall we return?’

vs.t: Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings. Behold, we come unto thee; for thou art the Lord our God.
vs.e: Come back, you children who have been turned away, and I will take away your desire for wandering. See, we have come to you, for you are the Lord our God.
vs.w: Return, you backsliding children, and I will heal your backsliding. “Behold, we have come to you; for you are Yahweh our God.

vs.t: Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
vs.e: For this cause be ruled by God; but make war on the Evil One and he will be put to flight before you.
vs.w: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

vs.t: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
vs.e: Come near to God and he will come near to you. Make your hands clean, you evil-doers; put away deceit from your hearts, you false in mind.
vs.w: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.

vs.t: Be afflicted, and mourn, and weep: let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to heaviness.
vs.e: Be troubled, with sorrow and weeping; let your laughing be turned to sorrow and your joy to grief.
vs.w: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning, and your joy to gloom.

vs.t: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.
vs.e: Make yourselves low in the eyes of the Lord and you will be lifted up by him.
vs.w: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.

lessons.memtext: Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
lessons.memE: Come near to God and he will come near to you. Make your hands clean, you evil-doers; put away deceit from your hearts, you false in mind.
lessons.memW: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.

lessons.title: Times of Refreshing
lessons.question: What does God do when we turn back to Him?
ask: What follows repentance in Acts 3:19?
Who does God revive, according to Isaiah 57:15?
What does Hosea 6 say God will do?
lessons.note: Revival is God breathing new life into what had grown cold. It begins with repentance and leads to times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord. The high and holy God lives with the humble and contrite to revive their spirit and heart. He has torn, and He will heal; He will revive us, and we shall live in His sight.
lessons.reflect: What area of your life feels dry? Ask God to revive it.
lessons.declare: I repent and turn, and times of refreshing come from the presence of the Lord.

vs.t: Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord;
vs.e: So then, let your hearts be changed and be turned to God, so that your sins may be completely taken away, and times of blessing may come from the Lord;
vs.w: “Repent therefore, and turn again, that your sins may be blotted out, so that there may come times of refreshing from the presence of the Lord,

vs.t: Wilt thou not revive us again: that thy people may rejoice in thee?
vs.e: Will you not give us life again, so that your people may be glad in you?
vs.w: Won’t you revive us again, that your people may rejoice in you?

vs.t: For thus saith the high and lofty One that inhabiteth eternity, whose name is Holy; I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite ones.
vs.e: For this is the word of him who is high and lifted up, whose resting-place is eternal, whose name is Holy: my resting-place is in the high and holy place, and with him who is crushed and poor in spirit, to give life to the spirit of the poor, and to make strong the heart of the crushed.
vs.w: For the high and lofty One who inhabits eternity, whose name is Holy, says: “I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also who is of a contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite.

vs.t: Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us; he hath smitten, and he will bind us up.
vs.e: Come, let us go back to the Lord; for he has given us wounds and he will make us well; he has given blows and he will give help.
vs.w: “Come! Let’s return to Yahweh; for he has torn us to pieces, and he will heal us; he has injured us, and he will bind up our wounds.

vs.t: After two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up, and we shall live in his sight.
vs.e: After two days he will give us life, and on the third day he will make us get up, and we will be living before him.
vs.w: After two days he will revive us. On the third day he will raise us up, and we will live before him.

vs.t: Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord: his going forth is prepared as the morning; and he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.
vs.e: And let us have knowledge, let us go after the knowledge of the Lord; his going out is certain as the dawn, his decisions go out like the light; he will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain watering the earth.
vs.w: Let’s acknowledge Yahweh. Let’s press on to know Yahweh. As surely as the sun rises, Yahweh will appear. He will come to us like the rain, like the spring rain that waters the earth.”

lessons.title: Guard Your Heart
lessons.sub: Staying close and running the race
lessons.question: How do I stay close to God and not drift again?
ask: What weights and sins does Hebrews 12 tell us to lay aside?
What does God promise about temptation?
Why do we need other believers to stay strong?
lessons.note: Most people do not fall away in one day; they drift. Guard your heart, because everything flows from it. Lay aside the weights that slow you down, keep your eyes on Jesus, and remember God always provides a way of escape from temptation. Don't walk alone: find believers who will encourage you, pray with you and gently restore you if you stumble.
lessons.reflect: What weights do you need to lay aside? Who can you ask to walk with you and hold you accountable?
lessons.declare: I keep my heart with all diligence and run my race with my eyes on Jesus.

vs.t: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
vs.e: And keep watch over your heart with all care; so you will have life.
vs.w: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

vs.t: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
vs.e: For this reason, as we are circled by so great a cloud of witnesses, putting off every weight, and the sin into which we come so readily, let us keep on running in the way which is marked out for us,
vs.w: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,

vs.t: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
vs.e: Having our eyes fixed on Jesus, the guide and end of our faith, who went through the pains of the cross, not caring for the shame, because of the joy which was before him, and who has now taken his place at the right hand of God's seat of power.
vs.w: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.

vs.t: Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.
vs.e: So let him who seems to himself to be safe go in fear of a fall.
vs.w: Therefore let him who thinks he stands be careful that he doesn’t fall.

vs.t: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.
vs.e: You have been put to no test but such as is common to man: and God is true, who will not let any test come on you which you are not able to undergo; but he will make with the test a way out of it, so that you may be able to go through it.
vs.w: No temptation has taken you except what is common to man. God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able, but will with the temptation also make the way of escape, that you may be able to endure it.

vs.t: Brethren, if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness; considering thyself, lest thou also be tempted.
vs.e: Brothers, if a man is taken in any wrongdoing, you who are of the Spirit will put such a one right in a spirit of love; keeping watch on yourself, for fear that you yourself may be tested.
vs.w: Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness; looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.

vs.t: Bear ye one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
vs.e: Take on yourselves one another's troubles, and so keep the law of Christ.
vs.w: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.

vs.t: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:
vs.e: And let us be moving one another at all times to love and good works;
vs.w: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,

vs.t: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
vs.e: Not giving up our meetings, as is the way of some, but keeping one another strong in faith; and all the more because you see the day coming near.
vs.w: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

lessons.memtext: Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.
lessons.memE: And keep watch over your heart with all care; so you will have life.
lessons.memW: Keep your heart with all diligence, for out of it is the wellspring of life.

lessons.title: Revival Starts with Me
lessons.sub: Humble yourself, pray and seek His face
lessons.question: What part do I play in revival?
ask: What four things does God ask His people to do in 2 Chronicles 7:14?
What happened to Isaiah when he saw the Lord?
What did Isaiah say when God asked, "Whom shall I send?"
lessons.note: God promised healing to His people when they humble themselves, pray, seek His face and turn from their wicked ways. Revival in a family, church or nation always starts in someone's heart. When Isaiah saw the Lord, he saw his own sin, was cleansed, and then said, "Here am I; send me." Let it start with you.
lessons.reflect: Who in your family or community will you pray for, and who will you tell about your return to God?
lessons.declare: Revival starts with me. I humble myself, pray, seek God's face and turn from my wicked ways.

vs.t: If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.
vs.e: If my people, on whom my name is named, make themselves low and come to me in prayer, searching for me and turning from their evil ways; then I will give ear from heaven, overlooking their sin, and will give life again to their land.
vs.w: if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then I will hear from heaven, will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.

vs.t: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
vs.e: In the year of King Uzziah's death I saw the Lord seated in his place, high and lifted up, and the Temple was full of the wide skirts of his robe.
vs.w: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.

vs.t: Above it stood the seraphims: each one had six wings; with twain he covered his face, and with twain he covered his feet, and with twain he did fly.
vs.e: Over him were the winged ones: every one had six wings; two for covering his face, two for covering his feed, and two for flight.
vs.w: Above him stood the seraphim. Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.

vs.t: And one cried unto another, and said, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of hosts: the whole earth is full of his glory.
vs.e: And one said in a loud voice to another, Holy, holy, holy, is the Lord of armies: all the earth is full of his glory.
vs.w: One called to another, and said, “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahweh of Armies! The whole earth is full of his glory!”

vs.t: And the posts of the door moved at the voice of him that cried, and the house was filled with smoke.
vs.e: And the bases of the door-pillars were shaking at the sound of his cry, and the house was full of smoke.
vs.w: The foundations of the thresholds shook at the voice of him who called, and the house was filled with smoke.

vs.t: Then said I, Woe is me! for I am undone; because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips: for mine eyes have seen the King, the Lord of hosts.
vs.e: Then I said, The curse is on me, and my fate is destruction; for I am a man of unclean lips, living among a people of unclean lips; for my eyes have seen the King, the Lord of armies.
vs.w: Then I said, “Woe is me! For I am undone, because I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell among a people of unclean lips: for my eyes have seen the King, Yahweh of Armies!”

vs.t: Then flew one of the seraphims unto me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar:
vs.e: Then a winged one came to me with a burning coal in his hand, which he had taken from off the altar with the fire-spoon.
vs.w: Then one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.

vs.t: And he laid it upon my mouth, and said, Lo, this hath touched thy lips; and thine iniquity is taken away, and thy sin purged.
vs.e: And after touching my mouth with it, he said, See, your lips have been touched with this; and your evil is taken away, and you are made clean from sin.
vs.w: He touched my mouth with it, and said, “Behold, this has touched your lips; and your iniquity is taken away, and your sin forgiven.”

vs.t: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
vs.e: And the voice of the Lord came to my ears, saying, Whom am I to send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I, send me.
vs.w: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”

vs.t: O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid: O Lord, revive thy work in the midst of the years, in the midst of the years make known; in wrath remember mercy.
vs.e: O Lord, word of you has come to my ears; I have seen your work, O Lord; when the years come near make it clear; in wrath keep mercy in mind.
vs.w: Yahweh, I have heard of your fame. I stand in awe of your deeds, Yahweh. Renew your work in the middle of the years. In the middle of the years make it known. In wrath, you remember mercy.
