title: New Life in Christ
intro: You have a new life in Christ. In these sessions, discover your new Hero, your new Boss, your new identity, food, breath, home, family and job. Each one ends with a step to obey and someone to share with.
credit: Topics and passages follow the New Life in Christ 3/3 sessions for new believers.

lessons.title: Your New Life in Christ
lessons.sub: Repent and believe the good news
lessons.question: How do our lives change when we choose Jesus?
ask: What do you learn about Jesus in this story?
What do you learn about people in this story?
How does Zacchaeus' life change?
lessons.note: Zacchaeus was rich, unpopular and probably lonely. Jesus stopped, called him by name and chose his house. Zacchaeus did not clean himself up first; meeting Jesus changed him, and the change showed straight away in how he treated people and money. Repentance is a U-turn: turning from sin and turning to Jesus. And God wants you to be sure: whoever has the Son has life.
lessons.reflect: Has there been a time when you turned from your sin and trusted in Jesus? If not, what is stopping you?
lessons.declare: Jesus came to seek and to save the lost. I have the Son, so I have life.

vs.t: And Jesus entered and passed through Jericho.
vs.e: And he went into Jericho, and when he was going through it,
vs.w: He entered and was passing through Jericho.

vs.t: And, behold, there was a man named Zaccheus, which was the chief among the publicans, and he was rich.
vs.e: A man, named Zacchaeus, who was the chief tax-farmer, and a man of wealth,
vs.w: There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector, and he was rich.

vs.t: And he sought to see Jesus who he was; and could not for the press, because he was little of stature.
vs.e: Made an attempt to get a view of Jesus, and was not able to do so, because of the people, for he was a small man.
vs.w: He was trying to see who Jesus was, and couldn’t because of the crowd, because he was short.

vs.t: And he ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him: for he was to pass that way.
vs.e: And he went quickly in front of them and got up into a tree to see him, for he was going that way.
vs.w: He ran on ahead, and climbed up into a sycamore tree to see him, for he was going to pass that way.

vs.t: And when Jesus came to the place, he looked up, and saw him, and said unto him, Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.
vs.e: And when Jesus came to the place, looking up, he said to him, Zacchaeus, be quick and come down, for I am coming to your house today.
vs.w: When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and saw him, and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for today I must stay at your house.”

vs.t: And he made haste, and came down, and received him joyfully.
vs.e: And he came down quickly, and took him into his house with joy.
vs.w: He hurried, came down, and received him joyfully.

vs.t: And when they saw it, they all murmured, saying, That he was gone to be guest with a man that is a sinner.
vs.e: And when they saw it, they were all angry, saying, He has gone into the house of a sinner.
vs.w: When they saw it, they all murmured, saying, “He has gone in to lodge with a man who is a sinner.”

vs.t: And Zaccheus stood, and said unto the Lord; Behold, Lord, the half of my goods I give to the poor; and if I have taken any thing from any man by false accusation, I restore him fourfold.
vs.e: And Zacchaeus, waiting before him, said to the Lord, See, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor, and if I have taken anything from anyone wrongly, I give him back four times as much.
vs.w: Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Behold, Lord, half of my goods I give to the poor. If I have wrongfully exacted anything of anyone, I restore four times as much.”

vs.t: And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house, forsomuch as he also is a son of Abraham.
vs.e: And Jesus said to him, Today salvation has come to this house, for even he is a son of Abraham.
vs.w: Jesus said to him, “Today, salvation has come to this house, because he also is a son of Abraham.

vs.t: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.
vs.e: For the Son of man came to make search for those who are wandering from the way, and to be their Saviour.
vs.w: For the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost.”

vs.t: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
vs.e: And Peter said, Let your hearts be changed, every one of you, and have baptism in the name of Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of your sins; and you will have the Holy Spirit given to you.
vs.w: Peter said to them, “Repent, and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

vs.t: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
vs.e: He who has the Son has the life; he who has not the Son of God has not the life.
vs.w: He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.

vs.t: These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.
vs.e: I have put these things in writing for you who have faith in the name of the Son of God, so that you may be certain that you have eternal life.
vs.w: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.

lessons.memtext: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
lessons.memE: If we say openly that we have done wrong, he is upright and true to his word, giving us forgiveness of sins and making us clean from all evil.
lessons.memW: If we confess our sins, he is faithful and righteous to forgive us the sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.

lessons.title: Your New Hero
lessons.sub: The great cost of Jesus' love
lessons.question: What did it cost Jesus to live and die for us?
ask: Is there anything in this passage that surprises or shocks you?
What do you learn about Jesus here?
What is the main point?
lessons.note: Isaiah wrote about Jesus about 700 years before He was born: despised, rejected, wounded for our transgressions. Philippians shows how far He came down, from equality with God to a servant, to death on a cross. There is no greater love than laying down your life for a friend, and that is exactly what your Hero did for you.
lessons.reflect: What is God leading you to do in response to the love of Jesus?
lessons.declare: He was wounded for my transgressions. Jesus laid down His life for me.

vs.t: He is despised and rejected of men; a man of sorrows, and acquainted with grief: and we hid as it were our faces from him; he was despised, and we esteemed him not.
vs.e: Men made sport of him, turning away from him; he was a man of sorrows, marked by disease; and like one from whom men's faces are turned away, he was looked down on, and we put no value on him.
vs.w: He was despised and rejected by men, a man of suffering and acquainted with disease. He was despised as one from whom men hide their face; and we didn’t respect him.

vs.t: Surely he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows: yet we did esteem him stricken, smitten of God, and afflicted.
vs.e: But it was our pain he took, and our diseases were put on him: while to us he seemed as one diseased, on whom God's punishment had come.
vs.w: Surely he has borne our sickness and carried our suffering; yet we considered him plagued, struck by God, and afflicted.

vs.t: But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed.
vs.e: But it was for our sins he was wounded, and for our evil doings he was crushed: he took the punishment by which we have peace, and by his wounds we are made well.
vs.w: But he was pierced for our transgressions. He was crushed for our iniquities. The punishment that brought our peace was on him; and by his wounds we are healed.

vs.t: All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord hath laid on him the iniquity of us all.
vs.e: We all went wandering like sheep; going every one of us after his desire; and the Lord put on him the punishment of us all.
vs.w: All we like sheep have gone astray. Everyone has turned to his own way; and Yahweh has laid on him the iniquity of us all.

vs.t: He was oppressed, and he was afflicted, yet he opened not his mouth: he is brought as a lamb to the slaughter, and as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
vs.e: Men were cruel to him, but he was gentle and quiet; as a lamb taken to its death, and as a sheep before those who take her wool makes no sound, so he said not a word.
vs.w: He was oppressed, yet when he was afflicted he didn’t open his mouth. As a lamb that is led to the slaughter, and as a sheep that before its shearers is silent, so he didn’t open his mouth.

vs.t: Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ Jesus:
vs.e: Let this mind be in you which was in Christ Jesus,
vs.w: Have this in your mind, which was also in Christ Jesus,

vs.t: Who, being in the form of God, thought it not robbery to be equal with God:
vs.e: To whom, though himself in the form of God, it did not seem that to take for oneself was to be like God;
vs.w: who, existing in the form of God, didn’t consider equality with God a thing to be grasped,

vs.t: But made himself of no reputation, and took upon him the form of a servant, and was made in the likeness of men:
vs.e: But he made himself as nothing, taking the form of a servant, being made like men;
vs.w: but emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of men.

vs.t: And being found in fashion as a man, he humbled himself, and became obedient unto death, even the death of the cross.
vs.e: And being seen in form as a man, he took the lowest place, and let himself be put to death, even the death of the cross.
vs.w: And being found in human form, he humbled himself, becoming obedient to the point of death, yes, the death of the cross.

vs.t: This is my commandment, That ye love one another, as I have loved you.
vs.e: This is the law I give you: Have love one for another, even as I have love for you.
vs.w: “This is my commandment, that you love one another, even as I have loved you.

vs.t: Greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
vs.e: Greater love has no man than this, that a man gives up his life for his friends.
vs.w: Greater love has no one than this, that someone lay down his life for his friends.

lessons.memtext: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
lessons.memE: So if any man is in Christ, he is in a new world: the old things have come to an end; they have truly become new.
lessons.memW: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

lessons.title: Your New Boss
lessons.question: What does it cost us to follow Jesus?
ask: What did following Jesus cost the fishermen?
What does Jesus say about counting the cost?
What does it look like to walk as He walked?
lessons.note: Peter, Andrew, James and John left their nets straight away. Jesus is honest: following Him costs something, so count the cost like a builder before he starts a tower. A disciple puts Jesus first, above everything. But what we give up is small compared to what we gain: Christ living in us.
lessons.reflect: What might following Jesus cost you? Is there anything you are still holding on to?
lessons.declare: I am crucified with Christ. Jesus is my Lord, and I will follow Him.

vs.t: And Jesus, walking by the sea of Galilee, saw two brethren, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
vs.e: And when he was walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, whose other name was Peter, and Andrew, his brother, who were putting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
vs.w: Walking by the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.

vs.t: And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
vs.e: And he said to them, Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men.
vs.w: He said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers for men.”

vs.t: And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.
vs.e: And straight away they let go the nets and went after him.
vs.w: They immediately left their nets and followed him.

vs.t: And going on from thence, he saw other two brethren, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in a ship with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
vs.e: And going on from there he saw two other brothers, James, the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, in the boat with their father, stitching up their nets; and he said, Come.
vs.w: Going on from there, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.

vs.t: And they immediately left the ship and their father, and followed him.
vs.e: And they went straight from the boat and their father and came after him.
vs.w: They immediately left the boat and their father, and followed him.

vs.t: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,
vs.e: Now a great number of people went with him.
vs.w: Now great multitudes were going with him. He turned and said to them,

vs.t: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.
vs.e: And turning round, he said to them, If any man comes to me, and has not hate for his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters, and even for his life, he may not be my disciple.
vs.w: “If anyone comes to me, and doesn’t disregard his own father, mother, wife, children, brothers, and sisters, yes, and his own life also, he can’t be my disciple.

vs.t: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.
vs.e: Whoever does not take up his cross and come after me may not be my disciple.
vs.w: Whoever doesn’t bear his own cross, and come after me, can’t be my disciple.

vs.t: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
vs.e: For which of you, desiring to put up a tower, does not first give much thought to the price, if he will have enough to make it complete?
vs.w: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?

vs.t: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,
vs.e: For fear that if he makes a start and is not able to go on with it to the end, all who see it will be laughing at him,
vs.w: Or perhaps, when he has laid a foundation, and is not able to finish, everyone who sees begins to mock him,

vs.t: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.
vs.e: And saying, This man made a start at building and is not able to make it complete.
vs.w: saying, ‘This man began to build, and wasn’t able to finish.’

vs.t: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.
vs.e: And so whoever is not ready to give up all he has may not be my disciple.
vs.w: So therefore whoever of you who doesn’t renounce all that he has, he can’t be my disciple.

vs.t: But whoso keepeth his word, in him verily is the love of God perfected: hereby know we that we are in him.
vs.e: But in every man who keeps his word, the love of God is made complete. By this we may be certain that we are in him:
vs.w: But God’s love has most certainly been perfected in whoever keeps his word. This is how we know that we are in him:

vs.t: He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.
vs.e: He who says that he is living in him, will do as he did.
vs.w: he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.

lessons.memtext: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.
lessons.memE: I have been put to death on the cross with Christ; still I am living; no longer I, but Christ is living in me; and that life which I now am living in the flesh I am living by faith, the faith of the Son of God, who in love for me, gave himself up for me.
lessons.memW: I have been crucified with Christ, and it is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me. That life which I now live in the flesh, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself up for me.

lessons.title: Your New Identity
lessons.question: What is baptism and why should we do it?
ask: What did Jesus command about baptism?
What did Peter tell the people to do?
What does baptism picture in Romans 6?
lessons.note: Baptism is not what saves us; Jesus does. But Jesus commanded it, and the first believers obeyed straight away. Going under the water pictures being buried with Christ, and coming up pictures rising to walk in a new life. It is a public way of saying: I belong to Jesus now.
lessons.reflect: Have you been baptised since you believed? If not, what is your next step?
lessons.declare: I am buried with Christ and raised to walk in newness of life. I will obey Him in baptism.

vs.t: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
vs.e: And Jesus came to them and said, All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
vs.w: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.

vs.t: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
vs.e: Go then, and make disciples of all the nations, giving them baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit:
vs.w: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

vs.t: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
vs.e: Teaching them to keep all the rules which I have given you: and see, I am ever with you, even to the end of the world.
vs.w: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

vs.t: Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ.
vs.e: For this reason, let all Israel be certain that this Jesus, whom you put to death on the cross, God has made Lord and Christ.
vs.w: “Let all the house of Israel therefore know certainly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified.”

vs.t: Now when they heard this, they were pricked in their heart, and said unto Peter and to the rest of the apostles, Men and brethren, what shall we do?
vs.e: Now when these words came to their ears their hearts were troubled, and they said to Peter and the other Apostles, Brothers, what are we to do?
vs.w: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Brothers, what shall we do?”

vs.t: Then Peter said unto them, Repent, and be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and ye shall receive the gift of the Holy Ghost.
vs.e: And Peter said, Let your hearts be changed, every one of you, and have baptism in the name of Jesus Christ, for the forgiveness of your sins; and you will have the Holy Spirit given to you.
vs.w: Peter said to them, “Repent, and be baptized, every one of you, in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of sins, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.

vs.t: Know ye not, that so many of us as were baptized into Jesus Christ were baptized into his death?
vs.e: Or are you without the knowledge that all we who had baptism into Christ Jesus, had baptism into his death?
vs.w: Or don’t you know that all we who were baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death?

vs.t: Therefore we are buried with him by baptism into death: that like as Christ was raised up from the dead by the glory of the Father, even so we also should walk in newness of life.
vs.e: We have been placed with him among the dead through baptism into death: so that as Christ came again from the dead by the glory of the Father, we, in the same way, might be living in new life.
vs.w: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

vs.t: For if we have been planted together in the likeness of his death, we shall be also in the likeness of his resurrection:
vs.e: For, if we have been made like him in his death, we will, in the same way, be like him in his coming to life again;
vs.w: For if we have become united with him in the likeness of his death, we will also be part of his resurrection;

lessons.title: Your New Food
lessons.sub: The Word of God feeds your soul
lessons.question: How does God speak to us through the Bible?
ask: What do these verses say the Bible is?
What does the Bible do in our lives?
How should we treat God's Word?
lessons.note: All Scripture is "God-breathed". Just as your body needs bread, your new life needs every word from the mouth of God. The Word teaches, corrects and trains us, lights our path and reaches deep into the heart. Read it daily, think about it, and do what it says.
lessons.reflect: What time each day will you set aside to read God's Word?
lessons.declare: I live by every word of God. His Word is a lamp to my feet.

vs.t: And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.
vs.e: And that from the time when you were a child, you have had knowledge of the holy Writings, which are able to make you wise to salvation, through faith in Christ Jesus.
vs.w: From infancy, you have known the holy Scriptures which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith, which is in Christ Jesus.

vs.t: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
vs.e: Every holy Writing which comes from God is of profit for teaching, for training, for guiding, for education in righteousness:
vs.w: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,

vs.t: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
vs.e: So that the man of God may be complete, trained and made ready for every good work.
vs.w: that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.

vs.t: This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night, that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.
vs.e: Let this book of the law be ever on your lips and in your thoughts day and night, so that you may keep with care everything in it; then a blessing will be on all your way, and you will do well.
vs.w: This book of the law shall not depart from your mouth, but you shall meditate on it day and night, that you may observe to do according to all that is written in it; for then you shall make your way prosperous, and then you shall have good success.

vs.t: But he answered and said, It is written, Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceedeth out of the mouth of God.
vs.e: But he made answer and said, It is in the Writings, Bread is not man's only need, but every word which comes out of the mouth of God.
vs.w: But he answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds out of God’s mouth.’ ”

vs.t: ב BETH. Wherewithal shall a young man cleanse his way? by taking heed thereto according to thy word.
vs.e: How may a young man make his way clean? by guiding it after your word.
vs.w: How can a young man keep his way pure? By living according to your word.

vs.t: With my whole heart have I sought thee: O let me not wander from thy commandments.
vs.e: I have made search for you with all my heart: O let me not go wandering far from your teaching.
vs.w: With my whole heart, I have sought you. Don’t let me wander from your commandments.

vs.t: Thy word have I hid in mine heart, that I might not sin against thee.
vs.e: I have kept your sayings secretly in my heart, so that I might do no sin against you.
vs.w: I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.

vs.t: נ NUN. Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.
vs.e: Your word is a light for my feet, ever shining on my way.
vs.w: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light for my path.

vs.t: For the word of God is quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword, piercing even to the dividing asunder of soul and spirit, and of the joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.
vs.e: For the word of God is living and full of power, and is sharper than any two-edged sword, cutting through and making a division even of the soul and the spirit, the bones and the muscles, and quick to see the thoughts and purposes of the heart.
vs.w: For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of both joints and marrow, and is able to discern the thoughts and intentions of the heart.

lessons.memE: I have kept your sayings secretly in my heart, so that I might do no sin against you.
lessons.memW: I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you.

lessons.title: Your New Breath
lessons.sub: Prayer: a direct line to God
lessons.question: How can we talk to God?
ask: What does Jesus say about how NOT to pray?
What does the Lord's Prayer teach you about talking to God?
What does God promise when we pray instead of worrying?
lessons.note: Prayer is to your spiritual life what breathing is to your body. Jesus says it is not about long or impressive words but about talking honestly with your Father, in secret. The Lord's Prayer gives a pattern: worship, His kingdom, daily needs, forgiveness and protection. Bring everything to Him, and His peace will guard your heart.
lessons.reflect: What worry can you turn into a prayer right now?
lessons.declare: I am careful for nothing. I bring everything to my Father in prayer, and His peace guards my heart.

vs.t: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
vs.e: And when you make your prayers, be not like the false-hearted men, who take pleasure in getting up and saying their prayers in the Synagogues and at the street turnings so that they may be seen by men. Truly I say to you, They have their reward.
vs.w: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.

vs.t: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
vs.e: But when you make your prayer, go into your private room, and, shutting the door, say a prayer to your Father in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will give you your reward.
vs.w: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

vs.t: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
vs.e: And in your prayer do not make use of the same words again and again, as the Gentiles do: for they have the idea that God will give attention to them because of the number of their words.
vs.w: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.

vs.t: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
vs.e: So be not like them; because your Father has knowledge of your needs even before you make your requests to him.
vs.w: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.

vs.t: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
vs.e: Let this then be your prayer: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
vs.w: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.

vs.t: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
vs.e: Let your kingdom come. Let your pleasure be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
vs.w: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

vs.t: Give us this day our daily bread.
vs.e: Give us this day bread for our needs.
vs.w: Give us today our daily bread.

vs.t: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
vs.e: And make us free of our debts, as we have made those free who are in debt to us.
vs.w: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

vs.t: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
vs.e: And let us not be put to the test, but keep us safe from the Evil One.
vs.w: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

vs.t: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
vs.e: For if you let men have forgiveness for their sins, you will have forgiveness from your Father in heaven.
vs.w: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

vs.t: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
vs.e: But if you do not let men have forgiveness for their sins, you will not have forgiveness from your Father for your sins.
vs.w: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

vs.t: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
vs.e: Have no cares; but in everything with prayer and praise put your requests before God.
vs.w: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

vs.t: And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
vs.e: And the peace of God, which is deeper than all knowledge, will keep your hearts and minds in Christ Jesus.
vs.w: And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus.

lessons.memtext: Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.
lessons.memE: Have no cares; but in everything with prayer and praise put your requests before God.
lessons.memW: In nothing be anxious, but in everything, by prayer and petition with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known to God.

lessons.title: Your New Power
lessons.sub: The role of the Holy Spirit in our lives
lessons.question: How does God empower those who follow Jesus?
ask: What truths do you learn from these passages?
What role does the Holy Spirit play in our lives?
How will your life change based on what you are learning?
lessons.note: These words in John were spoken the night before Jesus died. His followers had been with Him almost every day for three years, and He told them He would soon leave. But He promised not to leave them as orphans: He would send the Holy Spirit, the Comforter. The Spirit lives in every believer. He teaches us and reminds us of Jesus' words, convicts the world of sin, gives us power to be witnesses, and even prays for us when we don't know what to pray.
lessons.reflect: Is there something God expects of you this week, in the power of His Spirit?
lessons.declare: I am not alone. The Holy Spirit lives in me, teaches me, prays for me and gives me power to be a witness.
lessons.tellnote: Practise a "gospel bridge": a natural way to turn an ordinary conversation toward Jesus. Pair up with a friend and try it.

vs.t: If ye love me, keep my commandments.
vs.e: If you have love for me, you will keep my laws.
vs.w: If you love me, keep my commandments.

vs.t: And I will pray the Father, and he shall give you another Comforter, that he may abide with you for ever;
vs.e: And I will make prayer to the Father and he will give you another Helper to be with you for ever,
vs.w: I will pray to the Father, and he will give you another Counselor, that he may be with you forever:

vs.t: Even the Spirit of truth; whom the world cannot receive, because it seeth him not, neither knoweth him: but ye know him; for he dwelleth with you, and shall be in you.
vs.e: Even the Spirit of true knowledge. That Spirit the world is not able to take to its heart because it sees him not and has no knowledge of him: but you have knowledge of him, because he is ever with you and will be in you.
vs.w: the Spirit of truth, whom the world can’t receive; for it doesn’t see him and doesn’t know him. You know him, for he lives with you, and will be in you.

vs.t: I will not leave you comfortless: I will come to you.
vs.e: I will not let you be without a friend: I am coming to you.
vs.w: I will not leave you orphans. I will come to you.

vs.t: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
vs.e: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will be your teacher in all things and will put you in mind of everything I have said to you.
vs.w: But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.

vs.t: Nevertheless I tell you the truth; It is expedient for you that I go away: for if I go not away, the Comforter will not come unto you; but if I depart, I will send him unto you.
vs.e: But what I am saying is true: my going is for your good: for if I do not go away, the Helper will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you.
vs.w: Nevertheless I tell you the truth: It is to your advantage that I go away, for if I don’t go away, the Counselor won’t come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you.

vs.t: And when he is come, he will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment:
vs.e: And he, when he comes, will make the world conscious of sin, and of righteousness, and of being judged:
vs.w: When he has come, he will convict the world about sin, about righteousness, and about judgment;

vs.t: Of sin, because they believe not on me;
vs.e: Of sin, because they have not faith in me;
vs.w: about sin, because they don’t believe in me;

vs.t: But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth.
vs.e: But you will have power, when the Holy Spirit has come on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and all Judaea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
vs.w: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

vs.t: Likewise the Spirit also helpeth our infirmities: for we know not what we should pray for as we ought: but the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered.
vs.e: And in the same way the Spirit is a help to our feeble hearts: for we are not able to make prayer to God in the right way; but the Spirit puts our desires into words which are not in our power to say;
vs.w: In the same way, the Spirit also helps our weaknesses, for we don’t know how to pray as we ought. But the Spirit himself makes intercession for us with groanings which can’t be uttered.

vs.t: And he that searcheth the hearts knoweth what is the mind of the Spirit, because he maketh intercession for the saints according to the will of God.
vs.e: And he who is the searcher of hearts has knowledge of the mind of the Spirit, because he is making prayers for the saints in agreement with the mind of God.
vs.w: He who searches the hearts knows what is on the Spirit’s mind, because he makes intercession for the saints according to God.

lessons.memtext: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
lessons.memE: So if any man is in Christ, he is in a new world: the old things have come to an end; they have truly become new.
lessons.memW: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

vs.t: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.
vs.e: And when the day of Pentecost was come, they were all together in one place.
vs.w: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.

vs.t: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
vs.e: And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like the rushing of a violent wind, and all the house where they were was full of it.
vs.w: Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

vs.t: And there appeared unto them cloven tongues like as of fire, and it sat upon each of them.
vs.e: And they saw tongues, like flames of fire, coming to rest on every one of them.
vs.w: Tongues like fire appeared and were distributed to them, and one sat on each of them.

vs.t: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance.
vs.e: And they were all full of the Holy Spirit, and were talking in different languages, as the Spirit gave them power.
vs.w: They were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak with other languages, as the Spirit gave them the ability to speak.

lessons.title: Your New Home
lessons.question: How do we stay connected to Jesus?
ask: What do you learn about Jesus and the Father here?
What do you learn about the people of God?
What happens when a branch stays in the vine?
lessons.note: A branch does not strain to produce fruit; it simply stays joined to the vine. Abide (meno) means remain, stay, make your home. Jesus is your home now. Through Him you have access to the Father, and you are no longer a stranger but part of God's household.
lessons.reflect: What helps you stay connected to Jesus through the day? What pulls you away?
lessons.declare: I abide in Jesus and He abides in me. I am part of God's household.

vs.t: I am the true vine, and my Father is the husbandman.
vs.e: I am the true vine and my Father is the gardener.
vs.w: “I am the true vine, and my Father is the farmer.

vs.t: Every branch in me that beareth not fruit he taketh away: and every branch that beareth fruit, he purgeth it, that it may bring forth more fruit.
vs.e: He takes away every branch in me which has no fruit, and every branch which has fruit he makes clean, so that it may have more fruit.
vs.w: Every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit, he takes away. Every branch that bears fruit, he prunes, that it may bear more fruit.

vs.t: Now ye are clean through the word which I have spoken unto you.
vs.e: You are clean, even now, through the teaching which I have given you.
vs.w: You are already pruned clean because of the word which I have spoken to you.

vs.t: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
vs.e: Be in me at all times as I am in you. As the branch is not able to give fruit of itself, if it is not still on the vine, so you are not able to do so if you are not in me.
vs.w: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.

vs.t: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
vs.e: I am the vine, you are the branches: he who is in me at all times as I am in him, gives much fruit, because without me you are able to do nothing.
vs.w: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

vs.t: If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch, and is withered; and men gather them, and cast them into the fire, and they are burned.
vs.e: If a man does not keep himself in me, he becomes dead and is cut off like a dry branch; such branches are taken up and put in the fire and burned.
vs.w: If a man doesn’t remain in me, he is thrown out as a branch and is withered; and they gather them, throw them into the fire, and they are burned.

vs.t: If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall ask what ye will, and it shall be done unto you.
vs.e: If you are in me at all times, and my words are in you, then anything for which you make a request will be done for you.
vs.w: If you remain in me, and my words remain in you, you will ask whatever you desire, and it will be done for you.

vs.t: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
vs.e: Here is my Father's glory, in that you give much fruit and so are my true disciples.
vs.w: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.

vs.t: As the Father hath loved me, so have I loved you: continue ye in my love.
vs.e: Even as the Father has given me his love, so I have given my love to you: be ever in my love.
vs.w: Even as the Father has loved me, I also have loved you. Remain in my love.

vs.t: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.
vs.e: If you keep my laws, you will be ever in my love, even as I have kept my Father's laws, and am ever in his love.
vs.w: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and remain in his love.

vs.t: For he is our peace, who hath made both one, and hath broken down the middle wall of partition between us;
vs.e: For he is our peace, who has made the two into one, and by whom the middle wall of division has been broken down,
vs.w: For he is our peace, who made both one, and broke down the middle wall of separation,

vs.t: For through him we both have access by one Spirit unto the Father.
vs.e: Because through him the two of us are able to come near in one Spirit to the Father.
vs.w: For through him we both have our access in one Spirit to the Father.

vs.t: Now therefore ye are no more strangers and foreigners, but fellowcitizens with the saints, and of the household of God;
vs.e: So then you are no longer as those who have no part or place in the kingdom of God, but you are numbered among the saints, and of the family of God,
vs.w: So then you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but you are fellow citizens with the saints and of the household of God,

lessons.title: Your New Family
lessons.question: How do we relate to one another in God's family?
ask: What did the first believers do together?
How should we treat one another?
Why should we not stop meeting together?
lessons.note: When you were born again, you were born into a family. The first church devoted themselves to teaching, fellowship (koinonia: sharing life), breaking bread and prayer. They shared what they had, met daily and praised God. Look out for each other, encourage one another and keep meeting together.
lessons.reflect: Who is your church family? How can you encourage one of them this week?
lessons.declare: I belong to God's family. I will love, encourage and meet with my brothers and sisters.

vs.t: And they continued stedfastly in the apostles’ doctrine and fellowship, and in breaking of bread, and in prayers.
vs.e: And they kept their attention fixed on the Apostles' teaching and were united together in the taking of broken bread and in prayer.
vs.w: They continued steadfastly in the apostles’ teaching and fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and prayer.

vs.t: And fear came upon every soul: and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles.
vs.e: But fear came on every soul: and all sorts of wonders and signs were done by the Apostles.
vs.w: Fear came on every soul, and many wonders and signs were done through the apostles.

vs.t: And all that believed were together, and had all things common;
vs.e: And all those who were of the faith kept together, and had all things in common;
vs.w: All who believed were together, and had all things in common.

vs.t: And sold their possessions and goods, and parted them to all men, as every man had need.
vs.e: And exchanging their goods and property for money, they made division of it among them all, as they had need.
vs.w: They sold their possessions and goods, and distributed them to all, according as anyone had need.

vs.t: And they, continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, did eat their meat with gladness and singleness of heart,
vs.e: And day by day, going in agreement together regularly to the Temple and, taking broken bread together in their houses, they took their food with joy and with true hearts,
vs.w: Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart,

vs.t: Praising God, and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added to the church daily such as should be saved.
vs.e: Giving praise to God, and having the approval of all the people; and every day the number of those who had salvation was increased by the Lord.
vs.w: praising God, and having favor with all the people. The Lord added to the assembly day by day those who were being saved.

vs.t: If there be therefore any consolation in Christ, if any comfort of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any bowels and mercies,
vs.e: If then there is any comfort in Christ, any help given by love, any uniting of hearts in the Spirit, any loving mercies and pity,
vs.w: If therefore there is any exhortation in Christ, if any consolation of love, if any fellowship of the Spirit, if any tender mercies and compassion,

vs.t: Fulfil ye my joy, that ye be likeminded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind.
vs.e: Make my joy complete by being of the same mind, having the same love, being in harmony and of one mind;
vs.w: make my joy full by being like-minded, having the same love, being of one accord, of one mind;

vs.t: Let nothing be done through strife or vainglory; but in lowliness of mind let each esteem other better than themselves.
vs.e: Doing nothing through envy or through pride, but with low thoughts of self let everyone take others to be better than himself;
vs.w: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;

vs.t: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
vs.e: Not looking everyone to his private good, but keeping in mind the things of others.
vs.w: each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.

vs.t: And let us consider one another to provoke unto love and to good works:
vs.e: And let us be moving one another at all times to love and good works;
vs.w: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,

vs.t: Not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as the manner of some is; but exhorting one another: and so much the more, as ye see the day approaching.
vs.e: Not giving up our meetings, as is the way of some, but keeping one another strong in faith; and all the more because you see the day coming near.
vs.w: not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

vs.t: Seeing ye have purified your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit unto unfeigned love of the brethren, see that ye love one another with a pure heart fervently:
vs.e: And as you have made your souls clean, being ruled by what is true, and loving one another without deceit, see that your love is warm and from the heart:
vs.w: Seeing you have purified your souls in your obedience to the truth through the Spirit in sincere brotherly affection, love one another from the heart fervently,

lessons.title: Your New Job
lessons.sub: Share the gospel and make disciples
lessons.question: What is God's heart for the nations?
ask: What do you learn about Jesus from how He treated the Samaritan woman?
What did the woman do after meeting Jesus?
How should we share our faith?
lessons.note: Jesus crossed every barrier of race, gender and reputation to reach one woman at a well. She went straight back to her town saying "Come, see a man", and many believed because of her story. Your new job is the same: share what Jesus has done, with grace and respect, and help others follow Him.
lessons.reflect: Who are three people you will pray for and share Jesus with?
lessons.declare: I will share the good news of Jesus and make disciples, always ready to give an answer for my hope.

vs.t: And he must needs go through Samaria.
vs.e: And it was necessary for him to go through Samaria.
vs.w: He needed to pass through Samaria.

vs.t: Then cometh he to a city of Samaria, which is called Sychar, near to the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
vs.e: So he came to a town of Samaria which was named Sychar, near to the bit of land which Jacob gave to his son Joseph:
vs.w: So he came to a city of Samaria, called Sychar, near the parcel of ground that Jacob gave to his son, Joseph.

vs.t: Now Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being wearied with his journey, sat thus on the well: and it was about the sixth hour.
vs.e: Now Jacob's fountain was there. Jesus, being tired after his journey, was resting by the fountain. It was about the sixth hour.
vs.w: Jacob’s well was there. Jesus therefore, being tired from his journey, sat down by the well. It was about the sixth hour.

vs.t: There cometh a woman of Samaria to draw water: Jesus saith unto her, Give me to drink.
vs.e: A woman of Samaria came to get water, and Jesus said to her, Give me some water.
vs.w: A woman of Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, “Give me a drink.”

vs.t: (For his disciples were gone away unto the city to buy meat.)
vs.e: For his disciples had gone to the town to get food.
vs.w: For his disciples had gone away into the city to buy food.

vs.t: Then saith the woman of Samaria unto him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, which am a woman of Samaria? for the Jews have no dealings with the Samaritans.
vs.e: The woman of Samaria said to him, Why do you, a Jew, make a request for water to me, a woman of Samaria? She said this because Jews have nothing to do with the people of Samaria.
vs.w: The Samaritan woman therefore said to him, “How is it that you, being a Jew, ask for a drink from me, a Samaritan woman?” (For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans.)

vs.t: Jesus answered and said unto her, If thou knewest the gift of God, and who it is that saith to thee, Give me to drink; thou wouldest have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
vs.e: In answer Jesus said, If you had knowledge of what God gives freely and who it is who says to you, Give me water, you would make your prayer to him, and he would give you living water.
vs.w: Jesus answered her, “If you knew the gift of God, and who it is who says to you, ‘Give me a drink,’ you would have asked him, and he would have given you living water.”

vs.t: The woman saith unto him, I know that Messias cometh, which is called Christ: when he is come, he will tell us all things.
vs.e: The woman said to him, I am certain that the Messiah, who is named Christ, is coming; when he comes he will make all things clear to us.
vs.w: The woman said to him, “I know that Messiah comes, he who is called Christ. When he has come, he will declare to us all things.”

vs.t: Jesus saith unto her, I that speak unto thee am he.
vs.e: Jesus said to her, I, who am talking to you, am he.
vs.w: Jesus said to her, “I am he, the one who speaks to you.”

vs.t: And upon this came his disciples, and marvelled that he talked with the woman: yet no man said, What seekest thou? or, Why talkest thou with her?
vs.e: At that point the disciples came back, and they were surprised to see him talking to a woman; but not one of them said to him, What is your purpose? or, Why are you talking to her?
vs.w: At this, his disciples came. They marveled that he was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, “What are you looking for?” or, “Why do you speak with her?”

vs.t: The woman then left her waterpot, and went her way into the city, and saith to the men,
vs.e: Then the woman put down her water-pot and went into the town, and said to the people,
vs.w: So the woman left her water pot, went away into the city, and said to the people,

vs.t: Come, see a man, which told me all things that ever I did: is not this the Christ?
vs.e: Come and see a man who has been talking to me of everything I ever did! Is it possible that this is the Christ?
vs.w: “Come, see a man who told me everything that I did. Can this be the Christ?”

vs.t: Then they went out of the city, and came unto him.
vs.e: So they went out of the town and came to him.
vs.w: They went out of the city, and were coming to him.

vs.t: And many of the Samaritans of that city believed on him for the saying of the woman, which testified, He told me all that ever I did.
vs.e: Now a number of the people of that town had faith in him because of the woman's witness: He has been talking to me of everything I ever did.
vs.w: From that city many of the Samaritans believed in him because of the word of the woman, who testified, “He told me everything that I did.”

vs.t: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
vs.e: Go then, and make disciples of all the nations, giving them baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit:
vs.w: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

vs.t: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
vs.e: Teaching them to keep all the rules which I have given you: and see, I am ever with you, even to the end of the world.
vs.w: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

vs.t: Walk in wisdom toward them that are without, redeeming the time.
vs.e: Be wise in your behaviour to those who are outside, making good use of the time.
vs.w: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time.

vs.t: Let your speech be alway with grace, seasoned with salt, that ye may know how ye ought to answer every man.
vs.e: Let your talk be with grace, mixed with salt, so that you may be able to give an answer to everyone.
vs.w: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.

vs.t: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts: and be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear:
vs.e: But give honour to Christ in your hearts as your Lord; and be ready at any time when you are questioned about the hope which is in you, to give an answer in the fear of the Lord and without pride;
vs.w: But sanctify the Lord God in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to everyone who asks you a reason concerning the hope that is in you, with humility and fear,

vs.t: Having a good conscience; that, whereas they speak evil of you, as of evildoers, they may be ashamed that falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ.
vs.e: Being conscious that you have done no wrong; so that those who say evil things about your good way of life as Christians may be put to shame.
vs.w: having a good conscience. Thus, while you are spoken against as evildoers, they may be disappointed who curse your good way of life in Christ.

title: Who God Is to Me
intro: God is not distant. He is your Saviour, your loving Father, your King, your Lord, your Sender and your Teacher. Discover what each one means for your life, and learn to pass it on by training someone else.
credit: Sessions follow the Training Faithful Trainers (TFT) series.

lessons.title: Passing the Baton
lessons.question: What would our nation be like if everyone loved and obeyed God?
ask: What are the three great commands of Jesus?
What does each part of Matthew 28:18-20 ask of us?
Who did the man in Mark 5 and the jailer in Acts 16 reach first?
lessons.note: Jesus gave three great commands: love God, love people, and make disciples. A disciple is an apprentice who follows the Master and fishes for people, so every disciple is a disciple-maker. Like a relay runner passing the baton, we pass on what we received to faithful people who will teach others also. Start with those closest to you: Noah, Rahab, the healed man in Mark 5, Cornelius, Lydia and the Philippian jailer all saw their households reached. The fields are ripe; people just need to hear.
lessons.reflect: Who in your family most needs to hear the good news?
lessons.declare: I will pass on what I have received to faithful people who will teach others also.

vs.t: Jesus said unto him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
vs.e: And he said to him, Have love for the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind.
vs.w: Jesus said to him, “ ‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your mind.’

vs.t: This is the first and great commandment.
vs.e: This is the first and greatest rule.
vs.w: This is the first and great commandment.

vs.t: And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
vs.e: And a second like it is this, Have love for your neighbour as for yourself.
vs.w: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’

vs.t: And Jesus came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.
vs.e: And Jesus came to them and said, All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.
vs.w: Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to me in heaven and on earth.

vs.t: Go ye therefore, and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost:
vs.e: Go then, and make disciples of all the nations, giving them baptism in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit:
vs.w: Go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

vs.t: Teaching them to observe all things whatsoever I have commanded you: and, lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world. Amen.
vs.e: Teaching them to keep all the rules which I have given you: and see, I am ever with you, even to the end of the world.
vs.w: teaching them to observe all things that I commanded you. Behold, I am with you always, even to the end of the age.” Amen.

vs.t: And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
vs.e: And the things which I have said to you before a number of witnesses, give to those of the faith, so that they may be teachers of others.
vs.w: The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

vs.t: Say not ye, There are yet four months, and then cometh harvest? behold, I say unto you, Lift up your eyes, and look on the fields; for they are white already to harvest.
vs.e: You would say, Four months from now is the time of the grain-cutting. Take a look, I say to you, at the fields; they are even now white for cutting.
vs.w: Don’t you say, ‘There are yet four months until the harvest?’ Behold, I tell you, lift up your eyes and look at the fields, that they are white for harvest already.

vs.t: And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.
vs.e: And when he was getting into the boat, the man in whom had been the evil spirits had a great desire to come with him.
vs.w: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.

vs.t: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
vs.e: And he would not let him, but said to him, Go to your house, to your friends, and give them news of the great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.
vs.w: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”

vs.t: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.
vs.e: And he went on his way, and made public in the country of Decapolis what great things Jesus had done for him: and all men were full of wonder.
vs.w: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.

vs.t: And brought them out, and said, Sirs, what must I do to be saved?
vs.e: And took them out and said, Sirs, what have I to do to get salvation?
vs.w: brought them out, and said, “Sirs, what must I do to be saved?”

vs.t: And they said, Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, and thy house.
vs.e: And they said, Have faith in the Lord Jesus, and you and your family will have salvation.
vs.w: They said, “Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and your household.”

vs.t: And they spake unto him the word of the Lord, and to all that were in his house.
vs.e: And they gave the word of the Lord to him and to all who were in his house.
vs.w: They spoke the word of the Lord to him, and to all who were in his house.

vs.t: And he took them the same hour of the night, and washed their stripes; and was baptized, he and all his, straightway.
vs.e: And that same hour of the night, he took them, and when he had given attention to their wounds, he and all his family had baptism straight away.
vs.w: He took them the same hour of the night and washed their stripes, and was immediately baptized, he and all his household.

vs.t: And when he had brought them into his house, he set meat before them, and rejoiced, believing in God with all his house.
vs.e: And he took them into his house and gave them food, and he was full of joy, having faith in God with all his family.
vs.w: He brought them up into his house, and set food before them, and rejoiced greatly, with all his household, having believed in God.

lessons.memtext: And the things that thou hast heard of me among many witnesses, the same commit thou to faithful men, who shall be able to teach others also.
lessons.memE: And the things which I have said to you before a number of witnesses, give to those of the faith, so that they may be teachers of others.
lessons.memW: The things which you have heard from me among many witnesses, commit the same things to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.

vs.t: Then came the Jews round about him, and said unto him, How long dost thou make us to doubt? If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly.
vs.e: Then the Jews came round him, saying, how long are you going to keep us in doubt? If you are the Christ, say so clearly.
vs.w: The Jews therefore came around him and said to him, “How long will you hold us in suspense? If you are the Christ, tell us plainly.”

vs.t: Jesus answered them, I told you, and ye believed not: the works that I do in my Father’s name, they bear witness of me.
vs.e: Jesus said in answer, I have said it and you have no belief: the works which I do in my Father's name, these give witness about me.
vs.w: Jesus answered them, “I told you, and you don’t believe. The works that I do in my Father’s name, these testify about me.

vs.t: But ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep, as I said unto you.
vs.e: But you have no belief because you are not of my sheep.
vs.w: But you don’t believe, because you are not of my sheep, as I told you.

vs.t: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:
vs.e: My sheep give ear to my voice, and I have knowledge of them, and they come after me:
vs.w: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

vs.t: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
vs.e: And I give them eternal life; they will never come to destruction, and no one will ever take them out of my hand.
vs.w: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.

vs.t: My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father’s hand.
vs.e: That which my Father has given to me has more value than all; and no one is able to take anything out of the Father's hand.
vs.w: My Father who has given them to me is greater than all. No one is able to snatch them out of my Father’s hand.

vs.t: Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.
vs.e: So if any man is in Christ, he is in a new world: the old things have come to an end; they have truly become new.
vs.w: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

vs.t: And all things are of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given to us the ministry of reconciliation;
vs.e: But all things are of God, who has made us at peace with himself through Christ, and has given to us the work of making peace;
vs.w: But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation;

vs.t: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
vs.e: That is, that God was in Christ making peace between the world and himself, not putting their sins to their account, and having given to us the preaching of this news of peace.
vs.w: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

vs.t: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.
vs.e: So we are the representatives of Christ, as if God was making a request to you through us: we make our request to you, in the name of Christ, be at peace with God.
vs.w: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

vs.t: For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.
vs.e: For him who had no knowledge of sin God made to be sin for us; so that we might become the righteousness of God in him.
vs.w: For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf; so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

vs.t: And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
vs.e: And his witness is this, that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
vs.w: The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.

vs.t: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
vs.e: He who has the Son has the life; he who has not the Son of God has not the life.
vs.w: He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.

vs.t: These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.
vs.e: I have put these things in writing for you who have faith in the name of the Son of God, so that you may be certain that you have eternal life.
vs.w: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.
