lessons.title: God Is My Saviour
lessons.sub: He saves me and gives me new life
lessons.question: How can I be sure I am saved?
ask: What do these verses say about God's plan and our sin?
What did Jesus do, and what must we do?
What promises does God give to those who are saved?
lessons.note: The gospel in five points: God loves you and has good plans for you. We have all sinned and are separated from Him. Jesus died to pay the price for our sin. God invites you into a relationship, but you must accept it. And new disciples cannot stand alone; they need someone to walk with them. God has done His part. Have you done yours? If you have, His promises are sure: you can know you are saved, His Spirit is His seal on you, and no one can pluck you out of His hand. (Baptism, your public step of obedience, is covered in New Life in Christ: Your New Identity.)
lessons.reflect: Since you believed, which changes have you noticed: inner peace, feeling God's love, the joy of being forgiven, a desire to read the Bible, caring for others?
lessons.declare: I have the Son, so I have life. I am sealed by His Spirit and safe in His hand.

vs.t: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you, saith the Lord, thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you an expected end.
vs.e: For I am conscious of my thoughts about you, says the Lord, thoughts of peace and not of evil, to give you hope at the end.
vs.w: For I know the thoughts that I think toward you,” says Yahweh, “thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.

vs.t: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;
vs.e: For all have done wrong and are far from the glory of God;
vs.w: for all have sinned, and fall short of the glory of God;

vs.t: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
vs.e: But God has made clear his love to us, in that, when we were still sinners, Christ gave his life for us.
vs.w: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

vs.t: That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
vs.e: Because, if you say with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and have faith in your heart that God has made him come back from the dead, you will have salvation:
vs.w: that if you will confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord, and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.

vs.t: And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
vs.e: And his witness is this, that God has given us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
vs.w: The testimony is this, that God gave to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.

vs.t: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
vs.e: He who has the Son has the life; he who has not the Son of God has not the life.
vs.w: He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.

vs.t: These things have I written unto you that believe on the name of the Son of God; that ye may know that ye have eternal life, and that ye may believe on the name of the Son of God.
vs.e: I have put these things in writing for you who have faith in the name of the Son of God, so that you may be certain that you have eternal life.
vs.w: These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the Son of God, that you may know that you have eternal life, and that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God.

vs.t: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me:
vs.e: My sheep give ear to my voice, and I have knowledge of them, and they come after me:
vs.w: My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me.

vs.t: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand.
vs.e: And I give them eternal life; they will never come to destruction, and no one will ever take them out of my hand.
vs.w: I give eternal life to them. They will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.

vs.t: Now he which stablisheth us with you in Christ, and hath anointed us, is God;
vs.e: Now he who makes our faith strong together with you, in Christ, and has given us of his grace, is God;
vs.w: Now he who establishes us with you in Christ and anointed us is God,

vs.t: Who hath also sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts.
vs.e: And it is he who has put his stamp on us, even the Spirit, as the sign in our hearts of the coming glory.
vs.w: who also sealed us, and gave us the down payment of the Spirit in our hearts.

lessons.memtext: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
lessons.memE: He who has the Son has the life; he who has not the Son of God has not the life.
lessons.memW: He who has the Son has the life. He who doesn’t have God’s Son doesn’t have the life.

vs.t: And as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of man be lifted up:
vs.e: As the snake was lifted up by Moses in the waste land, even so it is necessary for the Son of man to be lifted up:
vs.w: As Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, even so must the Son of Man be lifted up,

vs.t: That whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have eternal life.
vs.e: So that whoever has faith may have in him eternal life.
vs.w: that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

vs.t: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
vs.e: For God had such love for the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever has faith in him may not come to destruction but have eternal life.
vs.w: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

vs.t: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
vs.e: God did not send his Son into the world to be judge of the world; he sent him so that the world might have salvation through him.
vs.w: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.

vs.t: He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.
vs.e: The man who has faith in him does not come up to be judged; but he who has no faith in him has been judged even now, because he has no faith in the name of the only Son of God.
vs.w: He who believes in him is not judged. He who doesn’t believe has been judged already, because he has not believed in the name of the one and only Son of God.

vs.t: And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.
vs.e: And this is the test by which men are judged: the light has come into the world and men have more love for the dark than for the light, because their acts are evil.
vs.w: This is the judgment, that the light has come into the world, and men loved the darkness rather than the light; for their works were evil.

vs.t: For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.
vs.e: The light is hated by everyone whose acts are evil and he does not come to the light for fear that his acts will be seen.
vs.w: For everyone who does evil hates the light, and doesn’t come to the light, lest his works would be exposed.

vs.t: But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.
vs.e: But he whose life is true comes to the light, so that it may be clearly seen that his acts have been done by the help of God.
vs.w: But he who does the truth comes to the light, that his works may be revealed, that they have been done in God.”

vs.t: And when thou prayest, thou shalt not be as the hypocrites are: for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen of men. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
vs.e: And when you make your prayers, be not like the false-hearted men, who take pleasure in getting up and saying their prayers in the Synagogues and at the street turnings so that they may be seen by men. Truly I say to you, They have their reward.
vs.w: “When you pray, you shall not be as the hypocrites, for they love to stand and pray in the synagogues and in the corners of the streets, that they may be seen by men. Most certainly, I tell you, they have received their reward.

vs.t: But thou, when thou prayest, enter into thy closet, and when thou hast shut thy door, pray to thy Father which is in secret; and thy Father which seeth in secret shall reward thee openly.
vs.e: But when you make your prayer, go into your private room, and, shutting the door, say a prayer to your Father in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will give you your reward.
vs.w: But you, when you pray, enter into your inner room, and having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret, and your Father who sees in secret will reward you openly.

vs.t: But when ye pray, use not vain repetitions, as the heathen do: for they think that they shall be heard for their much speaking.
vs.e: And in your prayer do not make use of the same words again and again, as the Gentiles do: for they have the idea that God will give attention to them because of the number of their words.
vs.w: In praying, don’t use vain repetitions, as the Gentiles do; for they think that they will be heard for their much speaking.

vs.t: Be not ye therefore like unto them: for your Father knoweth what things ye have need of, before ye ask him.
vs.e: So be not like them; because your Father has knowledge of your needs even before you make your requests to him.
vs.w: Therefore don’t be like them, for your Father knows what things you need, before you ask him.

vs.t: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
vs.e: Let this then be your prayer: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
vs.w: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.

vs.t: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
vs.e: Let your kingdom come. Let your pleasure be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
vs.w: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

vs.t: Give us this day our daily bread.
vs.e: Give us this day bread for our needs.
vs.w: Give us today our daily bread.

vs.t: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
vs.e: And make us free of our debts, as we have made those free who are in debt to us.
vs.w: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

vs.t: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
vs.e: And let us not be put to the test, but keep us safe from the Evil One.
vs.w: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

vs.t: For if ye forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you:
vs.e: For if you let men have forgiveness for their sins, you will have forgiveness from your Father in heaven.
vs.w: “For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you.

vs.t: But if ye forgive not men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
vs.e: But if you do not let men have forgiveness for their sins, you will not have forgiveness from your Father for your sins.
vs.w: But if you don’t forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.

lessons.title: God Is My Loving Father
lessons.sub: How He shows His love to me
lessons.question: How does my Heavenly Father show His love to me?
ask: What do you learn about God as a Father?
In what three ways does He show His love here?
Why might discipline be a sign of love?
lessons.note: God created us to love us. He shows His love through His provision (He supplies all our needs), through His salvation (He gave His Son), and through His discipline (like a good parent, He corrects those He loves so we learn the right way to live). Even painful seasons can be the hands of a loving Father shaping you.
lessons.reflect: Where have you seen your Father's provision, salvation or discipline in your life recently?
lessons.declare: Behold what manner of love the Father has given me. I am called a child of God.

vs.t: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
vs.e: See what great love the Father has given us in naming us the children of God; and such we are. For this reason the world does not see who we are, because it did not see who he was.
vs.w: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.

vs.t: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
vs.e: And my God will give you all you have need of from the wealth of his glory in Christ Jesus.
vs.w: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

vs.t: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
vs.e: For God had such love for the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever has faith in him may not come to destruction but have eternal life.
vs.w: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

vs.t: And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
vs.e: And you have not kept in mind the word which says to you as to sons, My son, do not make little of the Lord's punishment, and do not give up hope when you are judged by him;
vs.w: You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are reproved by him;

vs.t: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
vs.e: For the Lord sends punishment on his loved ones; everyone whom he takes as his son has experience of his rod.
vs.w: for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”

vs.t: As many as I love, I rebuke and chasten: be zealous therefore, and repent.
vs.e: To all those who are dear to me, I give sharp words and punishment: then with all your heart have sorrow for your evil ways.
vs.w: As many as I love, I reprove and chasten. Be zealous therefore, and repent.

lessons.memtext: Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.
lessons.memE: See what great love the Father has given us in naming us the children of God; and such we are. For this reason the world does not see who we are, because it did not see who he was.
lessons.memW: See how great a love the Father has given to us, that we should be called children of God! For this cause the world doesn’t know us, because it didn’t know him.

vs.t: Ye have not yet resisted unto blood, striving against sin.
vs.e: Till now you have not given your blood in your fight against sin:
vs.w: You have not yet resisted to blood, striving against sin.

vs.t: And ye have forgotten the exhortation which speaketh unto you as unto children, My son, despise not thou the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when thou art rebuked of him:
vs.e: And you have not kept in mind the word which says to you as to sons, My son, do not make little of the Lord's punishment, and do not give up hope when you are judged by him;
vs.w: You have forgotten the exhortation which reasons with you as with children, “My son, don’t take lightly the chastening of the Lord, nor faint when you are reproved by him;

vs.t: For whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth, and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth.
vs.e: For the Lord sends punishment on his loved ones; everyone whom he takes as his son has experience of his rod.
vs.w: for whom the Lord loves, he disciplines, and chastises every son whom he receives.”

vs.t: If ye endure chastening, God dealeth with you as with sons; for what son is he whom the father chasteneth not?
vs.e: It is for your training that you undergo these things; God is acting to you as a father does to his sons; for what son does not have punishment from his father?
vs.w: It is for discipline that you endure. God deals with you as with children, for what son is there whom his father doesn’t discipline?

vs.t: But if ye be without chastisement, whereof all are partakers, then are ye bastards, and not sons.
vs.e: But if you have not that punishment of which we all have our part, then you are not true sons, but children of shame.
vs.w: But if you are without discipline, of which all have been made partakers, then you are illegitimate, and not children.

vs.t: Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence: shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?
vs.e: And again, if the fathers of our flesh gave us punishment and had our respect, how much more will we be under the authority of the Father of spirits, and have life?
vs.w: Furthermore, we had the fathers of our flesh to chasten us, and we paid them respect. Shall we not much rather be in subjection to the Father of spirits, and live?

vs.t: For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure; but he for our profit, that we might be partakers of his holiness.
vs.e: For they truly gave us punishment for a short time, as it seemed good to them; but he does it for our profit, so that we may become holy as he is.
vs.w: For they indeed, for a few days, punished us as seemed good to them; but he for our profit, that we may be partakers of his holiness.

vs.t: Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous: nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.
vs.e: At the time all punishment seems to be pain and not joy: but after, those who have been trained by it get from it the peace-giving fruit of righteousness.
vs.w: All chastening seems for the present to be not joyous but grievous; yet afterward it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.

lessons.title: Loving My Father Back
lessons.question: How can I show my love for God?
ask: What five things does Jesus include in His model prayer?
What do James, Luke and 1 Thessalonians teach about how to pray?
What is the ultimate test of loving God in John 14:23?
lessons.note: We love Him because He first loved us. We show it by spending time with Him each day (a quiet time with His Word and prayer), by prayer (Jesus' model: Praise, Purpose, Provision, Pardon, Protection; and pray without doubting, without selfish motives, without giving up, without ceasing), and by obedience. You can never have intimacy with God without obeying Him. Start a spiritual journal, a memorial of what God is doing in your life.
lessons.reflect: Use the Prayer Builder to write your own prayer to God using Jesus' five parts.
lessons.declare: I love God because He first loved me. I will spend time with Him, pray, and obey His word.

vs.t: We love him, because he first loved us.
vs.e: We have the power of loving, because he first had love for us.
vs.w: We love him, because he first loved us.

vs.t: After this manner therefore pray ye: Our Father which art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name.
vs.e: Let this then be your prayer: Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.
vs.w: Pray like this: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be kept holy.

vs.t: Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.
vs.e: Let your kingdom come. Let your pleasure be done, as in heaven, so on earth.
vs.w: Let your Kingdom come. Let your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.

vs.t: Give us this day our daily bread.
vs.e: Give us this day bread for our needs.
vs.w: Give us today our daily bread.

vs.t: And forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors.
vs.e: And make us free of our debts, as we have made those free who are in debt to us.
vs.w: Forgive us our debts, as we also forgive our debtors.

vs.t: And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil: For thine is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, for ever. Amen.
vs.e: And let us not be put to the test, but keep us safe from the Evil One.
vs.w: Bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one. For yours is the Kingdom, the power, and the glory forever. Amen.’

vs.t: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.
vs.e: But if any man among you is without wisdom, let him make his request to God, who gives freely to all without an unkind word, and it will be given to him.
vs.w: But if any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him.

vs.t: But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering. For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.
vs.e: Let him make his request in faith, doubting nothing; for he who has doubt in his heart is like the waves of the sea, which are troubled by the driving of the wind.
vs.w: But let him ask in faith, without any doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, driven by the wind and tossed.

vs.t: And he spake a parable unto them to this end, that men ought always to pray, and not to faint;
vs.e: And he made a story for them, the point of which was that men were to go on making prayer and not get tired;
vs.w: He also spoke a parable to them that they must always pray, and not give up,

vs.t: Pray without ceasing.
vs.e: Keep on with your prayers.
vs.w: Pray without ceasing.

vs.t: Jesus answered and said unto him, If a man love me, he will keep my words: and my Father will love him, and we will come unto him, and make our abode with him.
vs.e: Jesus said to him in answer, If anyone has love for me, he will keep my words: and he will be dear to my Father; and we will come to him and make our living-place with him.
vs.w: Jesus answered him, “If a man loves me, he will keep my word. My Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our home with him.

lessons.memtext: If ye keep my commandments, ye shall abide in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and abide in his love.
lessons.memE: If you keep my laws, you will be ever in my love, even as I have kept my Father's laws, and am ever in his love.
lessons.memW: If you keep my commandments, you will remain in my love; even as I have kept my Father’s commandments, and remain in his love.

vs.t: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
vs.e: Make no store of wealth for yourselves on earth, where it may be turned to dust by worms and weather, and where thieves may come in by force and take it away.
vs.w: “Don’t lay up treasures for yourselves on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;

vs.t: But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:
vs.e: But make a store for yourselves in heaven, where it will not be turned to dust and where thieves do not come in to take it away:
vs.w: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consume, and where thieves don’t break through and steal;

vs.t: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
vs.e: For where your wealth is, there will your heart be.
vs.w: for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

vs.t: The light of the body is the eye: if therefore thine eye be single, thy whole body shall be full of light.
vs.e: The light of the body is the eye; if then your eye is true, all your body will be full of light.
vs.w: “The lamp of the body is the eye. If therefore your eye is sound, your whole body will be full of light.

vs.t: But if thine eye be evil, thy whole body shall be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in thee be darkness, how great is that darkness!
vs.e: But if your eye is evil, all your body will be dark. If then the light which is in you is dark, how dark it will be!
vs.w: But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If therefore the light that is in you is darkness, how great is the darkness!

vs.t: No man can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.
vs.e: No man is able to be a servant to two masters: for he will have hate for the one and love for the other, or he will keep to one and have no respect for the other. You may not be servants of God and of wealth.
vs.w: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other; or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.

vs.t: Therefore I say unto you, Take no thought for your life, what ye shall eat, or what ye shall drink; nor yet for your body, what ye shall put on. Is not the life more than meat, and the body than raiment?
vs.e: So I say to you, Take no thought for your life, about food or drink, or about clothing for your body. Is not life more than food, and the body more than its clothing?
vs.w: Therefore I tell you, don’t be anxious for your life: what you will eat, or what you will drink; nor yet for your body, what you will wear. Isn’t life more than food, and the body more than clothing?

vs.t: Behold the fowls of the air: for they sow not, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns; yet your heavenly Father feedeth them. Are ye not much better than they?
vs.e: See the birds of heaven; they do not put seeds in the earth, they do not get in grain, or put it in store-houses; and your Father in heaven gives them food. Are you not of much more value than they?
vs.w: See the birds of the sky, that they don’t sow, neither do they reap, nor gather into barns. Your heavenly Father feeds them. Aren’t you of much more value than they?

vs.t: Which of you by taking thought can add one cubit unto his stature?
vs.e: And which of you by taking thought is able to make himself a cubit taller?
vs.w: “Which of you, by being anxious, can add one moment to his lifespan?

vs.t: And why take ye thought for raiment? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow; they toil not, neither do they spin:
vs.e: And why are you troubled about clothing? See the flowers of the field, how they come up; they do no work, they make no thread:
vs.w: Why are you anxious about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow. They don’t toil, neither do they spin,

vs.t: And yet I say unto you, That even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
vs.e: But I say to you that even Solomon in all his glory was not clothed like one of these.
vs.w: yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.

vs.t: Wherefore, if God so clothe the grass of the field, which to day is, and to morrow is cast into the oven, shall he not much more clothe you, O ye of little faith?
vs.e: But if God gives such clothing to the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is put into the oven, will he not much more give you clothing, O you of little faith?
vs.w: But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which today exists, and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, won’t he much more clothe you, you of little faith?

vs.t: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?
vs.e: Then do not be full of care, saying, What are we to have for food or drink? or, With what may we be clothed?
vs.w: “Therefore don’t be anxious, saying, ‘What will we eat?’, ‘What will we drink?’ or, ‘With what will we be clothed?’

vs.t: (For after all these things do the Gentiles seek:) for your heavenly Father knoweth that ye have need of all these things.
vs.e: Because the Gentiles go in search of all these things: for your Father in heaven has knowledge that you have need of all these things:
vs.w: For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need all these things.

vs.t: But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.
vs.e: But let your first care be for his kingdom and his righteousness; and all these other things will be given to you in addition.
vs.w: But seek first God’s Kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

vs.t: Take therefore no thought for the morrow: for the morrow shall take thought for the things of itself. Sufficient unto the day is the evil thereof.
vs.e: Then have no care for tomorrow: tomorrow will take care of itself. Take the trouble of the day as it comes.
vs.w: Therefore don’t be anxious for tomorrow, for tomorrow will be anxious for itself. Each day’s own evil is sufficient.

vs.t: For this cause we also, since the day we heard it, do not cease to pray for you, and to desire that ye might be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;
vs.e: For this reason, we, from the day when we had word of it, keep on in prayer for you, that you may be full of the knowledge of his purpose, with all wisdom and experience of the Spirit,
vs.w: For this cause, we also, since the day we heard this, don’t cease praying and making requests for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all spiritual wisdom and understanding,

vs.t: That ye might walk worthy of the Lord unto all pleasing, being fruitful in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
vs.e: Living uprightly in the approval of the Lord, giving fruit in every good work, and increasing in the knowledge of God;
vs.w: that you may walk worthily of the Lord, to please him in all respects, bearing fruit in every good work and increasing in the knowledge of God,

vs.t: Strengthened with all might, according to his glorious power, unto all patience and longsuffering with joyfulness;
vs.e: Full of strength in the measure of the great power of his glory, so that you may undergo all troubles with joy;
vs.w: strengthened with all power, according to the might of his glory, for all endurance and perseverance with joy,

vs.t: Giving thanks unto the Father, which hath made us meet to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light:
vs.e: Giving praise to the Father who has given us a part in the heritage of the saints in light;
vs.w: giving thanks to the Father, who made us fit to be partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light,

vs.t: Who hath delivered us from the power of darkness, and hath translated us into the kingdom of his dear Son:
vs.e: Who has made us free from the power of evil and given us a place in the kingdom of the Son of his love;
vs.w: who delivered us out of the power of darkness, and translated us into the Kingdom of the Son of his love,

vs.t: In whom we have redemption through his blood, even the forgiveness of sins:
vs.e: In whom we have our salvation, the forgiveness of sins:
vs.w: in whom we have our redemption, the forgiveness of our sins.

lessons.title: God Is My King
lessons.question: What is God's Kingdom like, and what is my part in it?
ask: What do you learn about God as King?
How is God's Kingdom different from the kingdoms of this world?
What privileges do you have as a citizen of His Kingdom?
lessons.note: God is eternal, He is the Creator, and He is the King who reigns. His Kingdom is the reign and rule of God, and it is upside down compared to the world: the great serve, the first are last, and giving is better than receiving. In His Kingdom you have your identity (a citizen, part of God's household), His sufficiency (His grace is enough) and His power (you will do the works Jesus did).
lessons.reflect: Which part of God's upside-down Kingdom challenges you most: serving, not fighting back, being last, or giving?
lessons.declare: I seek first the Kingdom of God. I am a citizen of heaven and His grace is sufficient for me.

lessons.title: The Throne of My Heart
lessons.sub: Who is in charge of my life?
lessons.question: Who sits on the throne of my heart?
ask: What has God rescued us from?
What are the three kinds of temptation in 1 John 2:16?
How do we stand against the enemy in Ephesians 6?
lessons.note: There is another kingdom, the power of darkness, led by Satan. If you follow Jesus, you were rescued from it, but the enemy still prowls to devour and uses the lust of the flesh, the lust of the eyes and the pride of life to pull us away. Each of us is born wanting to sit on the throne of our own heart. Jesus calls us to deny ourselves, take up our cross daily and let Him rule our time, money, relationships and decisions.
lessons.reflect: Which area of your life (time, money, relationships, decisions) have you not yet handed over to the King?
lessons.declare: I deny myself, take up my cross daily, and put Jesus on the throne of my heart.

lessons.question: What is the church, and who leads it?

lessons.note: The church is not a building. It is a gathering of disciples who obey Jesus and work together for God's purpose, and Jesus is the Head who gives it direction. lessons.declare: Jesus is the Head of the church and the Lord of my life. I will love God, love people and make disciples.

lessons.title: A Life of Sacrifice

lessons.question: How do I honour Jesus' sacrifice with my life?
ask: What did Jesus ask us to remember with the bread and the cup?
What do you learn about fasting and giving?
What does it mean to be a living sacrifice?
lessons.note: The gospel is all about the sacrifice of Jesus. At the Lord's Supper we remember His body broken and His blood poured out for us. In return we offer ourselves: fasting (denying ourselves to focus on God), tithes (giving our money for God's work), offerings (our time, talents and gifts) and, above all, our whole lives as living sacrifices.
lessons.reflect: Which sacrifice is God inviting you into this week: fasting, giving, serving, or surrendering an area of your life?
lessons.declare: I present my life as a living sacrifice to God, because Jesus gave His life for me.

vs.w: For I received from the Lord that which also I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was betrayed took bread.

vs.t: And when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me.
vs.e: And when it had been broken with an act of praise, he said, This is my body which is for you: do this in memory of me.
vs.w: When he had given thanks, he broke it and said, “Take, eat. This is my body, which is broken for you. Do this in memory of me.”

vs.t: After the same manner also he took the cup, when he had supped, saying, This cup is the new testament in my blood: this do ye, as oft as ye drink it, in remembrance of me.
vs.e: In the same way, with the cup, after the meal, he said, This cup is the new testament in my blood: do this, whenever you take it, in memory of me.
vs.w: In the same way he also took the cup, after supper, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink, in memory of me.”

vs.t: For as often as ye eat this bread, and drink this cup, ye do shew the Lord’s death till he come.
vs.e: For whenever you take the bread and the cup you give witness to the Lord's death till he comes.
vs.w: For as often as you eat this bread and drink this cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.

vs.t: Moreover when ye fast, be not, as the hypocrites, of a sad countenance: for they disfigure their faces, that they may appear unto men to fast. Verily I say unto you, They have their reward.
vs.e: And when you go without food, be not sad-faced as the false-hearted are. For they go about with changed looks, so that men may see that they are going without food. Truly I say to you, They have their reward.
vs.w: “Moreover when you fast, don’t be like the hypocrites, with sad faces. For they disfigure their faces, that they may be seen by men to be fasting. Most certainly I tell you, they have received their reward.

vs.t: But thou, when thou fastest, anoint thine head, and wash thy face;
vs.e: But when you go without food, put oil on your head and make your face clean;
vs.w: But you, when you fast, anoint your head, and wash your face;

vs.t: That thou appear not unto men to fast, but unto thy Father which is in secret: and thy Father, which seeth in secret, shall reward thee openly.
vs.e: So that no one may see that you are going without food, but your Father in secret; and your Father, who sees in secret, will give you your reward.
vs.w: so that you are not seen by men to be fasting, but by your Father who is in secret, and your Father, who sees in secret, will reward you.

vs.t: Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse, that there may be meat in mine house, and prove me now herewith, saith the Lord of hosts, if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there shall not be room enough to receive it.
vs.e: Let your tenths come into the store-house so that there may be food in my house, and put me to the test by doing so, says the Lord of armies, and see if I do not make the windows of heaven open and send down such a blessing on you that there is no room for it.
vs.w: Bring the whole tithe into the storehouse, that there may be food in my house, and test me now in this,” says Yahweh of Armies, “if I will not open you the windows of heaven, and pour you out a blessing, that there will not be room enough for.

vs.t: And Jesus sat over against the treasury, and beheld how the people cast money into the treasury: and many that were rich cast in much.
vs.e: And he took a seat by the place where the money was kept, and saw how the people put money into the boxes: and a number who had wealth put in much.
vs.w: Jesus sat down opposite the treasury, and saw how the multitude cast money into the treasury. Many who were rich cast in much.

vs.t: And there came a certain poor widow, and she threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
vs.e: And there came a poor widow, and she put in two little bits of money, which make a farthing.
vs.w: A poor widow came, and she cast in two small brass coins, which equal a quadrans coin.

vs.t: And he called unto him his disciples, and saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, That this poor widow hath cast more in, than all they which have cast into the treasury:
vs.e: And he made his disciples come to him, and said to them, Truly I say to you, This poor widow has put in more than all those who are putting money into the box:
vs.w: He called his disciples to himself, and said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, this poor widow gave more than all those who are giving into the treasury,

vs.t: For all they did cast in of their abundance; but she of her want did cast in all that she had, even all her living.
vs.e: Because they all put in something out of what they had no need for; but she out of her need put in all she had, even all her living.
vs.w: for they all gave out of their abundance, but she, out of her poverty, gave all that she had to live on.”

vs.t: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.
vs.e: For this reason I make request to you, brothers, by the mercies of God, that you will give your bodies as a living offering, holy, pleasing to God, which is the worship it is right for you to give him.
vs.w: Therefore I urge you, brothers, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service.

vs.t: Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house, unto a land that I will shew thee:
vs.e: Now the Lord said to Abram, Go out from your country and from your family and from your father's house, into the land to which I will be your guide:
vs.w: Now Yahweh said to Abram, “Leave your country, and your relatives, and your father’s house, and go to the land that I will show you.

vs.t: And I will make of thee a great nation, and I will bless thee, and make thy name great; and thou shalt be a blessing:
vs.e: And I will make of you a great nation, blessing you and making your name great; and you will be a blessing:
vs.w: I will make of you a great nation. I will bless you and make your name great. You will be a blessing.

vs.t: And I will bless them that bless thee, and curse him that curseth thee: and in thee shall all families of the earth be blessed.
vs.e: To them who are good to you will I give blessing, and on him who does you wrong will I put my curse: and you will become a name of blessing to all the families of the earth.
vs.w: I will bless those who bless you, and I will curse him who treats you with contempt. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you.”

vs.t: So Abram departed, as the Lord had spoken unto him; and Lot went with him: and Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.
vs.e: So Abram went as the Lord had said to him, and Lot went with him: Abram was seventy-five years old when he went away from Haran.
vs.w: So Abram went, as Yahweh had told him. Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.

vs.t: If the world hate you, ye know that it hated me before it hated you.
vs.e: If you are hated by the world, keep in mind that I was hated by the world before you.
vs.w: If the world hates you, you know that it has hated me before it hated you.

vs.t: If ye were of the world, the world would love his own: but because ye are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
vs.e: If you were of the world, you would be loved by the world: but because you are not of the world, but I have taken you out of the world, you are hated by the world.
vs.w: If you were of the world, the world would love its own. But because you are not of the world, since I chose you out of the world, therefore the world hates you.

vs.t: Remember the word that I said unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you; if they have kept my saying, they will keep yours also.
vs.e: Keep in mind the words I said to you, A servant is not greater than his lord. If they were cruel to me, they will be cruel to you; if they kept my words, they will keep yours.
vs.w: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.

vs.t: But all these things will they do unto you for my name’s sake, because they know not him that sent me.
vs.e: They will do all this to you because of my name--because they have no knowledge of him who sent me.
vs.w: But they will do all these things to you for my name’s sake, because they don’t know him who sent me.

lessons.title: God Is My Sender
lessons.sub: As the Father sent Jesus, He sends me
lessons.question: What is God's heart for the world, and where does He send me?
ask: What do these verses show about God's heart for the nations?
What were Jesus' first and last instructions to His followers?
Why does someone need to be sent, according to Romans 10?
lessons.note: From the very beginning God planned to bless all families of the earth, for foreigners to know Him, for His salvation to reach all nations and His house to be a house of prayer for all people. He loves the world and is not willing that any should perish. Jesus' first words to His disciples were "Come, and I will make you fishers of men"; His last were "Go and make disciples of all nations." There are four calls to share: from above (God commands it), from inside (His word burns within us), from outside (people crying "come and help us", Acts 16:9) and from below (the rich man in Luke 16 begging for his brothers to be warned).
lessons.reflect: Which of the four calls (above, inside, outside, below) speaks to you most strongly?
lessons.declare: As the Father sent Jesus, so Jesus sends me. I will go and make disciples.

vs.t: To the chief Musician on Neginoth, A Psalm or Song. God be merciful unto us, and bless us; and cause his face to shine upon us; Selah.
vs.e: May God give us mercy and blessing, and let the light of his face be shining on us; (Selah.)
vs.w: May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us.

vs.t: That thy way may be known upon earth, thy saving health among all nations.
vs.e: So that men may see your way on the earth, and your salvation among all nations.
vs.w: That your way may be known on earth, and your salvation among all nations,

vs.t: Let the people praise thee, O God; let all the people praise thee.
vs.e: Let the peoples give you praise, O God; let all the peoples give you praise.
vs.w: let the peoples praise you, God. Let all the peoples praise you.

vs.t: Even them will I bring to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer: their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar; for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.
vs.e: I will make them come to my holy mountain, and will give them joy in my house of prayer; I will take pleasure in the burned offerings which they make on my altar: for my house will be named a house of prayer for all peoples.
vs.w: I will bring these to my holy mountain, and make them joyful in my house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and their sacrifices will be accepted on my altar; for my house will be called a house of prayer for all peoples.”

vs.t: For God so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth in him should not perish, but have everlasting life.
vs.e: For God had such love for the world that he gave his only Son, so that whoever has faith in him may not come to destruction but have eternal life.
vs.w: For God so loved the world, that he gave his one and only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

vs.t: For God sent not his Son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world through him might be saved.
vs.e: God did not send his Son into the world to be judge of the world; he sent him so that the world might have salvation through him.
vs.w: For God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge the world, but that the world should be saved through him.

vs.t: The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.
vs.e: The Lord is not slow in keeping his word, as he seems to some, but he is waiting in mercy for you, not desiring the destruction of any, but that all may be turned from their evil ways.
vs.w: The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

vs.t: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
vs.e: And Jesus said to them, Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men.
vs.w: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”

vs.t: Then said Jesus to them again, Peace be unto you: as my Father hath sent me, even so send I you.
vs.e: And Jesus said to them again, May peace be with you! As the Father sent me, even so I now send you.
vs.w: Jesus therefore said to them again, “Peace be to you. As the Father has sent me, even so I send you.”

vs.t: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher?
vs.e: But how will they give worship to him in whom they have no faith? and how will they have faith in him of whom they have not had news? and how will they have news without a preacher?
vs.w: How then will they call on him in whom they have not believed? How will they believe in him whom they have not heard? How will they hear without a preacher?

vs.t: And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things!
vs.e: And how will there be preachers if they are not sent? As it is said, How beautiful are the feet of those who give the glad news of good things.
vs.w: And how will they preach unless they are sent? As it is written: “How beautiful are the feet of those who preach the Good News of peace, who bring glad tidings of good things!”

vs.t: And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; There stood a man of Macedonia, and prayed him, saying, Come over into Macedonia, and help us.
vs.e: And Paul had a vision in the night; a man of Macedonia came, requesting him, and saying, Come over into Macedonia and give us help.
vs.w: A vision appeared to Paul in the night. There was a man of Macedonia standing, begging him, and saying, “Come over into Macedonia and help us.”

vs.t: And after he had seen the vision, immediately we endeavoured to go into Macedonia, assuredly gathering that the Lord had called us for to preach the gospel unto them.
vs.e: And when he had seen the vision, straight away we made the decision to go into Macedonia, for it seemed certain to us that God had sent us to give the good news to them.
vs.w: When he had seen the vision, immediately we sought to go out to Macedonia, concluding that the Lord had called us to preach the Good News to them.

vs.t: There was a certain rich man, which was clothed in purple and fine linen, and fared sumptuously every day:
vs.e: Now there was a certain man of great wealth, who was dressed in fair clothing of purple and delicate linen, and was shining and glad every day.
vs.w: “Now there was a certain rich man, and he was clothed in purple and fine linen, living in luxury every day.

vs.t: And there was a certain beggar named Lazarus, which was laid at his gate, full of sores,
vs.e: And a certain poor man, named Lazarus, was stretched out at his door, full of wounds,
vs.w: A certain beggar, named Lazarus, was taken to his gate, full of sores,

vs.t: And desiring to be fed with the crumbs which fell from the rich man’s table: moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
vs.e: Desiring the broken bits of food which came from the table of the man of wealth; and even the dogs came and put their tongues on his wounds.
vs.w: and desiring to be fed with the crumbs that fell from the rich man’s table. Yes, even the dogs came and licked his sores.

vs.t: And it came to pass, that the beggar died, and was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;
vs.e: And in time the poor man came to his end, and angels took him to Abraham's breast. And the man of wealth came to his end, and was put in the earth.
vs.w: The beggar died, and he was carried away by the angels to Abraham’s bosom. The rich man also died, and was buried.

vs.t: And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.
vs.e: And in hell, being in great pain, lifting up his eyes he saw Abraham, far away, and Lazarus on his breast.
vs.w: In Hades, he lifted up his eyes, being in torment, and saw Abraham far off, and Lazarus at his bosom.

vs.t: And he cried and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
vs.e: And he gave a cry and said, Father Abraham, have mercy on me and send Lazarus, so that he may put the end of his finger in water and put it on my tongue, for I am cruelly burning in this flame.
vs.w: He cried and said, ‘Father Abraham, have mercy on me, and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water, and cool my tongue! For I am in anguish in this flame.’

vs.t: But Abraham said, Son, remember that thou in thy lifetime receivedst thy good things, and likewise Lazarus evil things: but now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
vs.e: But Abraham said, Keep in mind, my son, that when you were living, you had your good things, while Lazarus had evil things: but now, he is comforted and you are in pain.
vs.w: “But Abraham said, ‘Son, remember that you, in your lifetime, received your good things, and Lazarus, in the same way, bad things. But here he is now comforted, and you are in anguish.

vs.t: And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.
vs.e: And in addition, there is a deep division fixed between us and you, so that those who might go from here to you are not able to do so, and no one may come from you to us.
vs.w: Besides all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed, that those who want to pass from here to you are not able, and that no one may cross over from there to us.’

vs.t: Then he said, I pray thee therefore, father, that thou wouldest send him to my father’s house:
vs.e: And he said, Father, it is my request that you will send him to my father's house;
vs.w: “He said, ‘I ask you therefore, father, that you would send him to my father’s house;

vs.t: For I have five brethren; that he may testify unto them, lest they also come into this place of torment.
vs.e: For I have five brothers; and let him give them an account of these things, so that they may not come to this place of pain.
vs.w: for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, so they won’t also come into this place of torment.’

vs.t: Abraham saith unto him, They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them.
vs.e: But Abraham said, They have Moses and the prophets; let them give ear to what they say.
vs.w: “But Abraham said to him, ‘They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.’

vs.t: And he said, Nay, father Abraham: but if one went unto them from the dead, they will repent.
vs.e: And he said, No, father Abraham, but if someone went to them from the dead, their hearts would be changed.
vs.w: “He said, ‘No, father Abraham, but if one goes to them from the dead, they will repent.’

vs.t: And he said unto him, If they hear not Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead.
vs.e: And he said to him, If they will not give attention to Moses and the prophets, they will not be moved even if someone comes back from the dead.
vs.w: “He said to him, ‘If they don’t listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded if one rises from the dead.’ ”

lessons.title: Bold in the Face of Suffering
lessons.sub: What will it take to stop me?
lessons.question: What will it take to stop me from sharing the good news?
ask: What did it take to stop Jesus, and the first believers, from sharing?
What does Jesus say we should expect from the world?
What does it mean to confess Jesus before men?
lessons.note: Jesus was met with fierce opposition and was eventually put to death, yet nothing stopped Him. The first believers were threatened, imprisoned and killed, but they said, "we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard." They shared boldly, even unto death. If you follow Jesus, you can expect opposition. He suffered for you. Are you willing to suffer for Him? Practise telling the gospel story (try the Gospel on the Hand tool) until you can share it with confidence.
lessons.reflect: What fear or pressure is most likely to stop you from sharing? Bring it to God now.
lessons.declare: I will not be ashamed. I will confess Jesus before men, whatever it costs.

vs.w: They called them, and commanded them not to speak at all nor teach in the name of Jesus.

vs.w: But Peter and John answered them, “Whether it is right in the sight of God to listen to you rather than to God, judge for yourselves,

vs.w: Remember the word that I said to you: ‘A servant is not greater than his lord.’ If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they kept my word, they will also keep yours.

vs.t: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
vs.e: To everyone, then, who gives witness to me before men, I will give witness before my Father in heaven.
vs.w: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.

vs.t: But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.
vs.e: But if anyone says before men that he has no knowledge of me, I will say that I have no knowledge of him before my Father in heaven.
vs.w: But whoever denies me before men, I will also deny him before my Father who is in heaven.

vs.t: For unto you it is given in the behalf of Christ, not only to believe on him, but also to suffer for his sake;
vs.e: Because to you it has been given in the cause of Christ not only to have faith in him, but to undergo pain on his account:
vs.w: Because it has been granted to you on behalf of Christ, not only to believe in him, but also to suffer on his behalf,

vs.t: Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.
vs.e: And the voice of the Lord came to my ears, saying, Whom am I to send, and who will go for us? Then I said, Here am I, send me.
vs.w: I heard the Lord’s voice, saying, “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?” Then I said, “Here I am. Send me!”

lessons.memtext: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.
lessons.memE: To everyone, then, who gives witness to me before men, I will give witness before my Father in heaven.
lessons.memW: Everyone therefore who confesses me before men, I will also confess him before my Father who is in heaven.

vs.t: But the Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, whom the Father will send in my name, he shall teach you all things, and bring all things to your remembrance, whatsoever I have said unto you.
vs.e: But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will be your teacher in all things and will put you in mind of everything I have said to you.
vs.w: But the Counselor, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you all things, and will remind you of all that I said to you.

vs.t: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
vs.e: May peace be with you; my peace I give to you: I give it not as the world gives. Let not your heart be troubled; let it be without fear.
vs.w: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

vs.t: But now I go my way to him that sent me; and none of you asketh me, Whither goest thou?
vs.e: But now I am going to him who sent me; and not one of you says to me, Where are you going?

vs.t: Of righteousness, because I go to my Father, and ye see me no more;

vs.t: Of judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.

lessons.title: God Is My Teacher
lessons.sub: The Holy Spirit lives in me
lessons.question: How does the Holy Spirit teach and help me?
ask: What did God promise in Joel 2:28?
What four things does the Holy Spirit do in these verses?
Which of these do you most need right now?
lessons.note: God reveals Himself as Father, Son and Holy Spirit. In Old Testament times the Spirit came on special leaders, but God promised to pour out His Spirit on all people, and at Pentecost He did. Now the Holy Spirit lives in every believer. He convicts us (shows us sin), teaches us (reminds us of Jesus' words), guides us (into all truth) and empowers us (to be witnesses). He is our primary Teacher.
lessons.reflect: Where do you need the Holy Spirit to convict, teach, guide or empower you this week?
lessons.declare: The Holy Spirit teaches me, guides me into all truth and empowers me to be a witness.

vs.t: And it shall come to pass afterward, that I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your old men shall dream dreams, your young men shall see visions:
vs.e: And after that, it will come about, says the Lord, that I will send my spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will be prophets, your old men will have dreams, your young men will see visions:
vs.w: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions.

vs.e: But you will have power, when the Holy Spirit has come on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and all Judaea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.
vs.w: But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you. You will be witnesses to me in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth.”

vs.t: And when the day of Pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.
vs.e: And when the day of Pentecost was come, they were all together in one place.
vs.w: Now when the day of Pentecost had come, they were all with one accord in one place.

vs.t: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.
vs.e: And suddenly there came from heaven a sound like the rushing of a violent wind, and all the house where they were was full of it.
vs.w: Suddenly there came from the sky a sound like the rushing of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house where they were sitting.

vs.e: And on my men-servants and my women-servants I will send my Spirit, and they will be prophets.
vs.w: Yes, and on my servants and on my handmaidens in those days, I will pour out my Spirit, and they will prophesy.

lessons.title: Doers of the Word
lessons.question: How do I study the Bible so that I obey it?
ask: What four things is Scripture useful for?
What is the difference between a hearer and a doer?
Who does Jesus call great in the kingdom of heaven?
lessons.note: The Bible is 66 books, written by over 40 authors across about 1,500 years, all inspired by the Holy Spirit. It is useful for teaching (what is right), rebuking (what is not right), correcting (how to get right) and training in righteousness (how to stay right). But knowledge is not enough: we must obey, and we need accountability to keep obeying. A simple tool is S.O.S.: what does it Say, what must I Obey, with whom can I Share? Start with the Gospel of Mark, a passage at a time.
lessons.reflect: Open the S.O.S. Bible Study and begin with Mark 1:1-20. What is God teaching you to obey?
lessons.declare: I will be a doer of the Word and not a hearer only.

vs.t: All scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness:
vs.e: Every holy Writing which comes from God is of profit for teaching, for training, for guiding, for education in righteousness:
vs.w: Every Scripture is God-breathed and profitable for teaching, for reproof, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,

vs.t: That the man of God may be perfect, throughly furnished unto all good works.
vs.e: So that the man of God may be complete, trained and made ready for every good work.
vs.w: that each person who belongs to God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.

vs.t: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
vs.e: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers of it, blinding yourselves with false ideas.
vs.w: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.

vs.t: Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.
vs.e: Whoever then goes against the smallest of these laws, teaching men to do the same, will be named least in the kingdom of heaven; but he who keeps the laws, teaching others to keep them, will be named great in the kingdom of heaven.
vs.w: Whoever, therefore, shall break one of these least commandments, and teach others to do so, shall be called least in the Kingdom of Heaven; but whoever shall do and teach them shall be called great in the Kingdom of Heaven.

vs.t: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;
vs.e: The first words of the good news of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
vs.w: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.

vs.t: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
vs.e: Even as it is said in the book of Isaiah the prophet, See, I send my servant before your face, who will make ready your way;
vs.w: As it is written in the prophets, “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you:

vs.t: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
vs.e: The voice of one crying in the waste land, Make ready the way of the Lord, make his roads straight;
vs.w: the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’ ”

vs.t: John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
vs.e: John came, and gave baptism in the waste land, preaching baptism as a sign of forgiveness of sin for those whose hearts were changed.
vs.w: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.

vs.t: And there went out unto him all the land of Judea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.
vs.e: And there went out to him all the people of Judaea, and all those of Jerusalem, and they were given baptism by him in the river Jordan, saying that they were sinners.
vs.w: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.

vs.t: And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;
vs.e: And John was clothed in camel's hair, with a leather band about him; and his food was locusts and honey.
vs.w: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.

vs.t: And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.
vs.e: And he said to them all, There is one coming after me who is greater than I, whose shoes I am not good enough to undo.
vs.w: He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.

vs.t: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
vs.e: I have given you baptism with water, but he will give you baptism with the Holy Spirit.
vs.w: I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”

vs.t: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.
vs.e: And it came about in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was given baptism by John in the Jordan.
vs.w: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

vs.t: And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him:
vs.e: And straight away, coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens broken open and the Spirit coming down on him as a dove:
vs.w: Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.

vs.t: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
vs.e: And a voice came out of heaven, You are my dearly loved Son, with whom I am well pleased.
vs.w: A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

vs.t: And immediately the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.
vs.e: And straight away the Spirit sent him out into the waste land.
vs.w: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.

vs.t: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
vs.e: And he was in the waste land for forty days, being tested by Satan; and he was with the beasts; and the angels took care of him.
vs.w: He was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.

vs.t: Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
vs.e: Now after John had been put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the good news of God,
vs.w: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,

vs.t: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
vs.e: And saying, The time has come, and the kingdom of God is near: let your hearts be turned from sin and have faith in the good news.
vs.w: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”

vs.t: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
vs.e: And going by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon, and Andrew, the brother of Simon, putting a net into the sea: for they were fishermen.
vs.w: Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew, the brother of Simon, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.

vs.t: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
vs.e: And Jesus said to them, Come after me, and I will make you fishers of men.
vs.w: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”

vs.t: And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.
vs.e: And they went straight from their nets, and came after him.
vs.w: Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.

vs.t: And when he had gone a little further thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
vs.e: And going on a little farther, he saw James, the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were in their boat stitching up their nets.
vs.w: Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.

vs.t: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.
vs.e: And he said, Come after me: and they went away from their father Zebedee, who was in the boat with the servants, and came after him.
vs.w: Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.

vs.t: Wherefore lay apart all filthiness and superfluity of naughtiness, and receive with meekness the engrafted word, which is able to save your souls.
vs.e: For this reason, putting away all dirty behaviour and the overweight of evil, take into your souls without pride the word which, being planted there, is able to give you salvation.
vs.w: Therefore, putting away all filthiness and overflowing of wickedness, receive with humility the implanted word, which is able to save your souls.

vs.t: But be ye doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving your own selves.
vs.e: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers of it, blinding yourselves with false ideas.
vs.w: But be doers of the word, and not only hearers, deluding your own selves.

vs.t: For if any be a hearer of the word, and not a doer, he is like unto a man beholding his natural face in a glass:
vs.e: Because if any man is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a glass;
vs.w: For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man looking at his natural face in a mirror;

vs.t: For he beholdeth himself, and goeth his way, and straightway forgetteth what manner of man he was.
vs.e: For after looking at himself he goes away, and in a short time he has no memory of what he was like.
vs.w: for he sees himself, and goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was.

vs.t: But whoso looketh into the perfect law of liberty, and continueth therein, he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work, this man shall be blessed in his deed.
vs.e: But he who goes on looking into the true law which makes him free, being not a hearer without memory but a doer putting it into effect, this man will have a blessing on his acts.
vs.w: But he who looks into the perfect law of freedom and continues, not being a hearer who forgets, but a doer of the work, this man will be blessed in what he does.

vs.t: If any man among you seem to be religious, and bridleth not his tongue, but deceiveth his own heart, this man’s religion is vain.
vs.e: If a man seems to have religion and has no control over his tongue but lets himself be tricked by what is false, this man's religion is of no value.
vs.w: If anyone among you thinks himself to be religious while he doesn’t bridle his tongue, but deceives his heart, this man’s religion is worthless.

vs.t: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
vs.e: The religion which is holy and free from evil in the eyes of our God and Father is this: to take care of children who have no fathers and of widows who are in trouble, and to keep oneself untouched by the world.
vs.w: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

title: Who Is Jesus Christ?
intro: Before we can know who we are, we must know who He is. Walk through the Scriptures that reveal Jesus: eternal God, perfect man, Saviour and coming King.

lessons.title: The Eternal Word
lessons.note: Jesus did not begin in Bethlehem. John calls Him the Logos, the Word: God's full self-expression. He was with God, He was God, and everything that exists was made through Him. Then the Word became flesh and lived among us.
lessons.reflect: If Jesus made everything, what does that say about His power over the things you face today?
lessons.declare: Jesus is the eternal Word. Everything was made by Him and for Him, including me.

vs.t: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
vs.e: From the first he was the Word, and the Word was in relation with God and was God.
vs.w: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.

vs.t: The same was in the beginning with God.
vs.e: This Word was from the first in relation with God.
vs.w: The same was in the beginning with God.

vs.t: All things were made by him; and without him was not any thing made that was made.
vs.e: All things came into existence through him, and without him nothing was.
vs.w: All things were made through him. Without him, nothing was made that has been made.

vs.t: And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us, (and we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father,) full of grace and truth.
vs.e: And so the Word became flesh and took a place among us for a time; and we saw his glory--such glory as is given to an only son by his father--saw it to be true and full of grace.
vs.w: The Word became flesh, and lived among us. We saw his glory, such glory as of the one and only Son of the Father, full of grace and truth.

vs.t: Who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of every creature:
vs.e: Who is the image of the unseen God coming into existence before all living things;
vs.w: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.

vs.t: For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible, whether they be thrones, or dominions, or principalities, or powers: all things were created by him, and for him:
vs.e: For by him all things were made, in heaven and on earth, things seen and things unseen, authorities, lords, rulers, and powers; all things were made by him and for him;
vs.w: For by him all things were created in the heavens and on the earth, visible things and invisible things, whether thrones or dominions or principalities or powers. All things have been created through him and for him.

vs.t: And he is before all things, and by him all things consist.
vs.e: He is before all things, and in him all things have being.
vs.w: He is before all things, and in him all things are held together.

vs.t: I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end, the first and the last.
vs.e: I am the First and the Last, the start and the end.
vs.w: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.

lessons.title: The Son of God
lessons.note: "Son of God" does not mean Jesus was created. It means He shares the very nature of the Father. Hebrews says He is the brightness of God's glory and the exact image of His person. To see Jesus is to see what God is like.
lessons.reflect: Peter's answer came by revelation from the Father. Who do you say Jesus is?
lessons.declare: Jesus is the only begotten Son of God, the exact image of the Father.

vs.e: He says to them, But who do you say that I am?
vs.w: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?”

vs.t: And Simon Peter answered and said, Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.

lessons.title: The Great "I AM"
lessons.note: God revealed Himself to Moses as "I AM THAT I AM". In John's Gospel Jesus takes that same name: "Before Abraham was, I am." Then He completes it: I am the bread, the light, the good shepherd, the resurrection, the way, the vine.

lessons.declare: Jesus is my bread, my light, my shepherd, my life, my way and my vine.

title: My Identity in Christ
intro: What God says about you is truer than what anyone else says, including you. Discover every scripture that tells you who you are in Christ.
