lessons.note: In Christ you are not a repaired version of the old you. You are a brand new kind of creation (kainos: new in nature, not just new in time). God gives a new heart and a new spirit.
lessons.reflect: What old label do you need to stop wearing?
lessons.declare: I am a new creation. Old things are passed away; all things are new.

vs.e: So if any man is in Christ, he is in a new world: the old things have come to an end; they have truly become new.
vs.w: Therefore if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things have passed away. Behold, all things have become new.

vs.w: We were buried therefore with him through baptism into death, that just as Christ was raised from the dead through the glory of the Father, so we also might walk in newness of life.

lessons.title: I Am Chosen and Loved
lessons.note: God chose you before the foundation of the world. You are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a people for His own possession. His love for you is everlasting.
lessons.reflect: How would you live differently if you never doubted being wanted?
lessons.declare: I am chosen, loved with an everlasting love, and set apart for God.

vs.t: According as he hath chosen us in him before the foundation of the world, that we should be holy and without blame before him in love:
vs.e: Even as he made selection of us in him from the first, so that we might be holy and free from all evil before him in love:
vs.w: even as he chose us in him before the foundation of the world, that we would be holy and without defect before him in love,

vs.t: But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light:
vs.e: But you are a special people, a holy nation, priests and kings, a people given up completely to God, so that you may make clear the virtues of him who took you out of the dark into the light of heaven.
vs.w: But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God’s own possession, that you may proclaim the excellence of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.

vs.e: You did not take me for yourselves, but I took you for myself; and I gave you the work of going about and producing fruit which will be for ever; so that whatever request you make to the Father in my name he may give it to you.
vs.w: You didn’t choose me, but I chose you and appointed you, that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain; that whatever you will ask of the Father in my name, he may give it to you.

lessons.title: I Am God's Workmanship
lessons.note: Poiema (where we get "poem") means something carefully made. You are God's masterpiece, created in Christ Jesus for good works He planned ahead of time.
lessons.reflect: What gifts or passions has God built into you that point to your good works?

vs.w: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared before that we would walk in them.

vs.w: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

lessons.title: I Am Free
lessons.note: Jesus did not just improve your situation; He broke the chains. Whom the Son sets free is free indeed. Stand firm and do not go back to any yoke of bondage.
lessons.reflect: Is there a habit, fear or lie you need to stand against in your freedom?
lessons.declare: The Son has set me free and I am free indeed.

vs.t: If the Son therefore shall make you free, ye shall be free indeed.
vs.e: If then the son makes you free, you will be truly free.
vs.w: If therefore the Son makes you free, you will be free indeed.

vs.t: Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.
vs.e: Christ has truly made us free: then keep your free condition and let no man put a yoke on you again.
vs.w: Stand firm therefore in the liberty by which Christ has made us free, and don’t be entangled again with a yoke of bondage.

vs.w: knowing this, that our old man was crucified with him, that the body of sin might be done away with, so that we would no longer be in bondage to sin.

vs.t: For he that is dead is freed from sin.
vs.e: Because he who is dead is free from sin.
vs.w: For he who has died has been freed from sin.

lessons.note: Naos is the inner sanctuary, the holiest place where God's presence dwelt. Now that place is you. The same Spirit who raised Jesus from the dead lives in you.
lessons.reflect: How does knowing God lives in you change how you treat your body and mind?
lessons.declare: My body is the temple of the Holy Spirit. The Spirit of the risen Christ lives in me.

vs.t: Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?
vs.e: Do you not see that you are God's holy house, and that the Spirit of God has his place in you?
vs.w: Don’t you know that you are a temple of God, and that God’s Spirit lives in you?

vs.t: For ye are bought with a price: therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.
vs.e: For a payment has been made for you: let God be honoured in your body.
vs.w: for you were bought with a price. Therefore glorify God in your body and in your spirit, which are God’s.

vs.t: But if the Spirit of him that raised up Jesus from the dead dwell in you, he that raised up Christ from the dead shall also quicken your mortal bodies by his Spirit that dwelleth in you.

vs.w: But if the Spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwells in you, he who raised up Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through his Spirit who dwells in you.

lessons.note: Hupernikao means to win an overwhelming victory. Not barely surviving, but prevailing completely through Him who loved us. Greater is He that is in you than he that is in the world.

vs.w: and if children, then heirs: heirs of God and joint heirs with Christ, if indeed we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified with him.

vs.w: So you are no longer a bondservant, but a son; and if a son, then an heir of God through Christ.

vs.w: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his great mercy caused us to be born again to a living hope through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead,

intro: God reveals who He is through His names and His nature. Explore His titles in the original Hebrew and Greek and the verses where He made Himself known.

lessons.title: Elohim: The Mighty Creator
lessons.note: Elohim is the first name of God in the Bible. It speaks of strength and might, and its plural form hints at the fullness of the Godhead ("Let US make man"). He is the Creator of all.
lessons.reflect: If Elohim created everything out of nothing, what can He create in your situation?
lessons.declare: My God is Elohim, the mighty Creator of heaven and earth.

vs.t: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.
vs.e: At the first God made the heaven and the earth.
vs.w: In the beginning, God created the heavens and the earth.

vs.t: And God said, Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the fowl of the air, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.
vs.e: And God said, Let us make man in our image, like us: and let him have rule over the fish of the sea and over the birds of the air and over the cattle and over all the earth and over every living thing which goes flat on the earth.
vs.w: God said, “Let’s make man in our image, after our likeness. Let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the livestock, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.”

vs.t: So God created man in his own image, in the image of God created he him; male and female created he them.
vs.e: And God made man in his image, in the image of God he made him: male and female he made them.
vs.w: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.

vs.w: Haven’t you known? Haven’t you heard? The everlasting God, Yahweh, the Creator of the ends of the earth, doesn’t faint. He isn’t weary. His understanding is unsearchable.

lessons.note: When your KJV prints LORD in capitals, the Hebrew is YHWH, God's personal covenant name. It comes from the verb "to be": the self-existent, ever-present One who keeps His promises.
lessons.reflect: God gave His personal name to His people. What does that tell you about the relationship He wants?
lessons.declare: The LORD, the great I AM, is my God, and He keeps His covenant.

vs.e: And God said to Moses, I am Yahweh:
vs.w: God spoke to Moses, and said to him, “I am Yahweh.

vs.t: And I appeared unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, by the name of God Almighty, but by my name Jehovah was I not known to them.
vs.e: I let myself be seen by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, as God, the Ruler of all; but they had no knowledge of my name Yahweh.
vs.w: I appeared to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, as God Almighty; but by my name Yahweh I was not known to them.

vs.t: That men may know that thou, whose name alone is Jehovah, art the most high over all the earth.
vs.e: So that men may see that you only, whose name is Yahweh, are Most High over all the earth.
vs.w: that they may know that you alone, whose name is Yahweh, are the Most High over all the earth.

lessons.title: Adonai: My Lord and Master
lessons.note: Adonai (printed "Lord" with lower-case letters) means Master or Owner. Calling God Adonai is a statement of surrender: He leads and I follow.
lessons.reflect: What does calling God "my Lord" ask you to hand over?
lessons.declare: You are Adonai, my Lord and Master. I yield to You.

vs.t: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David. O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.
vs.e: O Lord, our Lord, whose glory is higher than the heavens, how noble is your name in all the earth!
vs.w: Yahweh, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens!

vs.t: In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.
vs.e: In the year of King Uzziah's death I saw the Lord seated in his place, high and lifted up, and the Temple was full of the wide skirts of his robe.
vs.w: In the year that king Uzziah died, I saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.

vs.t: And Abram said, Lord God, what wilt thou give me, seeing I go childless, and the steward of my house is this Eliezer of Damascus?
vs.e: And Abram said, What will you give me? for I have no child and this Eliezer of Damascus will have all my wealth after me.
vs.w: Abram said, “Lord Yahweh, what will you give me, since I go childless, and he who will inherit my estate is Eliezer of Damascus?”

lessons.memtext: To the chief Musician upon Gittith, A Psalm of David. O Lord our Lord, how excellent is thy name in all the earth! who hast set thy glory above the heavens.
lessons.memE: O Lord, our Lord, whose glory is higher than the heavens, how noble is your name in all the earth!
lessons.memW: Yahweh, our Lord, how majestic is your name in all the earth! You have set your glory above the heavens!

H136: the Lord (used as a proper name of God only)
H113: lord, master, owner. Compare also names beginning with 'Adoni-'.
or (shortened) אָדֹן; from an unused root (meaning to rule);

lessons.title: El Shaddai: God Almighty
lessons.note: God revealed Himself to Abraham as El Shaddai when the promise looked impossible. He is the Almighty, all-sufficient God. In the New Testament the Greek is Pantokrator, ruler over all.
lessons.reflect: Which "impossible" promise do you need El Shaddai for?
lessons.declare: My God is El Shaddai, God Almighty. Nothing is too hard for Him.

vs.t: And when Abram was ninety years old and nine, the Lord appeared to Abram, and said unto him, I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.
vs.e: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the Lord came to him, and said, I am God, Ruler of all; go in my ways and be upright in all things,
vs.w: When Abram was ninety-nine years old, Yahweh appeared to Abram and said to him, “I am God Almighty. Walk before me and be blameless.

vs.t: And God said unto him, I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins;
vs.e: And God said to him, I am God, the Ruler of all: be fertile, and have increase; a nation, truly a group of nations, will come from you, and kings will be your offspring;
vs.w: God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body.

vs.t: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
vs.e: Happy is he whose resting-place is in the secret of the Lord, and under the shade of the wings of the Most High;
vs.w: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

lessons.title: El Elyon: The Most High God
lessons.note: El Elyon means the Most High: no one and nothing is above Him. Kings rise and fall, but His dominion is everlasting. Those who dwell in His secret place abide under His shadow.
lessons.reflect: What is trying to sit higher than God in your life right now?
lessons.declare: The Most High God is my refuge and my fortress.

vs.t: And Melchizedek king of Salem brought forth bread and wine: and he was the priest of the most high God.
vs.e: And Melchizedek, king of Salem, the priest of the Most High God, took bread and wine,
vs.w: Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine. He was priest of God Most High.

vs.t: And he blessed him, and said, Blessed be Abram of the most high God, possessor of heaven and earth:
vs.e: And blessing him, said, May the blessing of the Most High God, maker of heaven and earth, be on Abram:
vs.w: He blessed him, and said, “Blessed be Abram of God Most High, possessor of heaven and earth.

vs.t: And blessed be the most high God, which hath delivered thine enemies into thy hand. And he gave him tithes of all.
vs.e: And let the Most High God be praised, who has given into your hands those who were against you. Then Abram gave him a tenth of all the goods he had taken.
vs.w: Blessed be God Most High, who has delivered your enemies into your hand.” Abram gave him a tenth of all.

vs.t: He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
vs.e: Happy is he whose resting-place is in the secret of the Lord, and under the shade of the wings of the Most High;
vs.w: He who dwells in the secret place of the Most High will rest in the shadow of the Almighty.

vs.t: I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust.
vs.e: Who says of the Lord, He is my safe place and my tower of strength: he is my God, in whom is my hope.
vs.w: I will say of Yahweh, “He is my refuge and my fortress; my God, in whom I trust.”

vs.t: And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:
vs.e: And at the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifting up my eyes to heaven, got back my reason, and, blessing the Most High, I gave praise and honour to him who is living for ever, whose rule is an eternal rule and whose kingdom goes on from generation to generation.
vs.w: At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

lessons.memtext: And at the end of the days I Nebuchadnezzar lifted up mine eyes unto heaven, and mine understanding returned unto me, and I blessed the most High, and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation:
lessons.memE: And at the end of the days, I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifting up my eyes to heaven, got back my reason, and, blessing the Most High, I gave praise and honour to him who is living for ever, whose rule is an eternal rule and whose kingdom goes on from generation to generation.
lessons.memW: At the end of the days I, Nebuchadnezzar, lifted up my eyes to heaven, and my understanding returned to me, and I blessed the Most High, and I praised and honored him who lives forever; for his dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom from generation to generation.

H5945: an elevation, i.e. (adj.) lofty (compar.); as title, the Supreme
H410: strength; as adjective, mighty; especially the Almighty (but used also of any deity)
God (god), [idiom] goodly, [idiom] great, idol, might(-y one), power, strong. Compare names in '-el.'

lessons.title: El Roi: The God Who Sees
lessons.note: Hagar, a runaway slave in the desert, was the one who named God El Roi: "Thou God seest me." No one is invisible to Him. He sees the overlooked and comes to them.
lessons.reflect: Where do you feel unseen? Hear El Roi say, "I see you."
lessons.declare: You are El Roi, the God who sees me. I am never unseen.

vs.t: And she called the name of the Lord that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?
vs.e: And to the Lord who was talking with her she gave this name, You are a God who is seen; for she said, Have I not even here in the waste land had a vision of God and am still living?
vs.w: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”

vs.t: Behold, the eye of the Lord is upon them that fear him, upon them that hope in his mercy;
vs.e: See, the eye of the Lord is on those in whose hearts is the fear of him, on those whose hope is in his mercy;
vs.w: Behold, Yahweh’s eye is on those who fear him, on those who hope in his loving kindness,

vs.t: For the eyes of the Lord run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to shew himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. Herein thou hast done foolishly: therefore from henceforth thou shalt have wars.
vs.e: For the eyes of the Lord go this way and that, through all the earth, letting it be seen that he is the strong support of those whose hearts are true to him. In this you have done foolishly, for from now you will have wars.
vs.w: For Yahweh’s eyes run back and forth throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him. You have done foolishly in this; for from now on you will have wars.”

lessons.memtext: And she called the name of the Lord that spake unto her, Thou God seest me: for she said, Have I also here looked after him that seeth me?
lessons.memE: And to the Lord who was talking with her she gave this name, You are a God who is seen; for she said, Have I not even here in the waste land had a vision of God and am still living?
lessons.memW: She called the name of Yahweh who spoke to her, “You are a God who sees,” for she said, “Have I even stayed alive after seeing him?”

lessons.title: Jehovah Jireh: The LORD Will Provide
lessons.note: On Mount Moriah God provided a ram in place of Isaac. The name literally means "the LORD will see (to it)". He sees the need ahead of time and provides, ultimately in His own Son.
lessons.reflect: What need can you place in the hands of Jehovah Jireh today?
lessons.declare: The LORD is my provider. He has already seen what I need.

vs.t: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
vs.e: And Abraham said, God himself will give the lamb for the burned offering: so they went on together.
vs.w: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.

vs.t: And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns: and Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.
vs.e: And lifting up his eyes, Abraham saw a sheep fixed by its horns in the brushwood: and Abraham took the sheep and made a burned offering of it in place of his son.
vs.w: Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and saw that behind him was a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt offering instead of his son.

vs.t: And Abraham called the name of that place Jehovah–jireh: as it is said to this day, In the mount of the Lord it shall be seen.
vs.e: And Abraham gave that place the name Yahweh-yireh: as it is said to this day, In the mountain the Lord is seen.
vs.w: Abraham called the name of that place “Yahweh Will Provide”. As it is said to this day, “On Yahweh’s mountain, it will be provided.”

vs.t: But my God shall supply all your need according to his riches in glory by Christ Jesus.
vs.e: And my God will give you all you have need of from the wealth of his glory in Christ Jesus.
vs.w: My God will supply every need of yours according to his riches in glory in Christ Jesus.

lessons.memtext: And Abraham said, My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering: so they went both of them together.
lessons.memE: And Abraham said, God himself will give the lamb for the burned offering: so they went on together.
lessons.memW: Abraham said, “God will provide himself the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So they both went together.

lessons.title: Jehovah Rapha: The LORD Who Heals
lessons.note: Rapha means to mend, cure or make whole. The LORD heals bodies, broken hearts and nations. He binds up our wounds.
lessons.reflect: What area of your life (body, heart, relationship) needs the touch of the Healer?
lessons.declare: You are Jehovah Rapha, the LORD who heals me.

vs.t: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.
vs.e: And he said, If with all your heart you will give attention to the voice of the Lord your God, and do what is right in his eyes, giving ear to his orders and keeping his laws, I will not put on you any of the diseases which I put on the Egyptians: for I am the Lord your life-giver.
vs.w: He said, “If you will diligently listen to Yahweh your God’s voice, and will do that which is right in his eyes, and will pay attention to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of the diseases on you, which I have put on the Egyptians; for I am Yahweh who heals you.”

vs.t: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and forget not all his benefits:
vs.e: Give praise to the Lord, O my soul; let not all his blessings go from your memory.
vs.w: Praise Yahweh, my soul, and don’t forget all his benefits,

vs.t: Who forgiveth all thine iniquities; who healeth all thy diseases;
vs.e: He has forgiveness for all your sins; he takes away all your diseases;
vs.w: who forgives all your sins, who heals all your diseases,

vs.t: He healeth the broken in heart, and bindeth up their wounds.
vs.e: He makes the broken-hearted well, and puts oil on their wounds.
vs.w: He heals the broken in heart, and binds up their wounds.

lessons.memtext: And said, If thou wilt diligently hearken to the voice of the Lord thy God, and wilt do that which is right in his sight, and wilt give ear to his commandments, and keep all his statutes, I will put none of these diseases upon thee, which I have brought upon the Egyptians: for I am the Lord that healeth thee.

H7495: properly, to mend (by stitching), i.e. (figuratively) to cure
cure, (cause to) heal, physician, repair, [idiom] thoroughly, make whole. See H7503 (רָפָה).

lessons.title: Jehovah Nissi: The LORD My Banner
lessons.note: After victory over Amalek, Moses built an altar and called it Jehovah Nissi. A banner was the rallying flag in battle. The LORD is the One we gather under, and the One who wins.
lessons.reflect: Under whose banner are you fighting your battles?
lessons.declare: The LORD is my banner. The victory belongs to Him.

vs.t: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi:
vs.e: Then Moses put up an altar and gave it the name of Yahweh-nissi:
vs.w: Moses built an altar, and called its name “Yahweh our Banner”.

vs.t: And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.
vs.e: And in that day, the eyes of the nations will be turned to the root of Jesse which will be lifted up as the flag of the peoples; and his resting-place will be glory.
vs.w: It will happen in that day that the nations will seek the root of Jesse, who stands as a banner of the peoples; and his resting place will be glorious.

vs.t: But thanks be to God, which giveth us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.
vs.e: But praise be to God who gives us strength to overcome through our Lord Jesus Christ.
vs.w: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory through our Lord Jesus Christ.

lessons.memtext: And Moses built an altar, and called the name of it JEHOVAH–nissi:
lessons.memE: Then Moses put up an altar and gave it the name of Yahweh-nissi:

lessons.title: Jehovah Shalom: The LORD Is Peace
lessons.note: Gideon was afraid and hiding when God met him. Shalom is more than calm: it means wholeness, completeness, nothing missing and nothing broken. Jesus gives a peace the world cannot.
lessons.reflect: What is stealing your peace? Bring it to Jehovah Shalom.
lessons.declare: The LORD is my peace. I am kept in perfect peace as I trust Him.

vs.t: And the Lord said unto him, Peace be unto thee; fear not: thou shalt not die.
vs.e: But the Lord said to him, Peace be with you; have no fear: you are in no danger of death.
vs.w: Yahweh said to him, “Peace be to you! Don’t be afraid. You shall not die.”

vs.t: Then Gideon built an altar there unto the Lord, and called it Jehovah–shalom: unto this day it is yet in Ophrah of the Abi–ezrites.
vs.e: Then Gideon made an altar there to the Lord, and gave it the name Yahweh-shalom; to this day it is in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.
vs.w: Then Gideon built an altar there to Yahweh, and called it “Yahweh is Peace.” To this day it is still in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

vs.t: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
vs.e: The man whose heart is unmoved you will keep in peace, because his hope is in you.
vs.w: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.

vs.t: Peace I leave with you, my peace I give unto you: not as the world giveth, give I unto you. Let not your heart be troubled, neither let it be afraid.
vs.e: May peace be with you; my peace I give to you: I give it not as the world gives. Let not your heart be troubled; let it be without fear.
vs.w: Peace I leave with you. My peace I give to you; not as the world gives, I give to you. Don’t let your heart be troubled, neither let it be fearful.

lessons.memtext: Thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee.
lessons.memE: The man whose heart is unmoved you will keep in peace, because his hope is in you.
lessons.memW: You will keep whoever’s mind is steadfast in perfect peace, because he trusts in you.

lessons.title: Jehovah Rohi: The LORD My Shepherd
lessons.note: Ra'ah means to tend, feed and lead a flock. David, a shepherd himself, knew what it meant: guidance, provision, protection and rest. Jesus is the Good Shepherd who lays down His life.
lessons.reflect: Where do you need the Shepherd to lead you right now?
lessons.declare: The LORD is my shepherd. I shall not want.

vs.t: A Psalm of David. The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
vs.e: The Lord takes care of me as his sheep; I will not be without any good thing.
vs.w: Yahweh is my shepherd: I shall lack nothing.

vs.t: He maketh me to lie down in green pastures: he leadeth me beside the still waters.
vs.e: He makes a resting-place for me in the green fields: he is my guide by the quiet waters.
vs.w: He makes me lie down in green pastures. He leads me beside still waters.

vs.t: He restoreth my soul: he leadeth me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.
vs.e: He gives new life to my soul: he is my guide in the ways of righteousness because of his name.
vs.w: He restores my soul. He guides me in the paths of righteousness for his name’s sake.

vs.t: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.
vs.e: He will give food to his flock like a keeper of sheep; with his arm he will get it together, and will take up the lambs on his breast, gently guiding those which are with young.
vs.w: He will feed his flock like a shepherd. He will gather the lambs in his arm, and carry them in his bosom. He will gently lead those who have their young.

vs.t: I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.
vs.e: I am the good keeper of sheep: the good keeper gives his life for the sheep.
vs.w: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.

lessons.memtext: He shall feed his flock like a shepherd: he shall gather the lambs with his arm, and carry them in his bosom, and shall gently lead those that are with young.

lessons.title: Jehovah Tsidkenu: The LORD Our Righteousness
lessons.note: Jeremiah prophesied a righteous Branch from David whose name would be "THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS". That is Jesus, who is made unto us righteousness.
lessons.reflect: Where are you trying to be your own righteousness?
lessons.declare: The LORD is my righteousness.

vs.t: Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.
vs.e: See, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will give to David a true Branch, and he will be ruling as king, acting wisely, doing what is right, and judging uprightly in the land.
vs.w: “Behold, the days come,” says Yahweh, “that I will raise to David a righteous Branch, and he will reign as king and deal wisely, and will execute justice and righteousness in the land.

vs.t: In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell safely: and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS.
vs.e: In his days Judah will have salvation and Israel will be living without fear: and this is the name by which he will be named, The Lord is our righteousness.
vs.w: In his days Judah will be saved, and Israel will dwell safely. This is his name by which he will be called: Yahweh our righteousness.

vs.t: But of him are ye in Christ Jesus, who of God is made unto us wisdom, and righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption:
vs.e: But God has given you a place in Christ Jesus, through whom God has given us wisdom and righteousness and salvation, and made us holy:
vs.w: Because of him, you are in Christ Jesus, who was made to us wisdom from God, and righteousness and sanctification, and redemption:

lessons.note: Abba is the Aramaic word Jesus used in Gethsemane. It is the warm, trusting word a child uses for a father. Through Jesus, we are invited to use it too.
lessons.reflect: Do you relate to God more as Judge, Boss or Father?

lessons.note: Holy (qadosh) means set apart, utterly pure, different from everything else. It is the only quality of God repeated three times in a row in Scripture. And He calls us to be holy too.

lessons.title: God Is Love
lessons.note: God does not just have love; He IS love. Agape is self-giving love that chooses the good of the other, even at great cost. God proved it while we were still sinners.
lessons.reflect: How has God shown His love to you personally?
lessons.declare: God is love, and nothing can separate me from His love.

vs.t: He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love.
vs.e: He who has no love has no knowledge of God, because God is love.
vs.w: He who doesn’t love doesn’t know God, for God is love.

vs.t: In this was manifested the love of God toward us, because that God sent his only begotten Son into the world, that we might live through him.
vs.e: And the love of God was made clear to us when he sent his only Son into the world so that we might have life through him.
vs.w: By this God’s love was revealed in us, that God has sent his one and only Son into the world that we might live through him.

vs.t: Herein is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son to be the propitiation for our sins.
vs.e: And this is love, not that we had love for God, but that he had love for us, and sent his Son to be an offering for our sins.
vs.w: In this is love, not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his Son as the atoning sacrifice for our sins.

vs.t: And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him.
vs.e: And we have seen and had faith in the love which God has for us. God is love, and everyone who has love is in God, and God is in him.
vs.w: We know and have believed the love which God has for us. God is love, and he who remains in love remains in God, and God remains in him.

vs.t: But God commendeth his love toward us, in that, while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

vs.w: But God commends his own love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.

vs.w: It is because of Yahweh’s loving kindnesses that we are not consumed, because his compassion doesn’t fail.

vs.t: They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

lessons.title: God Never Changes
lessons.note: "I am the LORD, I change not." People, moods and circumstances shift, but God has no variation or shadow of turning. What He promised, He will do.
lessons.reflect: What changing thing have you been relying on more than the unchanging God?
lessons.declare: My God never changes. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.

vs.w: “For I, Yahweh, don’t change; therefore you, sons of Jacob, are not consumed.

vs.w: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of lights, with whom can be no variation, nor turning shadow.

lessons.title: God Knows All Things
lessons.note: Yada means to know closely and personally, not just facts. God knows your sitting and rising, your words before you speak them, even the number of hairs on your head, and He still loves you.
lessons.reflect: Does being fully known by God feel frightening or comforting? Why?
lessons.declare: God knows me completely and loves me completely.

vs.t: To the chief Musician, A Psalm of David. O Lord, thou hast searched me, and known me.
vs.e: O Lord, you have knowledge of me, searching out all my secrets.
vs.w: Yahweh, you have searched me, and you know me.

vs.t: Thou knowest my downsitting and mine uprising, thou understandest my thought afar off.
vs.e: You have knowledge when I am seated and when I get up, you see my thoughts from far away.
vs.w: You know my sitting down and my rising up. You perceive my thoughts from afar.

vs.t: Thou compassest my path and my lying down, and art acquainted with all my ways.
vs.e: You keep watch over my steps and my sleep, and have knowledge of all my ways.
vs.w: You search out my path and my lying down, and are acquainted with all my ways.

vs.t: For there is not a word in my tongue, but, lo, O Lord, thou knowest it altogether.
vs.e: For there is not a word on my tongue which is not clear to you, O Lord.
vs.w: For there is not a word on my tongue, but, behold, Yahweh, you know it altogether.

vs.t: Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
vs.e: And there is nothing made which is not completely clear to him; there is nothing covered, but all things are open to the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
vs.w: There is no creature that is hidden from his sight, but all things are naked and laid open before the eyes of him to whom we must give an account.

vs.t: But the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
vs.e: But the hairs of your head are all numbered.
vs.w: but the very hairs of your head are all numbered.

vs.t: Fear ye not therefore, ye are of more value than many sparrows.
vs.e: Then have no fear; you are of more value than a flock of sparrows.
vs.w: Therefore don’t be afraid. You are of more value than many sparrows.

lessons.note: "Whither shall I flee from thy presence?" (paniym: face, presence). Heaven, the grave, the far side of the sea: He is there. In Him we live and move and have our being.
lessons.reflect: Where are you today? God is there with you.
lessons.declare: There is nowhere I can go where God is not with me.

vs.t: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?
vs.e: Where may I go from your spirit? how may I go in flight from you?
vs.w: Where could I go from your Spirit? Or where could I flee from your presence?

vs.t: If I ascend up into heaven, thou art there: if I make my bed in hell, behold, thou art there.
vs.e: If I go up to heaven, you are there: or if I make my bed in the underworld, you are there.
vs.w: If I ascend up into heaven, you are there. If I make my bed in Sheol, behold, you are there!

vs.t: If I take the wings of the morning, and dwell in the uttermost parts of the sea;

vs.w: If I take the wings of the dawn, and settle in the uttermost parts of the sea,

vs.t: Even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me.
vs.e: Even there will I be guided by your hand, and your right hand will keep me.

vs.t: Am I a God at hand, saith the Lord, and not a God afar off?

vs.w: “Am I a God at hand,” says Yahweh, “and not a God afar off?

vs.t: Can any hide himself in secret places that I shall not see him? saith the Lord. Do not I fill heaven and earth? saith the Lord.

vs.w: Can anyone hide himself in secret places so that I can’t see him?” says Yahweh. “Don’t I fill heaven and earth?” says Yahweh.

vs.t: That they should seek the Lord, if haply they might feel after him, and find him, though he be not far from every one of us:

vs.w: that they should seek the Lord, if perhaps they might reach out for him and find him, though he is not far from each one of us.

lessons.title: God Is Eternal
lessons.note: Olam points to time out of sight: before the mountains were formed and beyond any end we can imagine. The eternal God does not get tired or weary.
lessons.reflect: How does God's eternity put today's worries into perspective?
lessons.declare: From everlasting to everlasting, You are God.

vs.t: Before the mountains were brought forth, or ever thou hadst formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, thou art God.
vs.e: Before the mountains were made, before you had given birth to the earth and the world, before time was, and for ever, you are God.
vs.w: Before the mountains were born, before you had formed the earth and the world, even from everlasting to everlasting, you are God.

vs.t: Hast thou not known? hast thou not heard, that the everlasting God, the Lord, the Creator of the ends of the earth, fainteth not, neither is weary? there is no searching of his understanding.
vs.e: Have you no knowledge of it? has it not come to your ears? The eternal God, the Lord, the Maker of the ends of the earth, is never feeble or tired; there is no searching out of his wisdom.

lessons.title: Ambassadors for Christ

vs.t: To wit, that God was in Christ, reconciling the world unto himself, not imputing their trespasses unto them; and hath committed unto us the word of reconciliation.
vs.e: That is, that God was in Christ making peace between the world and himself, not putting their sins to their account, and having given to us the preaching of this news of peace.
vs.w: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to himself, not reckoning to them their trespasses, and having committed to us the word of reconciliation.

vs.t: Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us: we pray you in Christ’s stead, be ye reconciled to God.
vs.e: So we are the representatives of Christ, as if God was making a request to you through us: we make our request to you, in the name of Christ, be at peace with God.
vs.w: We are therefore ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were entreating by us: we beg you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.

lessons.note: Jesus went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed. He promised that those who believe would do the works He did, because He went to the Father and sent the Spirit.
lessons.reflect: What "good" is God asking you to go about doing in your community?
lessons.declare: I believe in Jesus, so I do the works that He did.

vs.t: Verily, verily, I say unto you, He that believeth on me, the works that I do shall he do also; and greater works than these shall he do; because I go unto my Father.
vs.e: Truly I say to you, He who puts his faith in me will do the very works which I do, and he will do greater things than these, because I am going to my Father.
vs.w: Most certainly I tell you, he who believes in me, the works that I do, he will do also; and he will do greater works than these, because I am going to my Father.

vs.t: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.
vs.e: About Jesus of Nazareth, how God gave the Holy Spirit to him, with power: and how he went about doing good and making well all who were troubled by evil spirits, for God was with him.
vs.w: even Jesus of Nazareth, how God anointed him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.

vs.t: And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues;
vs.e: And these signs will be with those who have faith: in my name they will send out evil spirits; and they will make use of new languages;
vs.w: These signs will accompany those who believe: in my name they will cast out demons; they will speak with new languages;

vs.t: They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.
vs.e: They will take up snakes, and if there is poison in their drink, it will do them no evil; they will put their hands on those who are ill, and they will get well.
vs.w: they will take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it will in no way hurt them; they will lay hands on the sick, and they will recover.”

vs.t: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.
vs.e: Make well those who are ill, give life to the dead, make lepers clean, send evil spirits out of men; freely it has been given to you, freely give.
vs.w: Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, and cast out demons. Freely you received, so freely give.

lessons.title: Bear Much Fruit
lessons.note: Fruit is not forced; it grows from connection. Abide (meno: remain, stay) in Jesus and fruit follows: love, joy, peace and the rest. This is how the Father is glorified.
lessons.reflect: Which fruit of the Spirit do you most want to grow right now?
lessons.declare: I abide in Christ and I bear much fruit to the glory of the Father.

vs.t: Abide in me, and I in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself, except it abide in the vine; no more can ye, except ye abide in me.
vs.e: Be in me at all times as I am in you. As the branch is not able to give fruit of itself, if it is not still on the vine, so you are not able to do so if you are not in me.
vs.w: Remain in me, and I in you. As the branch can’t bear fruit by itself unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you, unless you remain in me.

vs.t: I am the vine, ye are the branches: He that abideth in me, and I in him, the same bringeth forth much fruit: for without me ye can do nothing.
vs.e: I am the vine, you are the branches: he who is in me at all times as I am in him, gives much fruit, because without me you are able to do nothing.
vs.w: I am the vine. You are the branches. He who remains in me and I in him bears much fruit, for apart from me you can do nothing.

vs.t: Herein is my Father glorified, that ye bear much fruit; so shall ye be my disciples.
vs.e: Here is my Father's glory, in that you give much fruit and so are my true disciples.
vs.w: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.

vs.t: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith,
vs.e: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, a quiet mind, kind acts, well-doing, faith,
vs.w: But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith,

vs.t: Meekness, temperance: against such there is no law.
vs.e: Gentle behaviour, control over desires: against such there is no law.
vs.w: gentleness, and self-control. Against such things there is no law.

lessons.memE: Here is my Father's glory, in that you give much fruit and so are my true disciples.
lessons.memW: “In this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit; and so you will be my disciples.

lessons.title: Let Your Light Shine
lessons.note: Your good works are meant to be seen, not to make you look good but to point people to your Father. In a crooked world you shine as lights.
lessons.reflect: Where is your light hidden "under a bushel" right now?
lessons.declare: I arise and shine. My good works bring glory to my Father.

vs.t: Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.
vs.e: Even so let your light be shining before men, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father in heaven.
vs.w: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

vs.t: Do all things without murmurings and disputings:
vs.e: Do all things without protests and arguments;
vs.w: Do all things without complaining and arguing,

vs.t: That ye may be blameless and harmless, the sons of God, without rebuke, in the midst of a crooked and perverse nation, among whom ye shine as lights in the world;
vs.e: So that you may be holy and gentle, children of God without sin in a twisted and foolish generation, among whom you are seen as lights in the world,
vs.w: that you may become blameless and harmless, children of God without defect in the middle of a crooked and perverse generation, among whom you are seen as lights in the world,

vs.t: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.
vs.e: Up! let your face be bright, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord is shining on you.
vs.w: “Arise, shine; for your light has come, and Yahweh’s glory has risen on you.

lessons.memW: Even so, let your light shine before men; that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven.

lessons.title: Care for the Least
lessons.note: Jesus counts what we do for the hungry, the stranger, the sick and the prisoner as done to Him. God asks us to do justly, love mercy and walk humbly, and to speak up for those who cannot.
lessons.reflect: Who are "the least" around you? How can you serve them as unto Christ?
lessons.declare: What I do for the least, I do for Jesus.

vs.t: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in:
vs.e: For I was in need of food, and you gave it to me: I was in need of drink, and you gave it to me: I was wandering, and you took me in;
vs.w: for I was hungry, and you gave me food to eat. I was thirsty, and you gave me drink. I was a stranger, and you took me in.

vs.t: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me.
vs.e: I had no clothing, and you gave it to me: when I was ill, or in prison, you came to me.
vs.w: I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.’

vs.t: Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink?
vs.e: Then will the upright make answer to him, saying, Lord, when did we see you in need of food, and give it to you? or in need of drink, and give it to you?
vs.w: “Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry, and feed you; or thirsty, and give you a drink?

vs.t: When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee?
vs.e: And when did we see you wandering, and take you in? or without clothing, and give it to you?
vs.w: When did we see you as a stranger, and take you in; or naked, and clothe you?

vs.t: Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee?
vs.e: And when did we see you ill, or in prison, and come to you?
vs.w: When did we see you sick, or in prison, and come to you?’

vs.t: And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
vs.e: And the King will make answer and say to them, Truly I say to you, Because you did it to the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.
vs.w: “The King will answer them, ‘Most certainly I tell you, because you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’

vs.t: Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.
vs.e: The religion which is holy and free from evil in the eyes of our God and Father is this: to take care of children who have no fathers and of widows who are in trouble, and to keep oneself untouched by the world.
vs.w: Pure religion and undefiled before our God and Father is this: to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep oneself unstained by the world.

vs.t: He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth the Lord require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?
vs.e: He has made clear to you, O man, what is good; and what is desired from you by the Lord; only doing what is right, and loving mercy, and walking without pride before your God.
vs.w: He has shown you, O man, what is good. What does Yahweh require of you, but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God?

vs.t: Open thy mouth for the dumb in the cause of all such as are appointed to destruction.
vs.e: Let your mouth be open for those who have no voice, in the cause of those who are ready for death.
vs.w: Open your mouth for the mute, in the cause of all who are left desolate.

vs.t: Open thy mouth, judge righteously, and plead the cause of the poor and needy.
vs.e: Let your mouth be open, judging rightly, and give right decisions in the cause of the poor and those in need.
vs.w: Open your mouth, judge righteously, and serve justice to the poor and needy.”

lessons.title: Use Your Gifts
lessons.note: Charisma means a gift of grace. Every believer has received at least one, not for show but to serve others. You are a steward, a manager of what belongs to God.
lessons.reflect: What gifts has God given you, and how are you using them to serve?
lessons.declare: I use the gifts God has given me to serve others and glorify Him.

vs.t: Having then gifts differing according to the grace that is given to us, whether prophecy, let us prophesy according to the proportion of faith;
vs.e: And having different qualities by reason of the grace given to us, such as the quality of a prophet, let it be made use of in relation to the measure of our faith;
vs.w: having gifts differing according to the grace that was given to us: if prophecy, let’s prophesy according to the proportion of our faith;

vs.t: Or ministry, let us wait on our ministering: or he that teacheth, on teaching;
vs.e: Or the position of a Deacon of the church, let a man give himself to it; or he who has the power of teaching, let him make use of it;
vs.w: or service, let’s give ourselves to service; or he who teaches, to his teaching;

vs.t: Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giveth, let him do it with simplicity; he that ruleth, with diligence; he that sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.
vs.e: He who has the power of comforting, let him do so; he who gives, let him give freely; he who has the power of ruling, let him do it with a serious mind; he who has mercy on others, let it be with joy.
vs.w: or he who exhorts, to his exhorting; he who gives, let him do it with generosity; he who rules, with diligence; he who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.

vs.t: As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.
vs.e: Making distribution among one another of whatever has been given to you, like true servants of the unmeasured grace of God;
vs.w: As each has received a gift, employ it in serving one another, as good managers of the grace of God in its various forms.

vs.t: If any man speak, let him speak as the oracles of God; if any man minister, let him do it as of the ability which God giveth: that God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom be praise and dominion for ever and ever. Amen.
vs.e: If anyone has anything to say, let it be as the words of God; if anyone has the desire to be the servant of others, let him do it in the strength which is given by God; so that in all things God may have the glory through Jesus Christ, whose are the glory and the power for ever.
vs.w: If anyone speaks, let it be as it were the very words of God. If anyone serves, let it be as of the strength which God supplies, that in all things God may be glorified through Jesus Christ, to whom belong the glory and the dominion forever and ever. Amen.

vs.t: But the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal.
vs.e: But to every man some form of the Spirit's working is given for the common good.
vs.w: But to each one is given the manifestation of the Spirit for the profit of all.

lessons.title: Pray and Intercede
lessons.note: Prayer is not the least we can do; it is part of the work itself. God looks for people who will stand in the gap for others: for leaders, families and nations.
lessons.reflect: Who has God put on your heart to pray for regularly?
lessons.declare: I stand in the gap in prayer, and my prayers avail much.

vs.t: I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men;
vs.e: My desire is, first of all, that you will make requests and prayers and give praise for all men;
vs.w: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks be made for all men:

vs.t: For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
vs.e: For kings and all those in authority; so that we may have a calm and quiet life in all fear of God and serious behaviour.
vs.w: for kings and all who are in high places, that we may lead a tranquil and quiet life in all godliness and reverence.

vs.t: Praying always with all prayer and supplication in the Spirit, and watching thereunto with all perseverance and supplication for all saints;
vs.e: With prayers and deep desires, making requests at all times in the Spirit, and keeping watch, with strong purpose, in prayer for all the saints,
vs.w: with all prayer and requests, praying at all times in the Spirit, and being watchful to this end in all perseverance and requests for all the saints:

vs.t: Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
vs.e: So then, make a statement of your sins to one another, and say prayers for one another so that you may be made well. The prayer of a good man is full of power in its working.
vs.w: Confess your offenses to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

vs.t: And I sought for a man among them, that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it: but I found none.
vs.e: And I was looking for a man among them who would make up the wall and take his station in the broken place before me for the land, so that I might not send destruction on it: but there was no one.
vs.w: “I sought for a man among them who would build up the wall and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I would not destroy it; but I found no one.

lessons.title: Walk as He Walked
lessons.note: Peripateo means to walk around, to conduct your daily life. Following Jesus is not just Sunday activity; it is how we walk every day, following in His steps.
lessons.reflect: What is one daily habit that could help you walk more like Jesus?
lessons.declare: I walk as Jesus walked, following in His steps.

vs.t: He that saith he abideth in him ought himself also so to walk, even as he walked.
vs.e: He who says that he is living in him, will do as he did.
vs.w: he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.

vs.t: Be ye therefore followers of God, as dear children;
vs.e: Let it then be your desire to be like God, as well-loved children;
vs.w: Be therefore imitators of God, as beloved children.

vs.t: And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.
vs.e: And be living in love, even as Christ had love for you, and gave himself up for us, an offering to God for a perfume of a sweet smell.
vs.w: Walk in love, even as Christ also loved us and gave himself up for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweet-smelling fragrance.

vs.t: For even hereunto were ye called: because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that ye should follow his steps:
vs.e: This is God's purpose for you: because Jesus himself underwent punishment for you, giving you an example, so that you might go in his footsteps:
vs.w: For you were called to this, because Christ also suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his steps,

lessons.memE: He who says that he is living in him, will do as he did.
lessons.memW: he who says he remains in him ought himself also to walk just like he walked.

lessons.title: Endure and Finish Well
lessons.note: Hupomone is patient endurance: staying under the load and not giving up. Your labour in the Lord is never in vain. Keep your eyes on Jesus, the author and finisher of your faith.
lessons.reflect: Where are you tempted to give up? What would finishing well look like?
lessons.declare: I will not grow weary in well doing. I will finish my race.

vs.t: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
vs.e: And let us not get tired of well-doing; for at the right time we will get in the grain, if we do not give way to weariness.
vs.w: Let’s not be weary in doing good, for we will reap in due season, if we don’t give up.

vs.t: Therefore, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, unmoveable, always abounding in the work of the Lord, forasmuch as ye know that your labour is not in vain in the Lord.
vs.e: For this cause, my dear brothers, be strong in purpose and unmoved, ever giving yourselves to the work of the Lord, because you are certain that your work is not without effect in the Lord.
vs.w: Therefore, my beloved brothers, be steadfast, immovable, always abounding in the Lord’s work, because you know that your labor is not in vain in the Lord.

vs.t: I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith:
vs.e: I have made a good fight, I have come to the end of my journey, I have kept the faith:
vs.w: I have fought the good fight. I have finished the course. I have kept the faith.

vs.t: Henceforth there is laid up for me a crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, shall give me at that day: and not to me only, but unto all them also that love his appearing.
vs.e: From now on, the crown of righteousness is made ready for me, which the Lord, the upright judge, Will give to me at that day: and not only to me, but to all those who have had love for his revelation.
vs.w: From now on, the crown of righteousness is stored up for me, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give to me on that day; and not to me only, but also to all those who have loved his appearing.

vs.t: Wherefore seeing we also are compassed about with so great a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which doth so easily beset us, and let us run with patience the race that is set before us,
vs.e: For this reason, as we are circled by so great a cloud of witnesses, putting off every weight, and the sin into which we come so readily, let us keep on running in the way which is marked out for us,
vs.w: Therefore let’s also, seeing we are surrounded by so great a cloud of witnesses, lay aside every weight and the sin which so easily entangles us, and let’s run with perseverance the race that is set before us,

vs.t: Looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith; who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising the shame, and is set down at the right hand of the throne of God.
vs.e: Having our eyes fixed on Jesus, the guide and end of our faith, who went through the pains of the cross, not caring for the shame, because of the joy which was before him, and who has now taken his place at the right hand of God's seat of power.
vs.w: looking to Jesus, the author and perfecter of faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured the cross, despising its shame, and has sat down at the right hand of the throne of God.
